# Sempera API: Full Documentation

> Build, test and run AI phone agents for businesses with one API.

This file is the complete Sempera developer documentation, concatenated for LLM ingestion. Each section below corresponds to one guide and is preceded by its canonical URL. The companion file [llms.txt](https://sempera.org/llms.txt) is a shorter index. The OpenAPI specification at https://api.sempera.org/openapi.json is the canonical definition of every endpoint, request body, response shape and webhook event.

Availability follows the [AI context](https://sempera.org/ai-context.md). A documented operation is not proof of activation for every workspace. General outbound calling, text messaging, live transfers, booking, ordering and payments are not enabled for the initial business release.

**Pages included:** 45


---

# Sempera API
URL: https://docs.sempera.org/

The Sempera API is a REST API at `https://api.sempera.org/v1` for building, testing and running AI phone agents for businesses: agents that answer a business's calls from its own facts, take messages and requests, and hand the complex parts to staff.

> **New to Sempera?** Start with [Getting started](https://api.sempera.org/docs/getting-started.md) to go from an API key to a published agent taking a real conversation, or read the [OpenAPI specification](https://api.sempera.org/openapi.json) for every endpoint.

Building with an AI agent?

Feed these docs straight to your LLM or coding agent: [`llms-full.txt`](https://sempera.org/llms-full.txt) is the complete documentation in one file, and [`llms.txt`](https://sempera.org/llms.txt) is a concise index. Coding agents can also connect over [MCP](https://api.sempera.org/docs/mcp.md).

## Prerequisites

To use the Sempera API, you'll need:

- A **Sempera account**: sign up free at https://app.sempera.org/sign-up
- An **API key** created by the workspace owner in Settings > API keys (starts with `sempera_sk_`, shown once)
- An endpoint URL for receiving **webhooks** (optional but recommended)

## What you can build

- **AI receptionist**: answer every call, take messages and requests, and pass the details to staff
- **Customer service line**: answer common questions from the business's own facts and hand off the rest
- **Outbound follow-ups**: reminders, confirmations and call-backs placed by an agent
- **Lead qualification**: ask the right questions and send qualified leads to the team
- **IVR replacement**: replace press-1 menus with a conversation
- **Agents that build agents**: let a coding assistant create, test and publish agents over the API or MCP

## Key capabilities

| Feature                     | Description                                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Agents with versions**    | Edit a draft, preview it, publish an immutable version, roll back any time                  |
| **Phone and browser voice** | Bind a phone number to an agent, or open a browser voice session with a short-lived token   |
| **Knowledge**               | Upload documents the agent answers from                                                     |
| **Tools and integrations**  | Let agents call your systems and connected apps during a conversation                       |
| **Text messages**           | Two-way text threads from the agent's numbers                                               |
| **Tests and evals**         | Run scripted tests before publishing and judge finished conversations against your criteria |
| **Conversations**           | Every call and session with transcript, tool timeline and outcome                           |
| **Live calls**              | See calls in progress and their transcripts as they happen                                  |
| **Recordings**              | Short-lived, signed download links for recorded calls                                       |
| **Webhooks**                | Signed events for completed calls, outcomes, publishes and tests                            |
| **MCP server**              | Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and other MCP clients to a workspace                         |
| **SDKs**                    | Official TypeScript (`npm i @sempera/sdk`) and Python (`pip install sempera`) clients       |
| **Request tracing**         | An `x-request-id` on every response for support and debugging                               |

## Authentication

All requests require a bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_...
```

Keys belong to one workspace and carry explicit scopes. For scopes, roles, MCP connections and OAuth, see [Authentication](https://api.sempera.org/docs/authentication.md) and [auth.md](https://sempera.org/auth.md).

## Quick example

Check your key, then create and publish an agent:

```bash
curl https://api.sempera.org/v1/me \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..."

curl -X POST https://api.sempera.org/v1/agents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: create-northwind-1" \
  -d '{"name": "Northwind Barbers"}'
```

## The developer journey

| Step                | Call                                            | What it does                                                   |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Get a key        | Settings > API keys, or `POST /v1/api-keys`     | Owner creates a workspace key                                  |
| 2. Create an agent  | `POST /v1/agents`                               | Returns the agent and its stable `id`                          |
| 3. Configure        | `PATCH /v1/agents/{id}/draft`                   | Instructions, voice and other draft fields                     |
| 4. Attach tools     | `POST /v1/tools`                                | Create once, reference from the draft                          |
| 5. Attach knowledge | `POST /v1/knowledge-sources?agent_id=...`       | Upload documents (multipart)                                   |
| 6. Preview          | `POST /v1/agents/{id}/preview`                  | One typed turn against the draft                               |
| 7. Test             | `POST /v1/tests`                                | Scripted test battery; poll `GET /v1/tests/{test_id}`          |
| 8. Publish          | `POST /v1/agents/{id}/publish`                  | New immutable version; production uses only published versions |
| 9. Go live          | `POST /v1/sessions` or `POST /v1/phone-numbers` | Browser voice session, or bind a number                        |
| 10. Inspect         | `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`                         | Transcript, tool timeline and outcome                          |
| 11. Evaluate        | `POST /v1/evals/run`                            | Judge conversations against criteria                           |
| 12. Iterate         | `POST /v1/agents/{id}/rollback`                 | Edit, publish again, or roll back                              |

## SDKs and tools

| Tool           | Install                                | Use it for                                      |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript SDK | `npm i @sempera/sdk`                   | Typed client for Node 22.18 or newer            |
| Python SDK     | `pip install sempera`                  | Client for Python 3.9 or newer, no dependencies |
| MCP server     | `https://api.sempera.org/v1/mcp`       | Coding agents and assistants                    |
| OpenAPI        | `https://api.sempera.org/openapi.json` | Generate your own client                        |

## Error responses

Every error has the same envelope with a stable `code`. Plan and phone limits have their own codes; see [Errors and limits](https://api.sempera.org/docs/errors-and-limits.md) for the complete list, pagination, idempotency and rate limits.

| Status | Code                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401`  | `authentication_required` | No credential                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `401`  | `invalid_credential`      | A key that is unknown, expired or revoked                                                                                                                                                         |
| `403`  | `insufficient_scope`      | The key lacks the route's scope                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `403`  | `forbidden`               | The role cannot do this                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `403`  | `workspace_suspended`     | The workspace is paused, so its agents take no new actions. Reads and exports still work                                                                                                          |
| `403`  | `csrf_failed`             | An App-session write without its CSRF proof                                                                                                                                                       |
| `400`  | `validation_failed`       | A field is missing or wrong (`field` names it)                                                                                                                                                    |
| `402`  | `credits_exhausted`       | Not enough credits for this building action, so nothing started. Carries `needed`, `balance`, `debt` and, where buying can work, `buy_path`. Live agents are not affected (billing-boundaries.md) |
| `404`  | `not_found`               | No such resource in your scope                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `405`  | `method_not_allowed`      | This route does not support the HTTP method; `Allow` lists supported methods                                                                                                                      |
| `409`  | `conflict`                | A rule refused it (a stale draft, a live version, a taken number); `reason` may carry a finer code                                                                                                |
| `409`  | `idempotency_key_reused`  | Same key, different request                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `410`  | `gone`                    | It existed and is no longer served (a deleted recording, or one whose access ended); `reason` says which                                                                                          |
| `413`  | `payload_too_large`       | The request body exceeds the route's size limit                                                                                                                                                   |
| `429`  | `rate_limited`            | A request or feature budget is exhausted; use `Retry-After` or the error's `retry_after_s` when present                                                                                           |
| `501`  | `capability_unavailable`  | Not offered on this platform. `POST /v1/calls` also answers it with `reason: do_not_contact` when the number is on the workspace's do-not-contact list (sessions-and-calls.md)                    |
| `502`  | `provider_failed`         | A provider behind the API failed                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `504`  | `provider_timeout`        | A service Sempera called did not answer in time                                                                                                                                                   |
| `503`  | `owner_setup_required`    | A feature the workspace owner has not configured yet                                                                                                                                              |
| `503`  | `credits_unavailable`     | The credit balance could not be read, so nothing started. Live agents are not affected                                                                                                            |
| `503`  | `service_unavailable`     | A required service or stored record cannot be read right now; check the operation's state before retrying a write                                                                                 |
| `500`  | `internal_error`          | Quote the `request_id` to support                                                                                                                                                                 |

## MCP tools

The table below lists 41 read tools for `https://api.sempera.org/v1/mcp`. Each maps to an API route and needs the same scope. Use `tools/list` for the tools your credential can use. See [MCP for coding agents](https://api.sempera.org/docs/mcp.md).

| Tool                       | Route                                                | Scope                | Changes anything? |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------- |
| `list_agents`              | `GET /v1/agents`                                     | `agents:read`        | No                |
| `get_agent`                | `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}`                          | `agents:read`        | No                |
| `mcp_client_setup`         | `GET /v1/mcp/clients/{client}`                       | `agents:read`        | No                |
| `get_agent_draft`          | `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/draft`                    | `agents:read`        | No                |
| `list_agent_versions`      | `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/versions`                 | `agents:read`        | No                |
| `get_agent_version`        | `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/versions/{version_id}`    | `agents:read`        | No                |
| `get_latest_agent_version` | `GET /v2/agents/{uuid}/versions/latest`              | `deploy:read`        | No                |
| `list_agent_environments`  | `GET /v2/agents/{uuid}/environments`                 | `deploy:read`        | No                |
| `list_agent_variables`     | `GET /v2/agents/{uuid}/environments/{env}/variables` | `deploy:read`        | No                |
| `list_agent_branches`      | `GET /v2/agents/{uuid}/branches`                     | `agents:read`        | No                |
| `list_agent_deployments`   | `GET /v2/agents/{uuid}/deployments`                  | `deploy:read`        | No                |
| `list_agent_check_runs`    | `GET /v2/agents/{uuid}/check-runs`                   | `evals:read`         | No                |
| `list_calls`               | `GET /v1/calls`                                      | `calls:read`         | No                |
| `list_post_call_events`    | `GET /v1/post-call-events`                           | `calls:read`         | No                |
| `get_analytics_overview`   | `GET /v2/analytics/overview`                         | `calls:read`         | No                |
| `get_call_log`             | `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}`                            | `calls:read`         | No                |
| `list_sessions`            | `GET /v1/sessions`                                   | `sessions:read`      | No                |
| `get_session`              | `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}`                      | `sessions:read`      | No                |
| `list_knowledge_sources`   | `GET /v1/knowledge-sources`                          | `knowledge:read`     | No                |
| `get_knowledge_source`     | `GET /v1/knowledge-sources/{source_id}`              | `knowledge:read`     | No                |
| `list_tools`               | `GET /v1/tools`                                      | `tools:read`         | No                |
| `get_tool`                 | `GET /v1/tools/{tool_id}`                            | `tools:read`         | No                |
| `list_integrations`        | `GET /v1/integrations`                               | `integrations:read`  | No                |
| `list_webhooks`            | `GET /v1/webhooks`                                   | `webhooks:read`      | No                |
| `get_webhook`              | `GET /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}`                      | `webhooks:read`      | No                |
| `list_webhook_deliveries`  | `GET /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries`           | `webhooks:read`      | No                |
| `list_tests`               | `GET /v1/tests`                                      | `tests:read`         | No                |
| `get_test_run`             | `GET /v1/tests/{test_id}`                            | `tests:read`         | No                |
| `list_eval_agents`         | `GET /v1/evals/agents`                               | `evals:read`         | No                |
| `get_eval_agent`           | `GET /v1/evals/{eval_id}`                            | `evals:read`         | No                |
| `get_eval_results`         | `GET /v1/evals/results`                              | `evals:read`         | No                |

| `get_docs_page`            | `GET /docs/{page}`                                   | none                 | No                |

# Getting started
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/getting-started.md

Base URL: `https://api.sempera.org/v1`. Server-to-server requests use HTTPS with an API key in the `Authorization` header. Most bodies are JSON; document uploads use multipart form data.

## Before you start

- **You need a workspace and an API key.** Sign in to the Sempera App at `https://app.sempera.org`. Registration availability is shown there. The workspace owner creates API keys under Settings, API keys, or with `POST /v1/api-keys` (authentication.md). If registration is unavailable and you do not have a workspace, write to [hello@sempera.org](mailto:hello@sempera.org) to ask for access.
- **There is one API hostname and no separate test host.** Everything below runs against `https://api.sempera.org`. Experiment in a workspace you can afford to change, and use `Idempotency-Key` on writes you may retry (errors-and-limits.md).
- **A key is a secret.** Keep it on your server, never in a browser or a repository (security-and-privacy.md).
- **Examples here are synthetic.** They use a demonstration agent, `northwind-barbers`. Substitute your own agent's id.

## The developer journey

1. **Get an API key.** The workspace owner creates one in the App (Settings, API keys, New API key) or with `POST /v1/api-keys`. The secret starts with `sempera_sk_` and is shown once.
2. **Create an Agent.** `POST /v1/agents` with `{"name": "Northwind Barbers"}`. The response is the Agent, including its stable `id`.
3. **Configure instructions and voice.** `PATCH /v1/agents/{id}/draft` with `{"fields": {...}}`. Read `GET /v1/agents/{id}/draft` first: `editable_fields` lists the keys a PATCH may carry, and `GET /v1/agents/{id}` shows their current values.
4. **Attach tools.** Create them once with `POST /v1/tools`, then reference their ids in the draft's attachment fields.
5. **Attach knowledge.** Upload documents with `POST /v1/knowledge-sources?agent_id=...` (multipart), then attach the collection in the draft.
6. **Preview.** `POST /v1/agents/{id}/preview` with `{"message": "Hi, can I book a haircut?"}` runs one typed turn against the draft.
7. **Run tests.** `POST /v1/tests` with `{"agent_id": "..."}` starts the scripted battery; poll `GET /v1/tests/{test_id}`.
8. **Publish.** `POST /v1/agents/{id}/publish` creates a new immutable version. Production only ever uses a published version.
9. **Open a conversation.** `POST /v1/sessions` with `{"agent_id": "...", "channel": "web_voice"}` returns a short-lived realtime token for a browser, or bind a number with `POST /v1/phone-numbers`.
10. **Inspect it.** `GET /v1/sessions?agent_id=...` lists every conversation; `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` has the transcript, tool timeline and outcome.
11. **Run evals.** Define criteria with `POST /v1/evals`, judge conversations with `POST /v1/evals/run`.
12. **Iterate.** Edit the draft, preview, publish again. Versions are never rewritten; roll back with `POST /v1/agents/{id}/rollback`.

## First request

```bash
curl https://api.sempera.org/v1/me \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..."
```

```js
// Node 18 or newer: fetch is built in
const res = await fetch("https://api.sempera.org/v1/me", {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SEMPERA_API_KEY}` },
});
console.log(res.headers.get("x-request-id"), await res.json());
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request(
    "https://api.sempera.org/v1/me",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SEMPERA_API_KEY']}"},
)
with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as res:
    print(res.headers["X-Request-Id"], json.load(res))
```

The answer says what the credential is: its kind, workspace, role, scopes and the agents it can see. Every response carries `X-Request-Id`; quote it when you write to support.

## Create and publish an agent

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.sempera.org/v1/agents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: create-northwind-1" \
  -d '{"name": "Northwind Barbers"}'

curl -X PATCH https://api.sempera.org/v1/agents/northwind-barbers/draft \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"fields": {"greeting": "Thanks for calling Northwind Barbers, this is Nova."}}'

curl -X POST https://api.sempera.org/v1/agents/northwind-barbers/publish \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: publish-northwind-1"
```

```js
const base = "https://api.sempera.org/v1";
const headers = {
  Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SEMPERA_API_KEY}`,
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
};

const agent = await fetch(`${base}/agents`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { ...headers, "Idempotency-Key": "create-northwind-1" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ name: "Northwind Barbers" }),
}).then((r) => r.json());

await fetch(`${base}/agents/${agent.id}/draft`, {
  method: "PATCH",
  headers,
  body: JSON.stringify({ fields: { greeting: "Thanks for calling Northwind Barbers, this is Nova." } }),
});

await fetch(`${base}/agents/${agent.id}/publish`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { ...headers, "Idempotency-Key": "publish-northwind-1" },
});
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

BASE = "https://api.sempera.org/v1"
KEY = os.environ["SEMPERA_API_KEY"]

def call(method, path, body=None, idempotency_key=None):
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if idempotency_key:
        headers["Idempotency-Key"] = idempotency_key
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as res:
        return json.load(res)

agent = call("POST", "/agents", {"name": "Northwind Barbers"}, "create-northwind-1")
call("PATCH", f"/agents/{agent['id']}/draft",
     {"fields": {"greeting": "Thanks for calling Northwind Barbers, this is Nova."}})
call("POST", f"/agents/{agent['id']}/publish", idempotency_key="publish-northwind-1")
```

## Connecting a coding agent (MCP)

`POST /v1/mcp` is a JSON-RPC 2.0 [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) endpoint for driving Sempera from an assistant or coding agent. Connect with a bearer key holding `agents:read` or a phone scope. `tools/list` returns the tools that credential's scopes allow, including reads, draft and test operations, explicit writes and phone tasks. Tool calls enforce the same role and workspace checks as REST. Read [MCP](https://api.sempera.org/docs/mcp.md) before enabling writes.

For connection guidance, `mcp_client_setup` needs `agents:read` and takes `{"client": "claude-code" | "claude-desktop" | "cursor" | "vs-code" | "windsurf" | "gemini-cli" | "codex" | "other"}`. It returns that client's URL, header and config snippet:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.sempera.org/v1/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"mcp_client_setup","arguments":{"client":"claude-code"}}}'
```

The same answer is a plain read at `GET /v1/mcp/clients/{client}` (same key, same scope), which is what the App's Settings > API keys page uses.

MCP is not read-only. Use a narrowly scoped credential and review a tool's arguments before calling it.

## What the API does not do yet

Plan for these before you design around the API:

- **Create a workspace.** A workspace is created in the App when a person signs up. No API route creates one, and the first API key is created in the App too (authentication.md).
- **Buy or search for a phone number.** `POST /v1/phone-numbers` points a number you supply at an agent.
- **Manage plans, payment methods or invoices.** Those live in the Sempera App (billing-boundaries.md).
- **Change recording, retention or deletion settings, or hand you call audio.** Those are workspace owner settings in the App, and an API key is never given audio (recordings.md).
- **Replace the App's owner features.** Call-data exports, outbound scheduling and tool analytics have no API route (app-features.md).
- **Use a browser-specific Sempera SDK.** The TypeScript and Python clients are server clients (sdks.md). For browser voice, mint a session on your server and use the realtime client protocol described in web-sdk.md.

## Where the rest is

The full contract is `https://api.sempera.org/openapi.json`. The guide pages are listed in `https://api.sempera.org/llms.txt`. Three pages answer the questions teams ask before they commit: [security and privacy](https://api.sempera.org/docs/security-and-privacy.md), [billing boundaries](https://api.sempera.org/docs/billing-boundaries.md) and [supported clients](https://api.sempera.org/docs/supported-clients.md).


---

# API overview
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/api-overview.md

## Hostnames

| Hostname          | What it is                                          |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `sempera.org`     | The company                                         |
| `app.sempera.org` | The Sempera App, the product a customer signs in to |
| `api.sempera.org` | The Sempera API, the one developer surface          |

There is exactly one API hostname. The App's own browser traffic goes to `app.sempera.org/api/*`, a same-origin routing layer for its session cookie; it is not a second API and nothing outside the App should call it.

## Versioning

The API major version is in the path: `/v1` for Sempera-native resources. It is not the Agent's version. An Agent's published configuration versions are `agent_version` resources under `/v1/agents/{id}/versions`.

The `/v2` paths that exist today are compatibility facades for observed console traffic. They are intentionally thin, keep the same credential and workspace boundary as `/v1`, and do not introduce a second source of truth. A future Sempera-native `/v2` would ship with a deprecation notice, a migration guide and a sunset date for `/v1`, published in the changelog. Nothing is removed from `/v1` silently.

## Routes that need no credential

These routes can be reached without an API credential, at the anonymous limit of 60 requests a minute per address (errors-and-limits.md). They expose no workspace data to an anonymous caller. OAuth registration, authorization and token exchange still require their protocol inputs and owner consent where applicable.

| Route                                                     | What it answers                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /` and `GET /v1`                                     | The API's front door, the same small JSON index at both: its name, version, `status` (`ok`), `documentation` (the docs site) and links to the contract and the guide pages.     |
| `GET /v1/health`                                          | Liveness: `ok`, the API version, the build and the environment, plus `status` (`ready`, `not_ready` or `unknown`) for whether the database has every update this release needs. |
| `GET /openapi.json`                                       | The OpenAPI 3.1 contract, generated from the running route table.                                                                                                               |
| `GET /llms.txt`                                           | The map of these pages for coding agents.                                                                                                                                       |
| `GET /robots.txt`                                         | The search policy of the API host.                                                                                                                                              |
| `GET /docs/{page}`                                        | A guide page as Markdown. The `.md` suffix is optional.                                                                                                                         |
| `GET /v2/models`                                          | The speech models Sempera publishes, as the model list many client libraries expect (sessions-and-calls.md).                                                                    |
| `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/.well-known/jwks.json` | A workspace's public signing keys, for a receiver that verifies a signed request (secrets-and-signing.md).                                                                      |
| `POST /v1/phone-onboarding/start`                         | Starts a Sempera Phone sign-up link an assistant shows its owner. It grants nothing (phone-plan.md).                                                                            |
| `POST /v1/phone-onboarding/poll`                          | Whether the owner approved that link. Only after the owner approves does it hand over one limited credential, once (phone-plan.md).                                             |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`             | Public authorization-server metadata (mcp.md).                                                                                                                                  |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`               | Public protected-resource metadata (mcp.md).                                                                                                                                    |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp`        | Public MCP resource metadata (mcp.md).                                                                                                                                          |
| `POST /v1/oauth/register`                                 | Registers an OAuth client; does not grant workspace access (mcp.md).                                                                                                            |
| `GET /v1/oauth/authorize`                                 | Starts the owner sign-in and consent flow, with PKCE and an exact registered redirect (mcp.md).                                                                                 |
| `POST /v1/oauth/token`                                    | Exchanges the protocol's code or refresh proof for its scoped token (mcp.md).                                                                                                   |

`GET /v1/me` needs a credential, but any class of credential may call it; without one it answers `401 authentication_required`. The routes that Sempera's service providers call are not in this table; the next section says why.

## Supported routes and compatibility routes

`openapi.json` groups every operation by tag. Two kinds are worth telling apart.

- **Supported routes** are everything outside the `Compatibility` tag. These pages name each one, the contract covers it, and it changes only under the deprecation policy in changelog.md.
- **Compatibility routes** carry the `Compatibility` tag. They are thin facades, at `/v1/compat/...`, under `/v2` and elsewhere, that answer in the shapes other consoles use so that a client built for those shapes keeps working. They use the same credential and the same workspace boundary as every other route and read the same records, so they add no second source of truth. These pages do not name each one: `openapi.json` is their contract.

Provider ingress, a few routes under `/v1/webhooks` that a telephony carrier or the payment provider calls, is a third group. It needs no Sempera credential because each route carries its provider's own proof. It is not part of the integration contract, these pages do not list its routes, and you never call it (webhooks.md).

## IDs

IDs are opaque strings. Agent ids are Sempera's own stable slugs (never a voice or telephony provider's identifier). Keys, workspaces, calls and webhook endpoints are UUIDs. Sessions carry the id the runtime recorded them under. Do not parse ids.

## JSON, timestamps, objects

Requests and responses are `application/json` (uploads are `multipart/form-data`). Timestamps are UTC ISO-8601. Most Sempera-native resources carry an `object` field naming their type, and most Sempera-native lists are `{"object": "list", "data": [...], "has_more": bool, "next_cursor": string|null}`. Compatibility facade endpoints keep their observed external envelopes instead; the OpenAPI `Compatibility` tag and the route-specific schemas are the source of truth for those shapes.

## Request ids and tracing

Every response carries `X-Request-Id`, minted by Sempera. A value you send in `X-Request-Id` is echoed back as `X-Client-Request-Id`. A W3C `traceparent` header is echoed back unchanged.

## Idempotency

Writes where a duplicate would be dangerous accept `Idempotency-Key`. See errors-and-limits.md.

## Tenancy

Every credential belongs to one workspace. Everything it can read or write is inside that workspace; an id from another workspace answers `not_found`, the same as an id that never existed.


---

# MCP for coding agents
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/mcp.md

`POST /v1/mcp` is a JSON-RPC 2.0 [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) endpoint. A coding agent or assistant can read its workspace and, with the matching permissions, create and edit agents, hold typed test conversations with a draft, see what publishing a draft would change, save versions, publish drafts with an explicit confirmation, run offline tests and simulations, manage text knowledge and bind owned phone numbers. Every tool runs the matching API handler as the caller. The write registry cannot place a call, send an SMS, buy a number or delete a resource. The separately scoped phone tools require the approvals described below. Write access does not bypass roles, workspace boundaries, quotas or release checks.

Use `tools/list` with the credential your client will use to discover the current tools and their input schemas. The result depends on the scopes and permissions of that connection. The tables below describe the tool families.

## Business plan handoff limits

MCP connections, OAuth grants and developer keys cannot open a business plan handoff or approve a purchase. An assistant can help evaluate a draft and point the owner to the App, but it must not ask for card details, confirm a payment, or treat a checkout return as proof of funding or activation. The signed-in workspace owner checks the review and any billing status in the App. Purchase consent is separate from permission to contact a business.

## Connect

Use the same bearer key as every other route (authentication.md), or sign in with OAuth (below). A key needs `agents:read` or a phone scope to connect. An OAuth token can connect with any approved scope. `tools/list` shows the tools that the credential can use. CI keys are refused with `403 forbidden`. The call below asks for the setup snippet of one client. The same answer is available at `GET /v1/mcp/clients/{client}`.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.sempera.org/v1/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"mcp_client_setup","arguments":{"client":"claude-code"}}}'
```

The endpoint takes one JSON message per POST and answers one JSON body. It offers no event stream and no session: with a live credential, any method but `POST` (`GET`, `HEAD` and `DELETE` among them) answers `405` with `Allow: POST`, and it sends no `Mcp-Session-Id`. That is the plain JSON form of the Streamable HTTP transport, which every published MCP revision lets a server choose and requires a client to accept, so ChatGPT and Claude need no event stream to connect. No tool here sends progress, so none is offered.

## Sign in with OAuth

A host that cannot hold a static key (ChatGPT, Claude) signs in with OAuth 2.1 instead. Give it the URL `https://api.sempera.org/v1/mcp`. Bearer keys keep working exactly as before.

1. The host posts without a token and gets `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://api.sempera.org/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp"`.
2. It reads that document, then `https://api.sempera.org/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.
3. It registers itself at `POST /v1/oauth/register` (RFC 7591) and sends the browser to `GET /v1/oauth/authorize` with PKCE (`S256`, required), the `resource` `https://api.sempera.org/v1/mcp`, and the scopes it wants. Redirects match exactly. A loopback address may differ by port alone, because a native client binds a free port each time.
4. The person signs in on `app.sempera.org` if they have not, and a workspace owner approves on the consent page: which client, which workspace, which scopes, and where the answer goes. A client Sempera cannot recognise by its published redirect is shown as unverified. The owner can approve fewer scopes than were asked for, never more.
5. The host swaps the code at `POST /v1/oauth/token`. An access token lasts one hour and a refresh token 30 days. Each refresh turns the refresh token over. Presenting a spent one ends every token from that sign-in, and so does presenting a spent code.

| Scope           | What it allows                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `phone:read`    | See the line, plan state and allowance, and read call tasks/results                                                                                                                                   |
| `phone:call`    | Preview calls, start approved calls and cancel tasks                                                                                                                                                  |
| `phone:text`    | Preview texts, send approved texts and read their threads                                                                                                                                             |
| `phone:approve` | Lets the signed-in owner approve a previewed call or text from its card in the chat. Off on the consent screen until the owner turns it on, and off on Sempera's side until enabled for that chat app |

Owners can also approve management permissions for reading workspace data, creating and editing agent drafts, publishing, rolling back, and attaching existing numbers. The consent screen shows the permissions the client requests and lets the owner narrow them. `create_agent` creates an unpublished draft. An OAuth connection needs both edit and publish consent to run `save_agent_version`, because the build becomes the current version. Call transcripts and recording links require a separate opt-in that starts off. When the token also holds the relevant read scope, `get_call_log` and `get_session` include available transcript excerpts and a link to available playback in the signed-in App. Lists remain metadata-only.

In-chat approval (`phone:approve`) is the one way an OAuth client can carry an owner's approval, and it is built for the card, not the assistant. The preview card receives a single-use code in the tool result's `_meta`, never in `content` or `structuredContent`, bound to that request, the consenting owner, that connection and an expiry of at most ten minutes. The card sends it to `phone_approve_request`, a tool marked for the card alone (`_meta.ui.visibility: ["app"]`). Sempera then repeats every check a start makes, allows one approval per request and a daily number of in-chat approvals, records the approval in the workspace's activity record and emails the owner. The card always keeps the **Approve in the Sempera app** link. What Sempera cannot check: a card and the assistant call with the same token, so keeping that tool and that code away from the model is the chat app's job. In-chat approval is turned on only for a chat app where that has been confirmed.

OAuth grants exclude purchases, billing changes, member and API-key management, paid tests and knowledge-source writes. A request with an unsupported scope is refused with `invalid_scope`. A client that requests no scopes gets `phone:read`.

A token works on `POST /v1/mcp` and nowhere else (any other route answers `401`), and only for the resource it was issued to. It resolves to the same principal a key does, so the same role, scope, workspace and audit checks apply. Only `SHA-256` hashes of tokens, codes and client secrets are stored.

Client Metadata Documents are not offered. A host that prefers them falls back to registration, which ChatGPT, Claude and Codex all document. Tools do not yet ask for more scope mid-conversation: to change what a client holds, approve it again, which replaces its grant.

Owners see every client in Settings, Connected clients (`GET /v1/client-grants`), with its scopes and last use, and end one with `DELETE /v1/client-grants/{grant_id}`. Its tokens stop at once and every other client keeps working.

Public discovery is served by `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp`. These publish authorization-server and resource metadata, without granting access or replacing owner consent.

## Protocol versions

Two revisions are spoken. Which rules a request is held to depends on one thing: whether it carries the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header.

| A request that...                                                                | What it gets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| carries `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18` or `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2024-11-05` | The Streamable HTTP rules for a server with no stream and no sessions. A notification, or a client's answer to a request, is accepted with `202` and no body. A body without `jsonrpc: "2.0"`, a request without an `id`, or a JSON array is refused with `400`. The two headers are served identically; what `initialize` answers depends only on the revision named in its own parameters. |
| carries `MCP-Protocol-Version` naming any other revision, empty or not           | `400 validation_failed`, with the revisions spoken listed in `supported`. Before the endpoint negotiated, the header was ignored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| carries no `MCP-Protocol-Version` header                                         | Served as this endpoint always served it: a notification gets `200` and an empty result, and a JSON array is a `400`. Only four of its answers change; they are listed under Which clients move.                                                                                                                                                                                             |

`initialize` answers the revision the client asked for when it is `2025-06-18` or `2024-11-05`. For a newer date (`2025-11-25`, `2026-07-28` and later) it answers `2025-06-18`, the newest spoken; for `2025-03-26`, an older date, an unknown value or none it answers `2024-11-05`, which is all it answered before it negotiated. Prompts, completions, logging, event streams and sessions are not offered; nothing here claims them. Resources are offered only as the in-chat screens described under Screens, and `structuredContent` only on the two tools those screens belong to, without an `outputSchema`.

Neither supported revision includes an `instructions` field in `initialize`. The editing and testing contracts are documented under Draft and test over MCP and Test an agent from your assistant.

With either supported version header, an `id` must be a string or a finite integral number. Numeric spellings such as `1`, `1.0` and `1e0` are accepted and the parsed value is echoed without conversion. Null, booleans, objects, arrays, fractional numbers and non-finite values are refused before a tool is called, with HTTP `400`, JSON-RPC `-32600` and a null response id. Notifications still omit the id and receive `202` with no body; valid client replies receive the same empty acknowledgement. Requests without the version header retain their legacy behavior.

### Which clients move

* **A client that sends the header.** The revisions from `2025-06-18` on require a client to send `MCP-Protocol-Version` on every request after `initialize`, so a client built on a current SDK sends it. Such a client now negotiates `2025-06-18` (it asks for a newer revision and is answered with the newest spoken), then gets `202` for its `notifications/initialized`, and may try to open a stream with a `GET` on the endpoint and be answered `405`, which that revision allows for a server that offers none. This is a change from the endpoint before this release, which answered such a client `2024-11-05` and `200`. A client that sends a header naming any other revision is refused with `400`.
* **A client that sends no header on any request.** Four of the answers it already got change: `initialize` asking for `2025-06-18` or newer is answered `2025-06-18` (it was `2024-11-05`); `tools/list` with a `cursor` is a `-32602` error (it was ignored, and the list never paged); each of the three original tools gains `title`, `annotations` and `_meta` in `tools/list`; and `initialize` declares `resources`, so `resources/list` answers the screens of the tools it can call (it was `-32601`). Its `tools/list` also includes the read tools its scopes allow. Every other answer to it is unchanged, including the text of the original tools' results and their `-32000` errors; a result now also carries `usage` beside `content` (see Usage on every result).
* **A browser page on another site.** See the `Origin` rule below. The API answers a browser's preflight for this endpoint with `401` and no CORS headers, so such a page could not send it a JSON request with a key in the first place; the `Origin` rule is a second lock.

## Origin

Every request that carries an `Origin` header is checked, with or without `MCP-Protocol-Version` (the only method served is `POST`; any other is refused `405`, or `401` with no live credential, before it gets that far). The `Origin` value must be this deployment's own host, a host the deployment is configured to allow, or an origin the App is served from (the origins the deployment lists for its web App); otherwise the answer is `403 forbidden`, and the request's scope, version header and body are never looked at. The App's own pages therefore reach this endpoint through the App's proxy even when that proxy runs on another host or port than the API, as it does in development and in the browser tests.

The API's front door looks at the credential first: a request with no key, an unknown key or a revoked key is refused `401` whatever its `Origin`, as is a dead token, and that `401` says where to sign in, so the `403` is what a request with a live key and a foreign `Origin` gets. A request with no `Origin` header (a command-line tool, an SDK, a server-side client) is not a browser's and is not checked. `Origin: null`, an empty `Origin` and a value that is not a URL are foreign, and so is a request with several `Origin` headers when any one of them is. The deployment's own host means the host and port the request arrived with, so that half relies on the deployment's host policy (which answers `404` to a host it does not know) and does not compare the scheme; an App origin is compared whole, scheme, host and port. This rule is new with the release that added these tools: a client that sent an `Origin` of another site and was served before is refused now.

## Tools

Every tool projects an existing route, run as the caller: the route's own scope, role, workspace and ownership checks apply. The table below lists 41 read tools; the other tool families, including writes and follow-up reads, are below. An id from another workspace is refused. The `list_agents` tool keeps its original shape; a list that its route pages is paged here the same way.

| Tool                       | Reads                                                | Scope                | Arguments                                   | Changes anything? |

| `list_voices`              | `GET /v1/voices`                                     | `agents:read`        | none                                        | No                |

| `get_docs_index`           | `GET /llms.txt`                                      | none                 | none                                        | No                |
| `get_credential`           | `GET /v1/me`                                         | none                 | none                                        | No                |
| `list_members`             | `GET /v1/compat/app/orgs/{uuid}/members`             | `organizations:read` | workspace_id (required)                     | No                |
| `get_credits`              | `GET /v1/credits`                                    | `organizations:read` | none                                        | No                |
| `list_models`              | `GET /v1/models`                                     | `models:read`        | none                                        | No                |
| `list_phone_numbers`       | `GET /v1/phone-numbers`                              | `phone_numbers:read` | agent_id (required), limit, cursor          | No                |
| `list_alerts`              | `GET /v1/alerts`                                     | `agents:read`        | agent_id, limit, page, sort, direction      | No                |
| `get_call_transcript`      | `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}`                            | `calls:read`         | call_id (required), agent_id                | No                |

`get_call_transcript` also needs a transcript permission that no API key or OAuth grant can hold yet: until an owner can grant it, the tool is not listed and a call is refused `insufficient_scope`. `get_credential` reads the credential itself, so every credential can call it, including an OAuth phone grant. Its `connection` says what signed the connection in: `oauth_grant` (with the client id, the label the owner approved and whether a verified redirect named it), `mcp_key`, `rest_credential` or `api_key`. An OAuth grant is stored as a developer-class key, so `kind` and `key_kind` alone do not tell it apart; its scopes and role are the grant's own. When no speech model is published for customers yet, `list_models` answers an empty `models` list with a `note` saying so. `list_members` takes the workspace id `get_credential` returns. With `days` set to 7, 14, 30 or 90, `get_analytics_overview` returns a phone-only breakdown. With `start` or `end`, it returns totals for the requested range and the preceding range of equal length. With no arguments those ranges cover the latest 30 days and the 30 days before them. The range totals report `total_cost` as `null`. A request can use either `days` or date bounds.

The read tools in this registry return JSON objects as `structuredContent` beside JSON text. Tools with screens may return a display projection in `structuredContent`. The two guide tools answer text only.

Every tool in `tools/list` carries a human title and all four MCP hints: `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint` and `openWorldHint`. The Changes anything? columns are the inverse of `readOnlyHint`; a test compares every row with the actual tool list, including the blueprint tool. Hints describe effects, not permission or directory approval. A state change alone is not destructive, and idempotency assumes identical arguments, including any required `idempotency_key` or approval id.

The read tools above carry `readOnlyHint` true, `destructiveHint` false, `idempotentHint` true and `openWorldHint` false. Sempera also gives explicit metadata under `_meta`: `org.sempera/effect` (`read`), `org.sempera/side-effects` (`false`), `org.sempera/scope`, `org.sempera/route`, `org.sempera/operation-id` and `org.sempera/paginated`. A host should treat hints as claims by the server. The read registry enforces `GET` routes only; these tools neither submit a paid task nor send arguments to an outside recipient. A read may still perform internal health checks or update a cache.

The blueprint tool, which has an in-chat screen (see Screens), uses the same read hints and scope:

| Tool                  | Scope         | Changes anything? |
| --------------------- | ------------- | ----------------- |
| `get_agent_blueprint` | `agents:read` | No                |

## Arguments, answers and errors

* An agent is named `agent_id` in every tool, whichever path variable the route calls it. Ids are letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:` and `-`, up to 200 characters. An unknown argument, a missing required one, a wrong type or an out-of-range number is refused before anything is read, with the argument named.
* An answer is the route's JSON as text in one `text` content item (narrowed as a later section says for seventeen tools), or, for the two guide tools, its Markdown. A failure is a tool result with `isError: true` whose text is the route's own error envelope, for example `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"no such agent","request_id":"req_..."}}`. The codes are those in errors-and-limits.md, and `request_id` is the one the call returned in `X-Request-Id`. An answer about your workspace never carries an internal address, the name of a setting, a file path, a stack trace or the name of an engine or supplier behind Sempera; the tests scan every tool's answer for them.
* Arguments that are not a JSON object, an unknown method and an unknown cursor on `tools/list` are protocol errors (`-32602`, `-32601`). The three original tools keep reporting a refusal as JSON-RPC error `-32000`, as they always did; every newer tool reports it as a tool result.
* Lists page with `limit` (1 to 200, default 50; `list_agent_check_runs` takes 1 to 100) and `cursor`. Pass `next_cursor` from the last page back unchanged to read the next one (`nextCursor` on `list_tools`, `data.next_cursor` on `list_eval_agents`). A cursor is an opaque position: the same cursor gives the same page while the rows are unchanged, and one issued to another key reads only that key's own rows. `list_integrations`, `list_voices` and the environment, branch and deployment reads answer in one piece.
* An answer larger than 1 MiB is refused with `payload_too_large`; ask for a smaller page or a more specific id. A read that runs longer than 30 seconds is refused with `service_unavailable`. A call counts once against the key's request budget (errors-and-limits.md), like any other request.
* A secret environment variable always reads `null` in `list_agent_variables`; its value never leaves the server.

### What seventeen tools leave out

Seventeen tools answer a short, written-out list of fields rather than the route's whole answer. A field the route gains later is not passed on until this page and the tool both name it.

* **Calls and conversation records** (`list_calls`, `get_call_log`, `list_sessions`, `get_session`) include the id, agent, channel, status, start and end times, duration, language, outcome code and label, version and turn count. There is no transcript or recording link without the separate OAuth content consent, and lists always return metadata only. Caller numbers, summaries, titles, extracted values and provider logs are omitted. Outcome, language and version are shown only when they have the shape of a short code (letters, digits and `.` `_` `:` `-`, with no spaces). Otherwise they read `null`. An outcome label is shown only when it is a Sempera outcome label or the plain wording of its code. No tool argument changes the consent required for content. `get_call_transcript` uses its own transcript permission.
* **`list_post_call_events`** returns each ended phone call as a `call.completed` event: the event id, `created_at` (when the call's record was stored), and in `data` the call id, agent, start time, duration, outcome code and `recording_stored`. The outcome reads `null` unless it has the shape of a short code. No caller number, summary, recording link or transcript.
* **`get_eval_results`** returns counts, pass rates, the weekly and per-version trend, and one row per scored conversation with its verdict and score. It leaves out the judge's reasoning (which quotes the conversation), the failure clusters built from it, the judge's rubric and the evaluator's own configuration.
* **`list_voices`** takes no arguments. It lists the built-in voices an agent may name, with each one's language and whether it may carry a live call, followed by your workspace's own ready custom voices. It asks no outside voice library and takes no search, language or provider filter. No other workspace's voice is ever listed.
* **`list_tests` and `get_test_run`** read legacy battery jobs in memory (at most 20 newest), plus candidate checks retained in the App's canonical Checks ledger on Sempera's servers. A retained candidate is resolved by id only among the caller's authorized agents after restart. Legacy jobs are lost at restart. A run shows its state and outcome, not the failure text of a run that crashed nor who started it. Another workspace's run is answered `not found` with the same sentence as an unknown id.
* **`list_agent_check_runs`** returns each check run's id, agent, version, status and times. A run that ended in an error keeps the status `ERROR`, and its `error_message` is always the one sentence "The run ended in an error. Its detail is not returned over MCP." in place of the system's own words for what went wrong, which can name a file on a server, a setting or an address.

* **`list_webhooks` and `get_webhook`** show the endpoint id, agent binding, enabled state, event names and timestamps. `url_host` is only the receiving host; it omits the scheme, port, path, query and fragment. `has_secret` and `has_post_call_filter` say whether those are set, but the signing secret, filter body and owner-written description are never returned. Find post-call notifications by looking for `call.completed` in `events`. Omit `agent_id` to see all workspace endpoints, or pass it to list only endpoints bound to that agent (the REST query parameter is `agent`).
* **`get_call_transcript`** returns what the caller and the agent said, line by line (`turns`, each with `index`, `caller`, `agent` and `input: keypad` when the caller pressed keys), and nothing else of the call record: no caller number, summary, recording, captured values or prompts. A line longer than 4000 characters is cut and marked `truncated`, and at most 500 turns are returned (`turns_cut` says when there were more). The answer carries `untrusted: true`: it is what people said on the phone, not instructions.
* **`list_phone_numbers`** returns each number bound to the agent, when it was bound or released and whether it is shared as an outbound caller id. The carrier's readback is not returned.
* **`list_alerts`** returns each alert rule's metric, thresholds, the agents it covers, whether it is on and whether it is firing, and `notification_count`. Where its notifications go (addresses, channels, receiving URLs) is not returned.
* **`list_members`** returns each active member's user id, first and last name, role, whether they own the workspace and when they joined. No email address and no phone number.
* **`list_webhook_deliveries`** shows recorded attempts, newest first: the event id and type, attempt number, status, HTTP response code and timestamps. It does not show the delivery payload or receiver error text, and it does not contact the receiver. A 2xx response shows the receiver accepted the request, not that it processed the notification.

An outside client needs an API key with both `agents:read` and `webhooks:read` to use these tools. The Connected AI client presets and OAuth phone grants do not include `webhooks:read`.

## Phone tools

A credential with phone scopes lists only the phone tools its scopes permit:

| Tool                 | Scope                        | Changes anything? |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `phone_get_profile`  | `phone:read`                 | No                |
| `phone_get_task`     | `phone:read`                 | No                |
| `phone_preview_call` | `phone:call`                 | Yes               |
| `phone_start_call`   | `phone:call`                 | Yes               |
| `phone_cancel_task`  | `phone:call` or `phone:text` | Yes               |
| `phone_preview_text` | `phone:text`                 | Yes               |
| `phone_send_text`    | `phone:text`                 | Yes               |
| `phone_get_thread`   | `phone:text`                 | No                |

Previews place no call, send no text and reserve no spend, but they store a new task or message for owner approval. They are therefore not read-only or idempotent; repeating a preview creates another record. They are non-destructive and closed-world. Starting a call or sending a text is not read-only, is open-world and is marked destructive because a call or delivered message cannot be taken back. Cancelling is destructive and open-world because it can end a live call without a way to resume it. It does not delete the task record. Start, send and cancel are idempotent for the same approval or task id. Phone reads have no call, message or approval side effects; they record credential usage.

They run the same operations as the [phone REST routes](https://api.sempera.org/docs/phone-plan.md#a-call) and refuse with the same codes. An ordinary workspace API key cannot use them: connect the client with OAuth, a phone-enabled MCP key or a scoped REST credential. OAuth tokens and MCP keys work on MCP only; a scoped REST credential also works on the phone REST routes.

In Settings > Connected clients > **Connected AI clients**, choose **Read**, turn on **Phone tools (owner approval required)** and create a new connection. This adds all three phone scopes to the read scopes; it does not upgrade an old key or create a phone-only credential. For OAuth, the host must request `phone:read` and `phone:call` for the call journey; approve `phone:text` only if needed.

A preview returns `approval.url` for the signed-in owner unless standing approval covers it. Unless the preview returned `standing: true`, read the task until `approved` is true. Then start the unchanged request with the preview's `id` and `spend_bound_cents`. `reserved` means queued, not dialing. Poll the task for its recorded outcome; a finished call does not reopen the assistant chat. No tool approves, buys, subscribes or tops up. Follow [Your first call](https://api.sempera.org/docs/phone-plan.md#your-first-call) for setup, limits and refusal help.

## Operator tools

Three tools act on what is already running. Each runs existing routes as the caller, with the route's own scope, role, workspace and agent checks, and is listed only to a credential that holds its scope.

| Tool                 | Runs                                                                | Scope            | Arguments                                                                                            | Changes anything? |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `get_call_recording` | `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}`, then `GET /v1/recordings/{recording_id}` | `calls:read`     | call_id (required), agent_id                                                                         | No                |
| `rollback_agent`     | `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/rollback` (owner role)                  | `agents:publish` | agent_id, to_deployment_id, version_number, confirm (the agent_id again), idempotency_key (required) | Yes               |
| `stop_call`          | `POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/stop` (owner role)                        | `calls:write`    | call_id, agent_id, reason, idempotency_key (required)                                                | Yes               |

* `get_call_recording` reads the call for its stored recording and then asks for a signed link, which expires after five minutes and is recorded in the workspace's audit log. A call that was not recorded, or whose recording was not kept, is refused `not_found` and nothing is signed. The link is bound to the credential that asked; the audio itself is served only to a signed-in member of the workspace in the App (recordings.md), so a link issued to an API key or an OAuth token does not play. OAuth tokens also need `calls:content:read` to use this tool. The answer explains playback access in `note`. `_meta["org.sempera/resource-domains"]` names the App address the audio is served from.
* `rollback_agent` is available to OAuth grants with `agents:publish` and puts an earlier live deployment back in front of callers through a new rollback record; no version is rewritten. Like `publish_agent_version`, it acts only when `confirm` repeats `agent_id`: otherwise it is refused `validation_failed` naming `confirm` and nothing is rolled back. `version_number` is the version the deployment carries (`list_agent_deployments` lists both); the deployment record checks it and refuses a mismatch. The answer is the rollback record and whether the platform read back the restored version (`verified`).
* `stop_call` ends one active phone call on an agent's line. The caller is disconnected and the call cannot be resumed, so it is marked destructive and open-world. It places no call. `calls:write` is not on any Connected AI client preset or OAuth grant, so only an API key that holds it lists this tool.
* Both writes take `idempotency_key`, write one `mcp.tool_call` audit row per call and one usage row under `mcp:<tool>` per completed call, as the draft tools do.

## Screens

Tools with an MCP Apps screen show the following views in supported hosts. Text-only clients still receive the tool's JSON and a plain-text fallback.

| Screen                  | Resource                                | Tool                                                               |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Agent blueprint         | `ui://sempera/agent-blueprint.html`     | `get_agent_blueprint` (`agents:read`)                              |
| Phone line              | `ui://sempera/phone-profile.html`       | `phone_get_profile` (`phone:read`)                                 |
| Call preview            | `ui://sempera/phone-call-preview.html`  | `phone_preview_call` (`phone:call`)                                |
| Text preview            | `ui://sempera/phone-text-preview.html`  | `phone_preview_text` (`phone:text`)                                |
| Live call status        | `ui://sempera/phone-live-call.html`     | `phone_start_call` (`phone:call`), `phone_get_task` (`phone:read`) |
| Contact thread          | `ui://sempera/phone-thread.html`        | `phone_get_thread` (`phone:text`)                                  |
| Agent card and carousel | `ui://sempera/agent-card.html`          | `get_agent`, `list_agents` (`agents:read`)                         |
| Draft changes           | `ui://sempera/agent-draft-changes.html` | `get_agent_draft_changes` (`agents:read`)                          |
| Call log                | `ui://sempera/call-log.html`            | `list_calls`, `get_call_log` (`calls:read`)                        |
| Call analytics          | `ui://sempera/analytics.html`           | `get_analytics_overview` (`calls:read`)                            |

* The tool names its screen in `_meta.ui.resourceUri` with `visibility` set to `["model", "app"]`. The response also includes the template metadata ChatGPT uses.
* A connection that can call a screen's tool can list it with `resources/list` and read it with `resources/read`. A phone-only OAuth grant cannot read agent or call metadata screens. A registered screen is refused with `403 insufficient_scope` if none of its tools are callable. An unknown URI is a `-32602` error. The front door and `Origin` rule still apply.
* A screen is one self-contained file of type `text/html;profile=mcp-app`. It loads nothing from the network. Both the standard and host-specific content security policies list no connect or resource domains. `_meta.ui.domain` is host-specific: by default it is Claude's sandbox host, the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of this endpoint's URL under `claudemcpcontent.com`. A ChatGPT OAuth grant, named by a verified ChatGPT redirect, gets this API's origin instead, also as `openai/widgetDomain`. The host only changes this value, never which screens or tools a connection gets. `resources/list` and `resources/read` accept the `_meta` object any MCP request may carry.
* A screen talks to the host over the MCP Apps `ui/*` bridge. If the host never answers `ui/initialize` and provides ChatGPT's `window.openai`, the screen reads `toolOutput` and calls its own tools through `callTool` instead.
* The tool's result carries `structuredContent`, the object the screen renders, beside the tool's JSON as the first `text` item and a second `text` item that says it in plain sentences. A refusal is unchanged.
* The agent blueprint re-reads the agent through the host before displaying it. The phone line card shows the delivered result and re-reads only on Refresh. Management screens show only the delivered fields and use the host to open a draft, open a call, or switch the analytics period.
* The agent card uses the authored description or persona, not raw instructions. Bound numbers are shown only with `phone_numbers:read`. The call log marks contact and direction as not shared when the call tool omits them. Analytics accepts a trailing window of 7, 14, 30 or 90 days. Its answered rate covers records classified from the recorded outcome and duration; unclassified calls are excluded from the rate and still included in the call count.
* Draft review uses `publish_agent_version` only after a separate confirmation. It repeats the agent id as `confirm` and sends the reviewed `expect_revision`. Existing role, scope and release checks still apply.

## Not available over MCP

* Archiving or deleting an agent, discarding a draft, buying or releasing a number, inviting members, changing billing, running a paid evaluation, changing a variable or a tool. There is no `/v1` route for buying a number, inviting a member or changing billing. Outbound calls are available only through the separately scoped and approved phone tools described above. The write registry is an explicit list, not arbitrary HTTP access.
* The caller's number and a call's summary. What was said is `get_call_transcript`, behind its own transcript permission.
* Integration detail by key. `list_integrations` answers; there is no tool for one integration.
* Creating, editing, testing or resending webhooks, a pushed post-call event subscription over MCP (Sempera does not call your assistant; read `list_post_call_events` instead, see below), MCP prompts, and any resource other than the screens. The webhook tools only inspect existing endpoints and recorded attempts.

## Post-call notifications over MCP

An assistant learns about finished calls by asking, not by being called. The hosted server opens no event stream and keeps no callback for your assistant: pushed MCP event subscriptions are not switched on, because they still need a release, an owner grant and a durable delivery lifecycle. `list_post_call_events` (`GET /v1/post-call-events`, `calls:read`) is the pull side of the `call.completed` webhook.

* It lists the phone calls of one agent that ended, oldest first, in the order their records were stored. They are the same calls, with the same ids, that `list_calls` and `GET /v1/calls` list; read one with `get_call_log`.
* The answer carries `next_after`. Send it back unchanged as `after` and you get only the calls that ended since. It is returned even when nothing new has ended, so an assistant keeps one value and asks again later. Without `after` the read starts at the oldest retained call. `has_more: true` means more are waiting now.
* An event's `id` is derived from its call, so reading the same calls twice names the same events, and an assistant that lost its place can drop the ones it has seen.
* A call deleted under retention, or recorded with Exclude from history, is not listed. A call from another workspace's agent is refused like an unknown agent.
* An `after` this route did not issue is refused `validation_failed` with `field: after`.

To have Sempera push each finished call to a server you run, create a webhook endpoint for `call.completed` in the App or with `POST /v1/webhooks`; that is unchanged and not available over MCP.

## Draft and test over MCP

Four tools run the same write routes the App and REST clients use, as the caller, with the route's own scope, role, workspace and agent checks. A draft edited here is the one canonical draft the App opens; there is no second copy. They are listed in `tools/list` only to a credential that holds their scope.

| Tool                     | Runs                                                   | Scope                            | Arguments                                                                                                                        | Changes anything? |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `create_agent`           | `POST /v1/agents` (owner role)                         | `agents:write`                   | name (required), template, idempotency_key (required)                                                                            | Yes               |
| `update_agent_draft`     | `PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id}/draft`                    | `agents:write`                   | agent_id (required), fields (required), expect_revision (required), idempotency_key (required)                                   | Yes               |
| `run_agent_tests`        | `POST /v1/tests`                                       | `tests:write`                    | agent_id (required), scenarios, candidate_revision, runtime_policy, idempotency_key (required)                                   | Yes               |
| `run_agent_conversation` | `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/preview`, once per message | `agents:write` and `tests:write` | agent_id (required), messages (required, 1 to 10), version (`draft` or `published`, default `draft`), idempotency_key (required) | Yes               |

* `idempotency_key` is the request's identity: a retry with the same value gets the first answer back and changes nothing again; the same value with a different change is refused `idempotency_key_reused`.
* `update_agent_draft` needs `expect_revision`, the `revision` that `get_agent_draft` returned. An edit made from an older read is refused `conflict` with `reason: stale_draft`, so a newer change by someone else is never overwritten. The keys `fields` may carry are listed in the draft's `editable_fields`; the common ones are `system_prompt` (standing instructions), `greeting` (the first sentence), `voice` (an id from `list_voices`), `request_data` (facts the agent knows on every call, a list of `key` and `value` rows) and `knowledge_collections`.
