* `update_agent_draft` checks every supplied field against the editing contract before the draft route runs, with no model call: a key the editor cannot change, or a value of the wrong shape, is refused `validation_failed` with `error.errors`, one `{field, message}` row per failing field (all of them at once), `error.field` naming the first, and `error.model_calls: 0`. What a value means is still checked when the draft is saved and at publish.
* `get_agent_authoring_context` is the one read a connected assistant needs to write or review an agent itself: the instructions (the draft's when it edited them, else the current document, invisible section markers included: keep them when writing the document back), the other draft fields, warnings, `contract` (`editable_fields` and the `expect_revision` to send), `knowledge` (up to 50 sources) and `checks` (up to 50 scenarios). A section this credential cannot read answers `{"unavailable": <code>}`. Sempera runs no model for it, and its usage row records zero tokens.
* `run_agent_tests` with `candidate_revision` and `runtime_policy` runs the reviewed draft through the App's canonical Checks runner, never a real call, booking, SMS or email. Without both it retains the legacy battery behavior, but a paid or unknown configured runtime is refused. Read the run with `get_test_run`.
* `run_agent_conversation` types each message to the agent in order, on one typed preview session, and answers the transcript: `transcript` holds one row per line (`caller` and `agent` with their `text`, and `tool` with only the `name` of a tool the agent reached for), plus `session_id`, `turns` and `ended`. It is the App's typed preview: never a phone call, every tool answers from its test fixture, and each message counts against the workspace's typed test allowance. A retry with the same `idempotency_key` replays the turns already taken instead of typing them again. If a message is refused, the answer is that refusal with `turns_taken`, the number of messages answered before it. It needs `tests:write` as well as `agents:write`, so a connection granted drafting alone, or testing alone, does not hold it.
* Every call writes one row to the workspace's audit log (`mcp.tool_call`: the tool, the agent, the outcome, the credential id; never the text you sent) and each completed change one builder usage row under `mcp:<tool>` (a refused call or a replayed retry is not counted), apart from the call minutes the call service records.

## Test an agent from your assistant

Your assistant can test an agent turn by turn and grade the result itself. It plays the caller; Sempera runs only the agent. Two tools do this, and neither places a phone call.

| Tool                 | Runs                                                   | Scope                            | Arguments                                                                                                  | Changes anything? |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `test_agent_turn`    | One typed turn of the agent, on Sempera's model        | `agents:write` and `tests:write` | agent_id (required), caller_message (required), history, version (`draft` or `published`, default `draft`) | Yes               |
| `judge_test_locally` | The reads `get_agent_authoring_context` uses; no model | `agents:read`                    | agent_id (required)                                                                                        | No                |

`test_agent_turn` is the one tool on this page built to spend Sempera's model budget on purpose: the agent has to answer as itself, so its side of the turn runs on Sempera's model. Each call is one agent turn, counts one message against the workspace's daily typed test allowance (the same allowance the App's Test and `run_agent_conversation` use), and reports what it used in `usage`. Your assistant's own thinking (writing the caller's lines, grading) costs Sempera nothing.

* **It keeps nothing between calls.** There is no session id. Send the turns so far as `history`, a list of `{"role": "caller" | "agent", "text": "..."}` rows, oldest first, with your next `caller_message`. The answer's `history` is the whole conversation after the turn: pass it back unchanged next time. The prior turns are put in front of the agent as words already said; Sempera runs no model to load them.
* **Limits.** A conversation holds at most 10 caller messages (the one you send counted), so `history` holds at most 19 rows, and each line is at most 4000 characters. More than that is refused `validation_failed` naming the argument, and nothing is run or counted. Start a new conversation instead.
* **The answer.** `reply` (what the agent said), `tool_calls` (each tool the agent reached for: its `name`, the `arguments` the typed preview records for it, its `environment` and a one-sentence `result`), `ended` (the agent finished the call), `history` and `usage`.
* **Nothing real happens.** Every tool answers from its test fixture, on the published version too, so nothing is booked, sent or changed. No conversation record is written.
* **What a replay cannot restore.** The agent starts each call from its first step with the history in front of it. Where it stood in a multi-step flow, and the values it had collected, are not carried over from the earlier calls: it works them out again from the history. For a test that depends on exact step-by-step state, use `run_agent_conversation`, which holds one session for up to ten messages.
* **On a draft, each call compiles the draft again**, so it also counts against the daily limit on tests of unpublished changes. Test the published version (`"version": "published"`) when you are not testing an edit.
* **Refusals.** A reached allowance is `rate_limited` with `retry_after_s` and the sentence a person reads. An agent in another workspace is `not_found`, the same as an id that does not exist. A credential without both scopes is `insufficient_scope`.

`judge_test_locally` returns a rubric and runs no model: `checks` (the agent's test scenarios, each with `when`, `until` and `steps`), `success_criteria` (what each check says must hold, one row each), `conduct_rules` (four fixed rules, the agent's own instructions and its greeting), `how_to_grade` and `answer_format`. Your assistant reads the transcript against it and gives a verdict per item: `pass`, `fail` or `not_tested`. A check the conversation never reached is `not_tested`, not passed. A section this credential cannot read answers `{"unavailable": <code>}`.

### A worked example

First turn. There is no history yet:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.sempera.org/v1/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"test_agent_turn","arguments":{"agent_id":"northwind-barbers","caller_message":"Hi, can I book a haircut for Friday?"}}}'
```

The tool result's text (the numbers are an example):

```json
{
  "object": "agent_test_turn",
  "agent_id": "northwind-barbers",
  "version": "draft",
  "reply": "Hello, this is the assistant at Northwind Barbers. Friday works. Would 10:00 or 14:30 suit you?",
  "tool_calls": [],
  "ended": false,
  "history": [
    {"role": "caller", "text": "Hi, can I book a haircut for Friday?"},
    {"role": "agent", "text": "Hello, this is the assistant at Northwind Barbers. Friday works. Would 10:00 or 14:30 suit you?"}
  ],
  "usage": {"sempera_model_calls": 1, "input_tokens": 1840, "output_tokens": 96, "total_tokens": 1936, "tokens_reported": true}
}
```

Second turn. Send that `history` back with the caller's next line:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.sempera.org/v1/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"test_agent_turn","arguments":{"agent_id":"northwind-barbers","history":[{"role":"caller","text":"Hi, can I book a haircut for Friday?"},{"role":"agent","text":"Hello, this is the assistant at Northwind Barbers. Friday works. Would 10:00 or 14:30 suit you?"}],"caller_message":"14:30 please. My name is Alex."}}}'
```

When the conversation is done, read the rubric and grade the transcript yourself:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.sempera.org/v1/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"judge_test_locally","arguments":{"agent_id":"northwind-barbers"}}}'
```

A verdict your assistant might then write: "Books a haircut: pass (the agent offered two times and confirmed 14:30). Conduct: pass. Reschedules a booking: not_tested."

### Usage on every result

A tool result that involved no Sempera model call says so beside its `content`: `"usage": {"sempera_model_calls": 0}`. Every read carries it (the original three tools, the read tools, the follow-up reads, `get_agent_authoring_context`, `judge_test_locally`, the phone reads), and so does `update_agent_draft`, whose pre-check and save run no model. A refusal of one of those carries it too.

`test_agent_turn` reports its real numbers there and in its answer: `sempera_model_calls` (at most one, including retries and tool follow-ups), `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `total_tokens` and `tokens_reported`. Tokens the model did not report read `null` with `tokens_reported: false`; they are never estimated in the answer. Refusals before the agent runs report zero, and failures after a request retain its count. If a tool answer or a rejected draft would need another model request, it is stopped: `reply` is empty and `note` explains that no reply was completed. Do not grade an incomplete turn as a pass.

Model-free writes also carry zero: `create_agent`, the version, knowledge and number writes, and every phone operation. That describes model use during the tool request only, not a claim that those operations have no other cost or that a queued phone call will use no model later. `run_agent_conversation`, `run_agent_tests` and `run_agent_simulations` are not counted per result here and do not claim zero.

## Connected AI clients

An owner connects one outside client at a time in Settings > Connected clients > Connected AI clients (or `POST /v1/mcp/connections` with `client`, `access` and optional `call_records`, `phone` and `expires_in_days`). Each connection is its own key, shown once, that:

* works on `POST /v1/mcp` and nothing else (any other route answers `403 forbidden`);
* holds a fixed scope list: `read` gives the preset read scopes (call and conversation metadata only with `call_records`), `draft` adds only `agents:write`, `test` adds only `tests:write`, and `build` adds both. Owners can authorize drafting without test execution, or testing without draft edits. Explicit `write` access also adds `agents:publish`, `knowledge:write`, `phone_numbers:read` and `phone_numbers:write`. It never holds `calls:write` or a key scope. Existing keys are not upgraded;
* expires (90 days by default, at most 365) and is listed with when it was last used.

`GET /v1/mcp/connections` lists them and `DELETE /v1/mcp/connections/{connection_id}` disconnects one. Disconnecting revokes that key only: the deployed agents keep answering calls exactly as before. Another workspace's connection, and an ordinary API key, read as `not_found` on these routes.

## Write tools and a safe agent recipe

Choose Write in Settings > Connected clients > Connected AI clients and confirm the permission change. This creates a new expiring key, not an upgrade of an existing connection. Ordinary API keys can use these tools when their scopes and roles allow them. A client should ask its operator to approve publishing and number binding before invoking those tools.

Every write requires `idempotency_key`. Reuse it only for an identical retry. A timeout is not proof that nothing changed: retry with the same key and read the resource before attempting another change.

| Tool                       | Method and path                                  | Scope                 | Arguments besides idempotency_key                                        | Changes anything? |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- |
| `save_agent_version`       | `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/versions`            | `agents:write`        | agent_id                                                                 | Yes               |
| `publish_agent_version`    | `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/publish`             | `agents:publish`      | agent_id, reason, confirm (the agent_id again); optional expect_revision | Yes               |
| `run_agent_simulations`    | `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/simulations`         | `tests:write`         | agent_id, scenario_keys, optional repeats                                | Yes               |
| `bind_phone_number`        | `POST /v1/phone-numbers`                         | `phone_numbers:write` | agent_id, number                                                         | Yes               |
| `create_knowledge_source`  | `POST /v1/knowledge-sources/text`                | `knowledge:write`     | agent_id, name ending in .txt, content                                   | Yes               |
| `update_knowledge_content` | `PATCH /v1/knowledge/{uuid}/content`             | `knowledge:write`     | source_id, content, expect_version_id                                    | Yes               |
| `reparse_knowledge_source` | `POST /v1/knowledge-sources/{source_id}/reparse` | `knowledge:write`     | agent_id, source_id                                                      | Yes               |

| Tool                          | Reads                                                                                                                          | Scope            | Arguments                                     | Changes anything? |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `get_knowledge_content`       | `GET /v1/knowledge/{uuid}/content`                                                                                             | `knowledge:read` | source_id (required)                          | No                |
| `get_agent_simulation`        | `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/simulations/{simulation_id}`                                                                        | `tests:read`     | agent_id (required), simulation_id (required) | No                |
| `get_agent_draft_changes`     | `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/draft`                                                                                              | `agents:read`    | agent_id (required)                           | No                |
| `get_agent_authoring_context` | `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/draft`, `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}`, `GET /v1/knowledge-sources`, `GET /v2/agents/{uuid}/scenarios` | `agents:read`    | agent_id (required)                           | No                |

Follow-up reads are `get_knowledge_content` (`source_id`, `knowledge:read`, `GET /v1/knowledge/{uuid}/content`), `get_agent_simulation` (`agent_id`, `simulation_id`, `tests:read`, `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/simulations/{simulation_id}`) and `get_agent_draft_changes` (`agent_id`, `agents:read`, `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/draft`). For `get_knowledge_content`, pass the library `id` from `list_knowledge_sources` or `get_knowledge_source`, or pass the `content_id` from `create_knowledge_source`. If no text is stored, the tool returns `data.content: null` and an explanation. To edit text, use the `content_id` and pass the `data.version_id` that you read as `expect_version_id`. A stale edit is refused.

`get_agent_draft_changes` compares the draft with the published version, using the same list the App's publish confirmation shows: `changes` has one row per setting that would change (`key`, `label`, `risk`, `before`, `after`, and `truncated` when a value was shortened to fit), `blocking` lists anything that would refuse the publish, and `ready_to_publish` is true only when something would change and nothing blocks it. It also returns the draft's `revision` and `risk_max`. A draft whose highest risk is `HIGH` needs the full name of the person deciding, which `publish_agent_version` does not take, so the tool refuses it with `conflict` and a person publishes it from the App.

`publish_agent_version` publishes only when `confirm` repeats the `agent_id`. A call without it, or with any other value, is refused `validation_failed` naming `confirm`, and nothing is published. A credential without `agents:publish` is refused `insufficient_scope` before its arguments are read.

1. Connect with the narrowest access needed and call `tools/list` to discover available tools.
2. Use `create_agent` with a synthetic business name, then `get_agent_draft` and `update_agent_draft` with the returned revision. The App reads the same draft.
3. Add a text source with `create_knowledge_source`. Use the draft's editable attachment fields to attach its collection. Uploading alone does not attach it or change the live agent.
4. Try the draft with `run_agent_conversation` and read its transcript, then run `run_agent_tests` on the draft and read `get_test_run`. A failed or unavailable runner is not a passed test.
5. Read `get_agent_draft_changes` and show the operator what would change. With their explicit approval, use `publish_agent_version` with `confirm` set to the agent's id to apply the draft and create an immutable version. `save_agent_version` compiles the already approved specification into the current version without applying unpublished edits. OAuth connections need both edit and publish consent for that tool. Both tools leave production environment promotion to its separate controls.
6. Run `run_agent_simulations` with chosen scenario keys and read `get_agent_simulation` until it finishes. The normal offline runner and its required local dependencies must be installed. Simulation results do not establish live-call proof.
7. Only after the normal telephony ownership and entitlement requirements are met, use `bind_phone_number` for an already owned number. Purchasing and releasing numbers are not MCP tools.

The new writes carry `readOnlyHint: false`, explicit effect metadata, and the same audit and usage accounting as the draft tools. Publishing is marked `org.sempera/publishes: true`. Live client interoperability, production database behavior and carrier ownership checks require separate authorized proof; local tests do not claim those.

## Build and test an agent from an outside AI client over REST

A client that does not speak MCP can do the same over the REST API, with a key an owner of the workspace creates in Settings, API keys. The steps below need `agents:write` to create and edit a draft and to try it with a typed preview, and `tests:write` to run the test battery. The key reads results back with the matching `read` scopes. A key made in the App holds every scope a developer key may have, so it can also publish (`agents:publish`) and place a real outbound phone call (`calls:write`). Keep it private and do not paste it into a shared chat.

| Step                                 | Method and path                                                                                                | Scope          |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| Create a draft agent                 | `POST /v1/agents` with `{"name": "..."}` (optional `template`, `answers`)                                      | `agents:write` |
| Read the draft and its revision      | `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/draft`                                                                              | `agents:read`  |
| Edit the draft                       | `PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id}/draft` with `{"fields": {...}, "expect_revision": "..."}`                         | `agents:write` |
| Add a test scenario to the draft     | `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios`                                                                         | `agents:write` |
| Try the draft with one typed message | `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/preview` with `{"message": "..."}`; it never places a call                         | `agents:write` |
| Run the test battery                 | `POST /v1/tests` with `{"agent_id": "...", "scenarios": ["..."]}`; it answers `202` and runs in the background | `tests:write`  |
| Read a test run                      | `GET /v1/tests/{test_id}` (or the `get_test_run` MCP tool)                                                     | `tests:read`   |

Send an `Authorization` header with the value `Bearer <api-key>`, replacing the placeholder with your key (authentication.md). A draft save that carries an old `expect_revision` is refused with `409 conflict`, so read the draft first and send its `revision`.

What a key cannot do:

* **Make another key.** Only an owner signed in to the App can, so a key cannot mint a narrower one.
* **Use the Builder.** The Builder's jobs (start, answer, review, apply) run inside the signed-in app. They are not on the API, and a key does not open them.

A connector that signs in with OAuth, such as a ChatGPT connector, uses the sign-in above.

## Clients

The [connection guides](https://api.sempera.org/docs/supported-clients.md#ai-assistants) cover exactly four assistant entries. ChatGPT and Codex share an entry, with separate instructions. These are connection guides, not claims of live assistant interoperability: no real assistant account has completed the full approved-call journey.

| Assistant     | Connection guide                                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude        | [Claude app and Claude Code](https://api.sempera.org/docs/connect-claude.md)                                                        |
| ChatGPT/Codex | [ChatGPT OAuth](https://api.sempera.org/docs/connect-chatgpt.md), [Codex MCP config](https://api.sempera.org/docs/connect-codex.md) |
| Grok Bot      | [Conditional MCP setup](https://api.sempera.org/docs/connect-grok.md)                                                               |
| Muse          | [Conditional REST connector](https://api.sempera.org/docs/connect-muse.md)                                                          |

`mcp_client_setup` and `GET /v1/mcp/clients/{client}` serve coding-client config snippets. A served snippet is guidance, not evidence that its client has connected. Muse's REST connector uses the same phone operations without MCP.

## Retained candidate checks

Read `get_agent_draft`, review its canonical fields and diff, then pass its revision as `candidate_revision` to `run_agent_tests`. Also pass exactly `runtime_policy: {"evidence":"local-model","tools":"fixture","max_cost":0}`. The two arguments are a pair: a missing policy or revision, a live tool policy, a hosted-model request, a nonzero cost limit or unknown policy fields is refused. The configured hosted fallback is not inherited. If the local model is unavailable, the run fails honestly rather than switching to a paid model.

The candidate response identifies the reviewed draft revision, the SHA-256 of the actual compiled candidate and its parent AgentVersion. Its runtime policy is explicit and `release_evidence` is false. Check results are written to the existing App Checks ledger, so `list_tests` and `get_test_run` can review them after a process restart. This does not create a new builder, agent store, compiler or publication road. These retained runs need Sempera's persistent evidence store; a deployment without it is refused before a battery starts. The actual served model build still needs independent runtime evidence; the policy label is not proof of a model version or a quality pass.

Fixture batteries in automated tests prove the route, compiler, private tool facade, candidate binding, record retention and refusal behavior. They are not local-model quality evidence, live-model evidence, private host receipt or a production approval. ChatGPT authorization remains unavailable until the separately approved external grant and release gates are satisfied.


---

# Authentication and credentials
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/authentication.md

One hostname does not mean one credential. Each class exists for one job and can never do another's.

| Class                             | Used by                                                           | How it authenticates                                                            | What it can never do                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Customer App session              | `app.sempera.org`                                                 | Host-only, HttpOnly, Secure cookie plus a CSRF token on writes                  | Be presented to `api.sempera.org`                                                                     |
| Developer key (`kind: developer`) | A developer's server                                              | `Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_...`                                          | Mint keys (`api_keys:write`)                                                                          |
| Runtime key (`kind: runtime`)     | The agent runtime executing tools                                 | Bearer                                                                          | Publish, edit or create agents, manage keys, read other workspaces, touch billing                     |
| Web session token                 | A browser in a Web voice conversation                             | The short-lived token `POST /v1/sessions` returns, bound to one room            | Anything but join that one conversation                                                               |
| Service key (`kind: service`)     | An internal Sempera service                                       | Bearer                                                                          | Publish, manage keys                                                                                  |
| CI key (`kind: ci`)               | Deployment and smoke automation                                   | Bearer, read-only scopes                                                        | Write anything                                                                                        |
| Admin key (`kind: admin`)         | A workspace owner's elevated automation                           | Bearer                                                                          | Leave its workspace                                                                                   |
| OAuth client                      | ChatGPT, Claude, Codex or Grok Bot, approved by a workspace owner | `Authorization: Bearer sempera_at_...`, one hour, refreshed by a rotating token | Reach anything but `POST /v1/mcp`, or hold a scope beyond `phone:read`, `phone:call` and `phone:text` |
| REST client credential            | A client that cannot do OAuth, such as Muse                       | `Authorization: Bearer <key>`                                                   | Reach anything but the phone routes and MCP endpoint, or buy anything                                 |
| Third-party webhook               | The payment provider, the telephony carrier                       | The provider's own signature or shared token                                    | Reach any other route                                                                                 |

## API keys

The `Authorization` header value is `Bearer <api-key>`. Replace `<api-key>`
with your key; the angle brackets are placeholder notation, not part of it.
Send the key as `Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_...`. No other header or scheme is recognised; a key on a route outside the canonical API surface (`/v1`, `/v2` and the public contract and guide paths) is ignored.

A key has:

- a **workspace**: the one customer account it lives in;
- a **role**: `owner`, `operator` or `viewer`, the same ladder a person has in the workspace. A key is never minted above the role of whoever minted it, and each kind has a ceiling (a runtime or CI key is at most a viewer);
- **scopes**: an explicit list. Each route names the scope it needs; a key without it gets `403 insufficient_scope` before anything runs. `kind` caps which scopes a key may hold at all.

Scopes: `agents:read`, `agents:write`, `agents:publish`, `sessions:read`, `sessions:write`, `calls:read`, `calls:write`, `phone_numbers:read`, `phone_numbers:write`, `tools:read`, `tools:write`, `tools:execute`, `integrations:read`, `integrations:write`, `knowledge:read`, `knowledge:write`, `tests:read`, `tests:write`, `evals:read`, `evals:write`, `workspaces:read`, `workspaces:write`, `organizations:read`, `organizations:write`, `api_keys:read`, `api_keys:write`, `webhooks:read`, `webhooks:write`, `deploy:read`, `models:read`, `prompts:read`, `prompts:write`, `phone:read`, `phone:call`, `phone:text`.

Authorization is two locks: the scope (what the credential was minted for) and the role (what that identity may do to the resource). Both must pass. Default is deny.

## Minting and revoking

A workspace owner creates keys in the Sempera App under Settings, API keys, or with `POST /v1/api-keys` (owner only, `api_keys:write`); either way the secret is shown once. The first key of a workspace is created in the App, because creating a key needs an owner's signed-in session or an admin key, and a developer key can never mint keys. `GET /v1/api-keys` lists keys without secrets. `DELETE /v1/api-keys/{id}` revokes immediately. `GET /v1/me` describes the calling credential.

## Connected clients

Each outside client gets its own grant, so one can be ended without touching another. An owner sees them all in Settings, Connected clients, with scopes and last use.

**OAuth, for MCP hosts.** The host discovers the door from the `401` on `POST /v1/mcp`, registers itself, and sends the browser to a consent page on `app.sempera.org`. Only a signed-in workspace owner can approve, and no key or token can do it for them. The grant covers one client in one workspace with the scopes approved there, and approving the same client again replaces it. The flow is authorization code with PKCE (`S256`), exact redirects and audience binding to `https://api.sempera.org/v1/mcp`. Details are in [MCP](https://api.sempera.org/docs/mcp.md#sign-in-with-oauth).

**A scoped REST credential, for a client that cannot do OAuth.** An owner creates one in Settings, Connected clients, or with `POST /v1/client-grants/rest` (`client`, `scopes`, optional `expires_in_days`). It holds phone scopes only, works on the phone routes and MCP endpoint only, expires in 90 days by default (at most 365), and is shown once.

`GET /v1/client-grants` lists every connected client (OAuth, MCP keys and REST credentials) and `DELETE /v1/client-grants/{grant_id}` ends one. An ordinary API key, another workspace's client and an unknown id all read as `not_found`.

## Browser clients

For customer-facing voice, keep the workspace API key on your server. Your server calls `POST /v1/sessions` and hands the browser the returned `token` and `url`; the token is scoped to one room and expires with the conversation. Never embed a workspace key in a public bundle.

Developer tools can call the public `/v1` API using an explicitly supplied `Authorization` bearer key and `credentials: "omit"`. The configured Sempera documentation origin may preflight the route's supported methods, including writes. Other origins may preflight read-only methods when `Access-Control-Request-Headers` includes `Authorization`; the actual read must carry the bearer key. A preflight announces the header name, not the key, and grants no access by itself: the actual request still needs valid authentication, scopes and workspace permissions.

CORS does not enable credentials mode. Requests carrying cookies, session-only routes, OAuth protocol doors, provider/server-to-server ingress, legacy `/api` routes and routes outside `/v1` receive no permissive CORS headers. Allowed request headers are `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `Idempotency-Key`, `X-Request-Id` and `traceparent`. Browser callers can read request and correlation ids, rate-limit and retry headers, `Idempotent-Replayed`, `Location`, `WWW-Authenticate` and `Content-Disposition` on permitted responses, including errors.

## Sign-in for people

People sign in to the Sempera App with Google, Apple, email or phone. Those roads live on `app.sempera.org` and never on the API.


---

# Agents
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/agents.md

An Agent is Sempera's core product object: an AI phone agent that answers a business's phone or Web calls, extra capacity for the business's team rather than a replacement for its people.

## Listing agents

`GET /v1/agents` (`agents:read`) lists the Agents the credential can see, with the cursor pagination in errors-and-limits.md. `status` is `active` (the default), `archived` or `all`; any other value is `400 validation_failed` with `field: status`. An Agent that cannot be read at the moment is not dropped: it appears as `{"id", "object": "agent", "status": "needs_repair", "reason"}`, so a list never silently shrinks.

## Creating an agent from a template

`POST /v1/agents` (`agents:write`) takes `name` (the business name) and an optional `template`. A template is a versioned role package, so a new agent starts with a real greeting, written instructions, structured call outcomes and a set of tests, not only a role name. `GET /v2/agents/starter-templates` (`agents:read`) lists the roles you can name, each with its `slug`, `title`, `description`, `version` and a short `capabilities_summary` (`can` and `cannot`). Omit `template` for a blank agent. An unknown slug is refused with `400 validation_failed` and nothing is created.

| Template                   | What the agent does                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `customer-support`         | Answers approved questions and captures unresolved issues for staff.                                                                                                                    |
| `appointment-scheduler`    | Captures new, move and cancellation requests for staff to confirm.                                                                                                                      |
| `front-desk`               | Greets callers, answers approved basics and takes messages for the team.                                                                                                                |
| `lead-qualification`       | Understands an inbound lead and captures a consultation request for staff.                                                                                                              |
| `restaurant-ordering`      | Captures pickup orders and answers approved menu questions for staff review.                                                                                                            |
| `after-hours-lead-capture` | Answers when the team cannot (overflow or after hours), captures the caller's name, company, phone, email, reason, urgency and preferred callback time, and writes a summary for staff. |
| `appointment-request`      | Collects an appointment request and says the business will confirm it.                                                                                                                  |

The two newest roles never invent a price, an opening time or a booking, never say an appointment is booked and never give a confirmation number. They say plainly that they are an AI assistant if asked. Neither can transfer a call or send a message in this release.

Each agent records the template `slug` and `version` it was created from in its first version's `provenance`. The package is copied once at creation. Changing a template later does not change an agent that already exists, and an agent created without a template is exactly as it was before.

`appointment-request` accepts two optional settings in `answers.template_variables`, sent together with `template`: `booking_link`, the business's own `http` or `https` booking address (the agent offers that exact link and no other; an invalid link is refused with `400 validation_failed`), and `industry_details`, a list of extra intake questions such as a vehicle make and model. With neither, the agent offers no link and asks no extra questions.

## Shape

`GET /v1/agents/{id}` returns the Agent with its stable `id`, `name`, `workspace_id`, `status` (`draft`, `published`, `archived`), the published version pointer, the verification gates, the channels it can speak on, and, on the detail read, its `draft`, `published`, `voice`, `language`, `instructions`, `tools` and `knowledge`.

`channels` says where the Agent can be reached: `web_voice`, `web_chat`, and `phone`, which is `true` once a phone number is set up for the Agent (a number bound to it, or a line released through its deployments). It is the same reading as the phone step of the App's launch checklist, and a numbers read that fails never reports a phone.

Provider identifiers (the voice platform's pathway or persona ids) are internal and never the Agent's identity.

The Agent's `voice` is `{id, name}` (plus `unresolved: true` when Sempera cannot say which engine the stored voice is on), where `id` is the Sempera voice id `GET /v1/voices` lists. A draft takes a voice the same way: `PATCH /v1/agents/{id}/draft` with `{"fields": {"voice": {"id": "voice_...", "name": "..."}}}`. The draft and every version store the underlying voice that id stands for, so a published version keeps speaking with exactly the voice it was built with.

## Workspace background sound

The workspace can store one custom background clip for its agents. `GET /v1/workspace-sound` (`agents:read`) returns `sound.available` and metadata for the current clip. `POST /v1/workspace-sound` (`agents:write`) replaces it using a single multipart `file` field, up to 5 MB. `DELETE /v1/workspace-sound` (`agents:write`) removes it.

The credential must be bound to the workspace. If you supply the optional `workspace` query parameter, it must match the credential's workspace. Upload returns `409 conflict` when the workspace is closing and `503 service_unavailable` when storage or the upload service is unavailable.

## Draft, preview, publish

Every Agent has one editable **draft** and a ledger of immutable **published versions**.

| Step                   | Route                                                                       | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Read the draft         | `GET /v1/agents/{id}/draft`                                                 | `editable_fields` lists the keys a PATCH may carry; their current values and choices are the named sections of `GET /v1/agents/{id}` (`instructions`, `voice`, `guardrails`, ...)                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Edit the draft         | `PATCH /v1/agents/{id}/draft`                                               | `{"fields": {...}, "expect_revision": "..."}`; a stale revision is refused with `409 conflict` and the current revision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Discard the draft      | `DELETE /v1/agents/{id}/draft`                                              |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Typed preview          | `POST /v1/agents/{id}/preview`                                              | One caller turn against the draft (default) or the published version; carry `session_id` to continue                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Web voice preview      | `POST /v1/sessions`                                                         | Always the published version                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Publish                | `POST /v1/agents/{id}/publish`                                              | Decides, applies and compiles: a new immutable version. Accepts `Idempotency-Key`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Versions               | `GET /v1/agents/{id}/versions`, `GET /v1/agents/{id}/versions/{version_id}` | Never mutated. `{version_id}` is a version's id or its number; a version this agent does not have is `404 not_found`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Deployments            | `GET /v1/agents/{id}/deployments`                                           | The release ledger on the voice platform                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Releases across agents | `GET /v1/release-deployments`                                               | `deploy:read`. Every version put on an environment, for every Agent the credential can see, newest first, with cursor pagination. Each row is a `release_deployment` with `agent_id`, `agent_name`, `workspace_id`, `version_id`, `version_number`, `environment` (`staging`, `production` or `practice`), `action` (`draft`, `promotion` or the ledger's own kind), `status`, `by` and `at` |
| Rollback               | `POST /v1/agents/{id}/rollback`                                             | `{"to_deployment_id": "..."}` creates a NEW rollback record; history is never rewritten                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

Production calls and sessions always run a published version. Secrets never appear in a version read; tool authentication is reported as a secret reference, configured or not.

## Lifecycle

`POST /v1/agents/{id}/archive` hides an agent, and `POST /v1/agents/{id}/unarchive` brings it back (`agents:write` for both). Each answers the Agent with an `archive` result, and a refusal is `409 conflict` with a sentence saying why. `DELETE /v1/agents/{id}` with `{"confirm": "<id>"}` removes the record, its conversations and its number bindings; it is refused while a version is live.

## Publishing roles

Publishing needs `agents:publish` on the key and the `owner` role in the workspace. An operator can edit and preview the draft; only an owner can make it live.

## Contact card and business identity

An agent has a contact card and owner-provided business details: `display_name`, `legal_name`, `phone`, `email`, `website`, `address`, `country` and `registration_number`. Reads need `agents:read`; writes need `agents:write` and the `owner` role.

| Route                                              | Does                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/identity`               | Reads `{profile, verification, revision}`.                                                                                                            |
| `PUT /v1/agents/{agent_id}/identity`               | Saves the whole `profile` with the `revision` you read; a stale revision is `409 conflict`. Changing the profile resets verification to `unverified`. |
| `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/identity/verification` | Records a review request for the `revision` you read. It needs legal name, address, country and registration number.                                  |
| `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/identity/vcard`         | Downloads the card as `text/vcard`.                                                                                                                   |
| `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/identity/send-test`    | Checks the delivery boundary for a `to` number. It always answers `503 owner_setup_required` with `sent: false`: nothing is sent.                     |

`verification.status` is `unverified` or `pending_review`. A review request is not a verified badge, `verified_at` stays `null`, and no client can mark a business verified.


---

# Custom model connections
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/custom-models.md

Custom model setup is in limited testing. Contact Sempera to confirm whether your workspace can test a custom model connection. Check the [live OpenAPI contract](https://api.sempera.org/openapi.json) for the supported developer operations.

`POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/custom-llm/test` checks whether Sempera can reach an endpoint and get a compatible response. The test does not save a credential, publish an agent or place a call.

Where saving is enabled, `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/custom-llm` stores the credential and updates the agent's draft. Send the current draft revision in `expect_revision`. Confirm that a published agent uses the chosen model before relying on it in production.

Use a public HTTPS base address without credentials, a query or a fragment. Sempera appends the chat completions path. Use a key dedicated to Sempera and provide it in the connection form or the write-only `api_key` field. See secrets-and-signing.md for secret storage and agents.md for publishing and versions.


---

# Agent branches
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/branches.md

A branch is a second working draft of an agent, cut from its main draft (what the App calls Development), so a change can be prepared apart and landed in one step. Merging is a fast-forward only: a branch lands while main has not moved since the branch was cut or last rebased, and otherwise it must be rebased first. Nothing here publishes; after a merge, main's draft is published the usual way (agents.md).

These are `/v2` compatibility routes (api-overview.md). `{agent_id}` is the Sempera agent id, and a branch id is a UUID.

| Route                                                            | Scope          | Notes                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/branches`                             | `agents:read`  | The agent's open branches, oldest first                         |
| `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/branches`                            | `agents:write` | `{"name"}`. Cuts a branch from main's draft as it stands. `201` |
| `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/branches/{branch_id}/rebase-preview` | `agents:write` | What rebasing onto main's current head would do. Writes nothing |
| `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/branches/{branch_id}/rebase`         | `agents:write` | Rebase onto the head the preview named, settling each conflict  |
| `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/branches/{branch_id}/merge`          | `agents:write` | Land the branch on main and close it                            |
| `DELETE /v2/agents/{agent_id}/branches/{branch_id}`              | `agents:write` | Close the branch without landing it: `{"deleted": true}`        |

Writes need the `operator` or `owner` role. A branch reads `id`, `agent_id`, `name`, `base_version_id`, `created_by`, `created_at` and `behind`, which is true once main has moved past the point the branch was cut from or last rebased onto.

A branch `name` is 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores or dashes, unique among the agent's open branches. `dev`, `latest`, `staging`, `production` and version-like names such as `1.2.3` are reserved.

## Rebase and merge

Branches are compared one draft setting at a time, with the instructions document counting as one setting. The preview answers `{"dev_head_version_id", "up_to_date", "auto_merged", "changes", "conflicts"}`: `changes` are settings only main changed, taken automatically; `conflicts` are settings both sides changed differently. Each item carries `id` (`setting:<key>`), `key`, `label`, `base` and `theirs` (main's value); a conflict adds `ours` (the branch's value).

```http
POST /v2/agents/northwind-barbers/branches/{branch_id}/rebase
{"dev_head_version_id": "<from the preview>", "resolutions": {"setting:greeting": "ours"}}
```

Every conflict needs a resolution: `"ours"`, `"theirs"` or `{"value": ...}`, a new value that passes the same checks a draft edit does. The merged result becomes the branch's draft and its base moves to main's head. The answer is `{"version", "auto_merged", "resolved"}`. If main moved since the preview, the rebase is refused and you preview again.

A merge takes no body and answers `{"version", "merged_fields"}`, the settings the branch changed.

## Refusals

Answers use the compatibility envelope `{"data": ..., "errors": null}`; a refusal these routes make is `{"data": null, "errors": [{"error", "message"}]}`. A missing credential, scope or role, and a request body that is not a JSON object, get the standard error envelope (errors-and-limits.md).

| Status | `error`                                       | When                                                                                                                          |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400`  | `INVALID_NAME`                                | The name breaks the rule above                                                                                                |
| `400`  | `INVALID_RESOLUTIONS`, `UNRESOLVED_CONFLICTS` | A resolution is malformed or its value is refused, or a conflict has none                                                     |
| `400`  | `NO_CHANGES`                                  | Merging a branch with no changes of its own                                                                                   |
| `404`  | `NOT_FOUND`                                   | No such agent, or no such open branch of it in this workspace. Deleting a branch that is not there answers `BRANCH_NOT_FOUND` |
| `409`  | `BRANCH_EXISTS`                               | An open branch already has this name                                                                                          |
| `409`  | `REBASE_STALE`                                | Main changed since the preview, or `dev_head_version_id` is missing or does not match main's head                             |
| `409`  | `BRANCH_BEHIND`                               | Main moved past the branch's base; preview, rebase, then merge again. Nothing is written                                      |
| `503`  | `UNAVAILABLE`                                 | The deployment has no database to keep branches in                                                                            |

Editing a branch's own draft is done in the Sempera App today; `PATCH /v1/agents/{id}/draft` edits main.


---

# Personas
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/personas.md

A persona is the identity an agent speaks with: the name callers hear, and the call settings that go with it. Sempera keeps one persona per agent, so the same persona answers on every number and channel the agent has. The personas routes are a **read-only view** of each agent, in a fixed shape; there is nothing to create, edit or delete here. Change the name, voice or call settings on the agent's draft and publish (agents.md).

| Route                           | Scope         | Notes                                                          |
| ------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/personas`              | `agents:read` | One persona per active agent the credential can read           |
| `GET /v1/personas/{persona_id}` | `agents:read` | One persona. `{persona_id}` is `per_` followed by the agent id |

`GET /v1/personas` takes `page` (from 1, default 1) and `limit` (1 to 100, default 20) and answers `{"data": [...], "errors": null}` with no total and no cursor; a page past the end is an empty list, and a `page` or `limit` outside its range is `400 validation_failed`. `GET /v1/personas/{persona_id}` answers the persona itself, unwrapped. An id that does not start with `per_` is `404 not_found`, and so is an agent the credential cannot read.

## The persona

A persona reads `id` (`per_<agent id>`), `name`, `description`, `image_url`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`, `current_draft_version_id`, `current_production_version_id`, `current_draft_version`, `current_production_version`, `inbound_numbers` and `workspace_id`. `name` is the agent's persona name, or its name when it has none. Both version ids are the same id, and both versions carry the same content: the draft copy differs only in `version_type` (`draft`).

A version reads `id` (`perver_<agent id>_production`), `persona_id`, `version_type`, `version_number`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `promoted_at`, `promoted_by`, `promoted_from_version_id`, `personality_prompt`, `orchestration_prompt`, `call_config`, `default_tools`, `entity_schemas`, `kb_ids`, `memory_enabled`, `pathway_conditions`, `skills` and `auth_config`. `call_config` reads `language`, `timezone`, `voice`, `record`, `wait_for_greeting`, `noise_cancellation`, `max_duration`, `transfer_phone_number`, `keywords`, `pronunciation_guide` and `background`.

What follows the agent, read from its current specs, call settings and version history:

| Field                                                                         | Value                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`, `name`, `workspace_id`                                                  | The agent's id, persona name and workspace                                                                                                            |
| `description`                                                                 | The agent's role, as its specs name it (for example `front-desk coordinator`); `null` when its specs cannot be read                                   |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`                                                    | When the agent's first version and its newest version were built; `null` for an agent that has never been built                                       |
| `version_number`, and a version's `created_at` and `updated_at`               | The number of the version the agent runs now, and when that version was built; `null` for an agent that has never been built                          |
| `personality_prompt`                                                          | The persona name again, not the agent's instructions (read those from `GET /v1/agents/{id}`)                                                          |
| `call_config.language`                                                        | The agent's language code, as its specs store it; `null` when its specs cannot be read                                                                |
| `call_config.timezone`                                                        | The business's time zone, the one the agent answers hours questions in; `null` when its specs cannot be read                                          |
| `call_config.voice`                                                           | The id of the voice the agent's calls use; `null` when no voice has been chosen or its specs cannot be read                                           |
| `call_config.record`, `wait_for_greeting`, `noise_cancellation`, `background` | The agent's call settings; `null` for the first three when its specs cannot be read                                                                   |
| `call_config.max_duration`                                                    | The longest a call may run, in seconds; `null` when the agent sets no limit of its own                                                                |
| `call_config.keywords`, `pronunciation_guide`                                 | The agent's speech keywords and pronunciation entries. Engine-specific keyword caps and editor hearing settings are documented in hearing-settings.md |
| `memory_enabled`                                                              | Whether the agent remembers callers (memory-schema.md); `null` when its specs cannot be read                                                          |

What is a fixed value, whatever the agent is configured with: `image_url`, `deleted_at` and `auth_config` are `null`; `promoted_at`, `promoted_by` and `promoted_from_version_id` are `null`, because Sempera records when a version was built, not when it began reaching callers; `orchestration_prompt` is `null`, because an agent runs one conversation and has no routing prompt; `transfer_phone_number` is `""`; and `inbound_numbers`, `default_tools`, `entity_schemas`, `kb_ids`, `pathway_conditions` and `skills` are empty lists. Read the agent's tools and knowledge from its detail read (`GET /v1/agents/{id}`) and its numbers from `GET /v1/phone-numbers?agent_id=` (sessions-and-calls.md).


---

# Hearing settings
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/hearing-settings.md

An agent's draft takes these settings through the same publish step as every other call setting (agents.md). They are saved under the same names in the agent's published call settings, and the draft and published reads of the agent show them.

| Setting                   | Values                                                                                                                | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `noise_cancellation`      | `true`, `false`, or an object with exactly `web`, `inbound` and `outbound`, each `off`, `noise` or `noise_and_voices` | Reduces background sound before the caller is recognised. `true` uses the existing noise filter on every channel. The `calls.noise_cancellation` read stays a boolean for older screens, and `calls.noise_cancellation_channels` holds the level for each channel.                                                     |
| `keywords`                | a list of up to 50 terms                                                                                              | Names and terms the recogniser should listen for. The limit depends on the recognition engine in use: `calls.keywords_max` shows it for the engine the agent uses, and an engine that takes no keywords reports 0. A new edit past the limit is refused with that limit. Keywords already published are not rewritten. |
| `max_wait_when_unsure_ms` | `null`, or a whole number from 600 to 4000                                                                            | The longest the agent waits for more speech when it is unsure the caller has finished. `null` is automatic: the response wait plus 500 ms. Not set keeps the previous timing.                                                                                                                                          |
| `ignore_phrases`          | up to 50 phrases of 1 to 40 characters                                                                                | Short phrases such as "uh huh" that do not interrupt the agent. Phrases are trimmed and compared without regard to case, and duplicates are dropped. A longer sentence that contains a phrase still counts as an interruption.                                                                                         |
| `echo_guard`              | an object with exactly `web`, `inbound` and `outbound`, each `true` or `false`                                        | For the first 3 seconds after the agent starts speaking, uncertain overlapping speech is ignored. Speech that carries on for the interruption sensitivity window is accepted. Not set means off on all three channels.                                                                                                 |

`noise_and_voices` is saved, but at present it applies the same noise reduction as `noise`; the call record says so. Ignore phrases and echo guard make interruptions wait for the final recognised words, because a whole phrase cannot be told from partial words.


---

# Caller memory schema
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/memory-schema.md

An agent can remember facts about the people who call it, so a returning caller is not asked the same questions twice. The memory schema says which facts the agent may keep. It is read from the agent's configuration; there is no route to write it.

| Route                                     | Scope                       | Notes                                              |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/memory/schema` | `agents:read`               | The agent's memory schema                          |
| `GET /v1/memory/changes`                  | `agents:read`, `owner` role | What the agents learned or corrected, newest first |

## Owner write API

All writes require `agents:write`, the owner-only `manage_contact_memory`
capability, an active entitled workspace, and an agent visible to the credential.
Existing workspace-bound storage and its database access rules apply; no new store is created.

- `POST /v1/memory`: `agent_id`, international `number` (for example
  `+12025550123`), `contact`, lowercase `key`, `value` (up to 300 characters),
  and `kind` (`fact` or `summary`, default `fact`). Returns 201 with the memory id.
  Facts use the existing replacement history. Summaries append entries.
- `PATCH /v1/memory/{memory_id}`: `agent_id` and `value`. Corrects a fact or
  summary by id, preserving correction history. Foreign rows return 404.
- `POST /v1/memory/reset`: `agent_id`, `number`, `reason`, `confirm: true`.
  Forgets all contacts on that one line for that agent, including verification
  credentials, and returns the existing deletion receipt. Legal hold returns 409.
- `PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id}/memory`: boolean `enabled` and `expect_revision`
  from the agent draft read. Saves only the draft. Publish separately to make it
  live. A stale revision returns 409.

Writes use owner provenance, not caller-controlled verification claims. Missing
workspace storage returns 503, never an invented successful memory write.
The console offers fact and summary entry, correction, and confirmed line reset.

## The schema

```json
{"object": "memory_schema", "enabled": true, "source": "settings",
 "entity_schemas": [{"entity_type": "contact",
                     "description": "Facts this agent may remember about a caller",
                     "identifier_field": "name",
                     "fields": [{"name": "preferred_time", "type": "string",
                                 "description": "Usual time of day", "required": false}]}]}
```

| `enabled`                              | `source`         | `entity_schemas`                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `false`                                | `null`           | Empty. The agent remembers nothing                                                                                           |
| `true`, with fields named on the agent | `settings`       | One `contact` entity holding those fields                                                                                    |
| `true`, with no fields named           | `cached_version` | One `contact` entity holding four default fields: `preferred_time`, `preferred_language`, `name` and `first_name`, each text |

A field is `name`, `type` (`string` unless the agent says otherwise), `description` and `required`. An agent that names fields by name alone gets `string` fields with an empty description that are not required.

Memory is turned on with the `contact_memory` field of the agent's draft (`"on"`), and the fields are the `memory_schema` field, a list of names (`PATCH /v1/agents/{id}/draft`, agents.md). The route reads the agent's configuration as last published, so a draft edit shows here only after the agent is published.

## What the schema decides

When a call ends, Sempera writes what it learned to the caller's memory. While memory is on, a fact it captured from the caller whose key is not a field of the schema is dropped. A caller's name is stored as `first_name`, so a schema that names its own fields should include `first_name` if names are to be remembered. A one-line summary of the call and the call's open tasks are not facts and are not filtered by the schema. Memory is kept for the retention period the workspace owner set.

The schema is a filter on writes only. It never removes what was stored before it changed, and a workspace owner can view, correct and forget a caller's memory in the App.

## Memory changes

`GET /v1/memory/changes` answers `{"data": {"changes", "initial_memory", "memory_history"}, "errors": null}`. It covers every agent the credential can read, or one agent with `agent_id`. `memory_history` is up to 100 entries, newest first, each with `id`, `timestamp`, `type` (`fact_update`, `summary_update` or `task_update`), `key`, `value`, `agent_id`, `source`, `verified`, `call_id`, `corrected_from` (the id of the entry this one replaced) and `superseded` (true once it was corrected; forgotten entries never appear). Add `call_id` (or `conversation_id`) to see one call's entries: `changes` is then what that call left in memory, as `facts` (key to value), `summary` and `open_items`, and a call with no entries is `404` with `{"data": null, "errors": [{"error": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "..."}]}`. Without `call_id`, `changes` is `null`. `initial_memory` is always `null`: Sempera keeps no snapshot of memory from before a call. The route needs the `owner` role as well as the scope; other roles are refused with `403 forbidden`.

## Contacts

Contacts are the people your agents have remembered, grouped across the workspace. These routes need the `owner` role as well as the scope.

| Route                       | Scope          | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/contacts/schema`   | `agents:read`  | Reads the shared contact schema: `{fields, revision}`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `PUT /v1/contacts/schema`   | `agents:write` | Replaces the fields (up to 50, each `name`, `type` of `string`, `number`, `boolean` or `date`, `description`, `required`). Send the `revision` you read; a stale revision is `409 conflict`.                                                                                             |
| `POST /v1/contacts/merge`   | `agents:write` | Groups two console profiles with `source_id` and `target_id`; answers `{id, merged, note}`.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `POST /v1/contacts/resolve` | `agents:read`  | Finds a contact by `contact_id`, or by `phone` (international, starting with `+`) with an optional `name`. Answers `status` (`resolved`, `ambiguous` or `not_found`), the `contact` when exactly one matches, and the `candidates` as `{id, name}`. It never guesses between candidates. |

A merge groups profiles for the owner only. Each memory entry keeps its own agent, line, provenance, expiry and verification, nothing about how a caller is recognised on a call changes, and a caller never gets another person's history.


---

# Scenarios
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/scenarios.md

A scenario is one situation an agent knows how to handle: when it applies, what to do, and when the agent may move on. "The caller wants to move an appointment; find the booking, offer two new times; keep going until the new time is confirmed." A scenario is a block inside the agent's own words (the "Anything else" part of its instructions), so a scenario is part of the draft, compiles into the agent when it is published and has no store of its own.

These are `/v2` compatibility routes (api-overview.md). `{agent_id}` is the Sempera agent id and `{id}` a scenario id. A scenario keeps its id across versions; a copy in another agent has its own. Reads need `agents:read`. Writes change the agent's working draft, so they need `agents:write` and the `operator` or `owner` role, and nothing reaches callers until the draft is published (agents.md).

| Route                                               | Scope          | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios`               | `agents:read`  | `{"agent_id", "revision", "current", "archived"}`: the scenarios in the draft, and the ones taken out of it                                                                                                                      |
| `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios`              | `agents:write` | Add one to the draft. `201`                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios/{id}`          | `agents:read`  | One scenario, current or archived                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios/{id}`         | `agents:write` | Replace one current scenario with the fields below plus `expect_revision`, the draft `revision` as last read. A renamed scenario answers with its new id. `409` when the draft changed since that read or the new name is taken  |
| `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios/{id}/archive` | `agents:write` | Take it out of the draft and keep it, restorable. It is not part of the agent once published                                                                                                                                     |
| `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios/{id}/restore` | `agents:write` | Put an archived scenario back into the draft                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `DELETE /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios/{id}`       | `agents:write` | Remove it for good, from the draft or from the archive. Answers the scenario with `"deleted": true`                                                                                                                              |
| `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios/{id}/copy`    | `agents:write` | `{"agent_id": "<the other agent>"}`. Adds a copy to that agent's draft. `201`                                                                                                                                                    |
| `GET /v2/scenarios`                                 | `agents:read`  | Every readable agent's current scenarios: `{"scenarios", "agents"}`, each scenario with its `agent_name`, and `agents` every agent the credential can read (the choices for a copy). `agent_id` narrows `scenarios` to one agent |
| `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios/{id}/history`  | `agents:read`  | One scenario per published version                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/scenarios/agent/history` | `agents:read`  | The agent's own words as a whole per published version                                                                                                                                                                           |

## Pathway folders

`GET /v2/scenarios` also returns `organization`, keyed by readable agent id. Each value has `revision`, `folders` (`id`, `name`), `placements` (pathway id to folder id or null), and `order` (saved pathway ids).

`POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/pathway-organization` needs `agents:write` and the same operator/owner capability, workspace and agent checks as pathway edits. Send `expect_revision` from that agent's organization value and one action:

- `{"action":"create_folder","name":"Bookings","expect_revision":"..."}`
- `{"action":"move","scenario_id":"...","folder_id":"...","expect_revision":"..."}`. A null folder moves to the root. Both the pathway and folder must belong to this agent.
- `{"action":"reorder","order":["..."],"expect_revision":"..."}`. List every current pathway exactly once.

The response is the saved organization value. Stale revisions and duplicate names are `409`; foreign or missing resources are `404`; invalid actions are `400`. Folder changes persist immediately and are audited, but do not change runtime content or publish an agent.
