Folder names are single lines, 1 to 120 characters, unique per agent ignoring case, with at most 100 folders. No provider request is made.

### Create a pathway

```http
POST /v2/agents/northwind-barbers/scenarios
{"name": "Reschedule a booking", "type": "complex",
 "when": "the caller wants to move an appointment",
 "until": "the new time is confirmed",
 "steps": ["find the booking", "offer two new times"]}
```

| Field          | Rule                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`         | Required, up to 120 characters                                                                                   |
| `when`         | Required: when the scenario applies                                                                              |
| `until`        | Required: the point at which the agent may move on                                                               |
| `type`         | `simple` (default), `complex` or `authentication`                                                                |
| `steps`        | 1 to 12 lines. Needed by `complex`, allowed by `authentication`, refused by `simple`                             |
| `verification` | The check that must pass before the agent goes on. Needed by `authentication`, refused by `simple` and `complex` |

`when`, `until`, each step and `verification` are single lines of up to 500 characters and may not begin with `Situation:`, `When:`, `Keep going until:`, `Only after:` or `Step:`. Any other field is refused. The type is read back from the shape, never stored: a scenario with a `verification` is `authentication`, one with steps is `complex`, and one with neither is `simple`.

A scenario reads `id`, `agent_id`, `name`, `named`, `when`, `until`, `verification`, `steps`, `text` (the block as it sits in the instructions), `type`, `type_label`, `state` (`current` or `archived`), `archived_at` and `archived_by`. An agent has at most 50 current scenarios, and a name is unique among its current and archived ones, ignoring case.

## History

`.../history` answers `{"versions", "next_cursor", "environments"}`. `versions` is newest first; each entry has `id`, `name` (`Version 4`), `version_number`, `created_at`, `author`, `added` and `removed` (lines changed against the version before) and `node`, the scenario as that version had it, or null once it was taken out. `environments` names the version the staging and production environments run, with the same `node`. A version whose specs were not kept cannot be read and is left out. `next_cursor` is always null.

## Refusals

Answers use the compatibility envelope `{"data": ..., "errors": null}`; a refusal about the thing named is `{"data": null, "errors": [{"error", "message"}]}`. A missing credential, scope or role gets the standard error envelope (errors-and-limits.md).

A stale pathway save adds `reason: stale_scenario` and `revision` to the first
`CONFLICT` error. Nothing is written or audited as a successful save. Ask the
owner before retrying their held fields with that revision; a further save by
someone else is refused again. To discard local edits, read the scenario and
revision together from the agent's scenario list, without writing. A duplicate
name or other conflict does not carry this reason or revision and must not be
treated as permission to overwrite. A missing or foreign pathway remains a
`404` and discloses no revision.

| Status | `error`       | When                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------ | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400`  | `BAD_REQUEST` | A field breaks a rule above, or the copy names the agent itself                                                                                                                        |
| `404`  | `NOT_FOUND`   | No such agent (or one the credential cannot reach), or no such scenario                                                                                                                |
| `409`  | `CONFLICT`    | The name is taken, the agent is at its 50, the scenario is already archived (or, for a restore, not archived), or the draft changed while the write was made and it should be repeated |

## Test scenarios

Test scenarios are a separate thing: scripted caller cases the test battery plays against an agent (tests-and-evals.md). `GET /v1/agent-testing/scenarios` (`agents:read`) lists them with `agent_id` (one agent, default every readable agent), `category` and `enabled` (`true` or `false`, anything else is `400 validation_failed`) as filters, in the compatibility envelope. Each row carries `id`, `name`, `tester_persona_prompt`, `max_turns`, `start_node_id`, `request_data`, `tags`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and `agent_id`; the remaining fields are fixed. `GET /v1/agent-testing/scenarios/{id}/eval-agents` (`agents:read`) lists the judges that score a test scenario's calls: this workspace's enabled evals that apply to the scenario's agent, in name order, each weighted `1` and aimed at the pass level (`target_level_keys: ["P"]`).


---

# Sessions and calls
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/sessions-and-calls.md

## Sessions

A Session is one conversation with an Agent on any channel:

| `channel`   | Where it came from                                           |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `web_voice` | A browser voice conversation opened with `POST /v1/sessions` |
| `web_chat`  | A typed preview turn                                         |
| `api_chat`  | An authenticated API chat turn with the published agent      |
| `simulator` | A simulated caller with a synthetic caller id                |
| `phone`     | A real phone call (also a Call)                              |
| `test`      | A scripted test scenario                                     |

`GET /v1/sessions?agent_id=...` lists them newest first; `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` returns the transcript (`turns`), the tool timeline and captured variables where the runtime recorded them, latency, outcome and the version that spoke.

## Live translation

`GET /v1/translation-sessions?agent_id=...` reads availability and recent sessions with `sessions:read`.
`POST /v1/translation-sessions` takes `agent_id`, `caller_language` and `staff_language`, requires `sessions:write`, and returns two room-scoped join tokens. Both routes require workspace activation and access to the agent. No phone call is placed. Tokens must not be logged or shared outside the intended participants.

## Dialing pools

These routes require access to the agent and the workspace's dialing-pool entitlement. Reads need `calls:read`; configuration writes need `calls:write` and permission to send outbound calls.

| Route                                                        | Behavior                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/dialing-pools`                    | Lists pools and owned-number readiness.                                                                 |
| `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/dialing-pools/{pool_id}`          | Reads one pool in this workspace and agent.                                                             |
| `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/dialing-pools`                   | Creates a pool from `name`, `phone_numbers`, `daily_cap` and `local_only`; supports an idempotency key. |
| `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/dialing-pools/{pool_id}/update`  | Replaces the same settings; supports an idempotency key.                                                |
| `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/dialing-pools/{pool_id}/preview` | Takes only `to` and previews selection without dialing or reserving capacity; needs `calls:read`.       |

## Rich messaging

These routes require an active workspace and access to the agent. Reads need `calls:read`.

| Route                                                                           | Behavior                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/messaging`                                           | Reports channel setup and remaining activation requirements.                                                                |
| `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/messaging/{channel}/conversations`                   | Lists stored conversations with `page` and `page_size`.                                                                     |
| `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/messaging/{channel}/conversations/{conversation_id}` | Reads a conversation belonging to this channel, agent and workspace.                                                        |
| `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/messaging/{channel}/messages`                       | Requires `calls:write` and send admission, then refuses with `409 owner_setup_required`. No message is queued or delivered. |

## Voices

`GET /v1/voices` lists every voice a session or a draft may name, with `production_eligible` (may carry a live call) and `available` (it can speak on this deployment right now). Each voice is named by a Sempera voice id (`id`, `voice_`, then letters and digits) and described by `name`, `description`, `language`, `source` (`built_in`, `library`, or the kind of a custom voice) and, for your workspace's own custom voices, `visibility: "private"`. The id is stable: the same voice has the same id on every read and every deployment, so it is safe to store. No voice payload names the speech engine or the engine's own id for the voice. Pass the id as `voice_id` on `POST /v1/sessions` to override the agent's published voice for one conversation, or set it as the draft's `voice.id` and publish. A raw voice id from before 2026-10-28 is still accepted wherever a voice is written; reads return only Sempera voice ids.

The optional `engine` filter (also accepted as `provider`) takes a Sempera engine alias returned by a runtime reading. Treat it as opaque. Older engine values remain accepted for compatibility. An invalid alias returns `400 validation_failed` with `reason: invalid_voice_id`; catalogue refusals use Sempera's wording and a stable reason, never the engine's own error text. The MCP `list_voices` tool lists the same Sempera voice identities without an engine argument.

Spec exports and frozen environment settings name speech engines and models by the same stable Sempera aliases. Existing saved agents, published versions and retained snapshots are not rewritten.

### Voice library and studio

A workspace keeps a shortlist of cleared Sempera voices. Every workspace member sees the whole library; sharing only controls a direct link to one entry. Private clones are never added or shared. Writes need the `agents:write` scope and an Operator role or above; the studio routes need an Owner.

| Route                                      | Scope          | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GET /v1/voices/library`                   | `agents:read`  | The workspace's saved voices: `{voices: [{id, voice_id, display_name, rating, shared, share_scope, share_path}]}`                                                                                      |
| `POST /v1/voices/library/add`              | `agents:write` | Save a cleared voice by its Sempera `voice_id`. Saving the same voice again returns the same entry. `201`                                                                                              |
| `GET /v1/voices/library/{entry_id}`        | `agents:read`  | One entry, only while it is shared. Otherwise `404`                                                                                                                                                    |
| `POST /v1/voices/library/{entry_id}/rate`  | `agents:write` | Set the workspace rating, a whole number from 1 to 5                                                                                                                                                   |
| `POST /v1/voices/library/{entry_id}/share` | `agents:write` | `{"enabled": true}` or `false` turns the direct entry link on or off                                                                                                                                   |
| `GET /v1/voices/library/{entry_id}/sample` | `agents:write` | Plays the voice with the workspace sample text as `audio/wav`. A sample can spend capacity, so it needs the write scope and the same Operator role as the writes and a workspace that is active        |
| `GET /v1/voices/studio`                    | `agents:read`  | Saved professional clone preparations, with a notice that training is not enabled                                                                                                                      |
| `POST /v1/voices/studio`                   | `agents:write` | Save preparation details: `display_name`, an active `consent_id` and `declared_audio_seconds` (600 to 7200). No recording is accepted, nothing is trained and the request stays `usable: false`. `201` |

## Models

`GET /v1/models` and `GET /v2/tts/models` (`GET /v2/tts/models/{id}` for one) list Sempera's own published, customer-eligible speech models: `scopes: models:read`. Values are Sempera's own model and voice names; no route ever names a supply account or an underlying engine. `GET /v2/models` is the same speech catalog, reshaped as the model list many client libraries expect (`{id, object: "model", created: 0, owned_by: "sempera", name, modality: "text-to-speech", capabilities: {encodings, sample_rates, containers, controls}}`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`), and needs no credential at all.

## Catalogue metadata

The App's agent-editor model catalogue also exposes the following display facts.
These fields are separate from the speech-only response shapes above, which stay
unchanged. The existing `0323` columns are the only stored estimate values;
`internal_mapping` is not a second estimate store. Derived currency, basis and
provenance are display metadata, never supplier charges or billing inputs.
A catalogue estimate cannot publish a model, connect supply or enable capacity.

| Field                    | Type                                                                                                                                                                                    | When unset                          |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `est_price_per_min`      | Nonnegative finite number or null, per call minute; currency is usable only with `price_currency` and `price_basis`                                                                     | `null`, show no price               |
| `est_first_reply_s`      | Nonnegative finite number or null, seconds to the first reply                                                                                                                           | `null`, show no latency estimate    |
| `currency`               | Always `CAD`: the currency of `price_per_minute_cad`                                                                                                                                    | `CAD`                               |
| `price_per_minute_cad`   | The Canadian-dollar display price per call minute: a stored `est_price_per_min` multiplied by the dated display rate below, or the derived estimate as it is (already Canadian dollars) | `null`, show no price               |
| `price_currency`         | `CAD` for a finance-derived display estimate; null when not established                                                                                                                 | `null`                              |
| `price_basis`            | `measured`, `assumed` or `unknown`; this derivation returns only `assumed` or `unknown`                                                                                                 | `unknown`, show no price            |
| `price_provenance`       | Derived evidence object or null, described below                                                                                                                                        | `null`                              |
| `first_reply_basis`      | Same basis vocabulary, independent of price; currently `unknown` because 0323 stores no measurement evidence                                                                            | `unknown`, show no latency estimate |
| `first_reply_provenance` | Measurement evidence or null; currently null                                                                                                                                            | `null`                              |
| `badges`                 | List of `recommended`, `smartest`, `fastest`, `included`                                                                                                                                | `[]`                                |
| `deprecated`             | Boolean                                                                                                                                                                                 | `false`                             |
| `retire_on`              | Date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format or null                                                                                                                                                     | `null`                              |
| `retire_note_url`        | HTTP or HTTPS URL without credentials, or null                                                                                                                                          | `null`                              |

### One stored source and a derived display estimate

Sempera staff maintain the 0323 columns. Workspace members cannot change them.
A stored `est_price_per_min` takes precedence, including an explicit zero, and
is returned unchanged. The column alone does not establish a currency or a
measurement basis, so it reads with null currency/provenance and `unknown`
basis. The same is true of a stored first-reply estimate: a number is not proof
that it was measured. `internal_mapping` estimate, currency, basis and badge
copies are ignored. Read-only evidence fields are derived by the server; an
operator request cannot certify them by sending those keys.

When the stored price is null, an existing published model with a joined supply
account identifying the hosted inference gateway may have a price derived from
that gateway's authoritative `list_price` inputs. A model id, a vendor-like name
or a provider claim in `internal_mapping` cannot establish that account identity.
No new published rows or supply accounts are created by a catalogue read.
Stored numbers are never overwritten with a derived value, so a null column can
produce a derived read without becoming a second saved estimate.

The calculation follows the finance generator's planning convention:

- Thinking: `(input tokens per call minute * USD per million input tokens +
  output tokens per call minute * USD per million output tokens) / 1,000,000`.
  Cached input is not assumed to be free or included; the planning scenario uses
  uncached input and no cached-token demand.
- Speaking: `characters per call minute * USD per million characters / 1,000,000`.
- Hearing: the USD rate per heard audio minute, assuming one heard minute per
  call minute. Multiple or unspecified catalogue languages use the explicit
  multilingual rate where the supplier prices one, not the cheaper single-language rate.

Token and character demand come from `01-company/cogs-model.json`, the same
inputs the finance generator uses. They are planning assumptions, not customer
usage measurements. A verified supplier rate does not turn an assumed usage
ratio into a measured call-minute cost. The existing test-traffic measurements
in finance are not silently substituted or attributed to other models.

`price_provenance` contains `source: finance_list_price`, `source_date` (the
supplier tariff snapshot date), `source_unit` (`million_tokens`,
`million_characters` or `minute`), `source_currency: USD`, the derived USD
`source_est_price_per_min`, named `assumptions` with value and unit, and `fx`.
It contains no supply id, credential, vendor model id or vendor pricing URL.
No unknown model or missing input becomes a zero. A genuine zero in the supplier
price table remains zero, but does not infer an `included` badge.

### Canadian-dollar display conversion boundary

The dated `usd_cad` input multiplies a stored estimate (into `price_per_minute_cad`); a derived estimate is computed in Canadian dollars with it, once,
in `06-tools/finance/build-finance-unit-economics.py`. That input identifies one
dated Bank of Canada FXUSDCAD observation; its date and rate are returned in `fx`. The
reader parses the literal input and evidence without executing the workbook
generator or fetching a live rate. `fx` carries `source` (the Bank of Canada
observation URL), `date` (the observation date, not today's date), `rate` and
`unit: CAD per USD`. Neither the planning stress rate nor an undated rate is a
substitute. This dated observation is not represented as a current FX quote.

If either finance file, its required units or its provenance cannot be read,
the derived value and currency are null and the basis is `unknown`. Deployments
that do not carry the finance generator therefore show no derived CAD estimate.
The server never bakes in a fallback rate and never relabels a USD amount as a
derived CAD one.

`list_price` still returns the identical USD supplier units and numeric values.
Supplier charges, credit pools, plan prices, settled usage, reserves, ledger
amounts and all billing inputs are unchanged. No catalogue evidence sets a plan,
opens paid service or enables runtime capacity. `included` is an explicit badge,
not an inference from a null or zero price. The existing `recommended` boolean
is independent of the badge. Deprecation and retirement notices do not disable a
model or replace a saved selection. Unavailable reference models remain unserved.

### What a client may rely on

Show a price only when `price_per_minute_cad` is a number. Show a latency only
when `first_reply_basis` is `measured` or `assumed`. A stored estimate reads with
`price_basis` `unknown` and a null `price_currency` (the column holds no currency
evidence), yet its Canadian-dollar display price is still served in
`price_per_minute_cad`, converted at the dated rate above. A derived estimate
already carries `price_currency` `CAD` and the basis `assumed`; it is not converted
a second time. Never label these planning estimates as measured. No migration or
new column is needed. No reference model is published or activated by a displayed
estimate.

## Stored prompts

`GET /v1/prompts` lists a workspace's saved prompts (`{"status": "success", "prompts": [...]}`); `GET /v1/prompts/{id}` reads one; `POST /v1/prompts` with `{"prompt": "...", "name": "..."}` (`name` optional) saves a new one, both wrapped the same way (`{"status": "success", "prompt": {"id", "prompt", "name", "last_updated"}}`). Reads need `prompts:read`; writes need `prompts:write`. A saved prompt is reused by hand, most often filling the `prompt` field on a call's own settings; nothing here runs at call time.

## Minting a Web voice session

```http
POST /v1/sessions
{"agent_id": "northwind-barbers", "channel": "web_voice", "end_user_id": "visitor-42", "language": "en"}
```

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.sempera.org/v1/sessions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"agent_id": "northwind-barbers", "channel": "web_voice", "end_user_id": "visitor-42", "language": "en"}'
```

```js
// On your server: the API key never reaches the browser.
const session = await fetch("https://api.sempera.org/v1/sessions", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SEMPERA_API_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ agent_id: "northwind-barbers", channel: "web_voice", end_user_id: "visitor-42", language: "en" }),
}).then((r) => r.json());
// Hand session.url and session.token to the browser.
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request(
    "https://api.sempera.org/v1/sessions",
    data=json.dumps({"agent_id": "northwind-barbers", "channel": "web_voice",
                     "end_user_id": "visitor-42", "language": "en"}).encode(),
    method="POST",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SEMPERA_API_KEY']}",
             "Content-Type": "application/json"},
)
with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as res:
    session = json.load(res)  # hand session["url"] and session["token"] to the browser
```

The response is `{"id", "transport", "url", "token", "expires_at", "voice", "speech_recognition"}`, where `transport` names the realtime media protocol the `url` and `token` are for (web-sdk.md). Hand `url` and `token` to the browser; the token is bound to that one room and expires in 30 minutes. Your API key never leaves your server. The request is refused with `409` when the agent has no published version, when the requested voice is not in the catalogue, or when the platform is at capacity (`503`). When the agent hears or speaks through a published Sempera model, `speech_recognition` or `voice` names it by its Sempera model id (`model_id`, repeated as `provider` and `model`), and the session runs that model; if the model cannot carry a call on this deployment, the request is refused with `409` and a sentence saying so, and no other model is used in its place. Otherwise the two legs name no engine and no model: `voice` carries the voice's Sempera id (`voice_id`) and name, and `speech_recognition` its language. A voice that cannot be used is refused in Sempera's words, and a `voice_id` that looks like a Sempera voice id but is not one is refused with `400` and `reason: invalid_voice_id`.

## What ran a session: `runtime_identity`

`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}` carries a `runtime_identity` block for a session recorded from 2026-10-29 on: one answer to "what heard, thought and spoke, did anything fall back, and was it a customer's conversation". Older sessions return `null`.

| Field                              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `legs.stt`, `legs.llm`, `legs.tts` | The hearing, thinking and speaking legs. Each has `engine`, `model` and `machine` (a category: `cloud` or `sempera`); `tts` also has `ended_on` (the engine the voice really ended on), `voice` (the Sempera voice id) and `language` when known |
| `fallbacks`                        | Handovers that happened: `llm` rows (`kind`, `from`, `to`) and `tts` rows (`from`, `to`, `reason` in Sempera's words). Empty lists mean nothing fell back                                                                                        |
| `worker`                           | `runtime` (`origin` when Sempera's own servers ran the call, `hosted` when a hosted call service ran it) and `transport`                                                                                                                         |
| `latency`                          | Timings the runtime measured: `greeting_at_s`, `first_reply_s`, `reply_turns`, and reply and voice percentiles                                                                                                                                   |
| `traffic`                          | `class` (`customer`, `demo`, `test` or `unrecorded`) and `company_overhead`, true for anything that is not a real caller on a real line                                                                                                          |
| `verified`                         | False when the stored block no longer matches its own integrity checksum. The checksum catches accidental corruption; it is not tamper evidence                                                                                                  |

Engines and models carry Sempera's sealed names (`engine_...`), or the Sempera model id when a leg ran a published Sempera model. The block never names a supplier, a host, a device or a failure's own text, and it prices nothing.

## Calls

A phone call is a Session with `channel: phone` and also a Call: `GET /v1/calls?agent_id=...`, `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}`. A Call adds the carrier's lifecycle: caller and called numbers, direction, duration, recording state and provider correlation ids (internal).

`POST /v1/calls` (`calls:write`, owner role, requires `Idempotency-Key`) places one outbound call through the App's guarded dispatcher. A missing gateway or unreadable outbound policy refuses the request; it never reports a ledger-only call as queued.

Outbound calls and text messaging are not enabled for the initial business release. A documented operation is not proof that a feature is enabled for every workspace.

### Rehearse with the workspace owner

An owner can rehearse an agent by calling the owner's own verified sign-in
phone, including while a Phone Plan pilot is active or the workspace is under
the launch restriction. Only verified primary phones of active members with
the Owner role in this workspace qualify. Other members, unverified phones,
service lines, business-line proofs and owners of another workspace do not.
Typing a number into a request does not verify it. Batches and SMS stay closed.

For this agent-mode rehearsal, no `agent_version` or `consent_basis` has to be
named. When no version or production environment is requested and no production
version is pinned, the newest published version is used, never a draft. An
existing production pin or an explicitly requested version is still respected.
Publish a version first if the agent has only a draft. Sempera records the
server-side consent basis as `owner_rehearsal` and audits the rehearsal with
only the destination's last four digits.

Calling hours still apply, with the same `outside_calling_hours` refusal and
no override. The do-not-contact list, idempotency key, call caps, gateway checks,
recording rules and the rule that `from` must be one of the agent's own answering numbers
or an answering number marked shared in the same workspace still apply.
Every other outbound call still needs its ordinary version pin and consent.

```http
POST /v1/calls
Idempotency-Key: owner-rehearsal-unique-intent
{"agent_id": "northwind-barbers", "to": "+141****0123"}
```

The example destination must match this workspace owner's verified phone.

### Other outbound calls

```http
POST /v1/calls
Idempotency-Key: appointment-reminder-unique-intent
{"agent_id": "northwind-barbers", "to": "+14165550123", "production": true,
 "message": "Your appointment reminder is ready.",
 "consent_basis": "This person asked Northwind Barbers to call them with appointment reminders.",
 "metadata": {"name": "Ada"}}
```

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.sempera.org/v1/calls \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sempera_sk_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: appointment-reminder-unique-intent" \
  -d '{"agent_id": "northwind-barbers", "to": "+14165550123", "production": true, "message": "Your appointment reminder is ready.", "consent_basis": "This person asked Northwind Barbers to call them with appointment reminders.", "metadata": {"name": "Ada"}}'
```

```js
const res = await fetch("https://api.sempera.org/v1/calls", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SEMPERA_API_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Idempotency-Key": "appointment-reminder-unique-intent",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    agent_id: "northwind-barbers",
    to: "+14165550123",
    production: true,
    message: "Your appointment reminder is ready.",
    consent_basis: "This person asked Northwind Barbers to call them with appointment reminders.",
    metadata: { name: "Ada" },
  }),
});
const call = await res.json();
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

body = {
    "agent_id": "northwind-barbers",
    "to": "+14165550123",
    "production": True,
    "message": "Your appointment reminder is ready.",
    "consent_basis": "This person asked Northwind Barbers to call them with appointment reminders.",
    "metadata": {"name": "Ada"},
}
req = urllib.request.Request(
    "https://api.sempera.org/v1/calls",
    data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
    method="POST",
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SEMPERA_API_KEY']}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Idempotency-Key": "appointment-reminder-unique-intent",
    },
)
with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as res:
    call = json.load(res)
```

| Field                                                                               | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agent_id`, `to` (alias `phone_number`)                                             | Required. `to` is E.164, or national digits with `country` (an ISO code the App's Send a call page lists)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `production` (alias `use_production`) or `agent_version` (alias `agent_version_id`) | By default, resolve the production deployment pin. An explicit version names a published id or number. That version's exact artifact must be installed; an older version is `400` on `agent_version`, not a silent fallback. No production pin is `400 AGENT_ENV_UNPINNED`. A publish that lands while the call is being placed or the call service is loading the version refuses rather than running different bytes              |
| `message` (aliases `opening`, `first_sentence`)                                     | The opening line after the required automated-call disclosure                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `consent_basis`                                                                     | Required sentence recording why this person opted in. Never invented by the API                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `from` (alias `from_number`)                                                        | The agent's own answering caller ID or a number marked `shared_outbound` in the same workspace. See Shared caller numbers below                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `metadata`                                                                          | Existing opening-template context: text values substituted into `{name}` and other placeholders. Not a per-call webhook payload. Values that the batch normalizer would truncate are refused                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `timezone`, `window`                                                                | Recipient calling hours. Defaults match the App: `America/Toronto`, `09:00-18:00`. Outside the window no call is placed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `precall_dtmf`                                                                      | Keys pressed after connection and before the employee speaks                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `name`                                                                              | Label in the outbound record, at most 80 characters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `settings`                                                                          | `voice_id`, `language`, `max_call_minutes`, `interruptions`, `interruptibility`, `interruption_threshold`, `acknowledgements`, `background_noise`, `noise_cancellation`, `voicemail`, `prompt`, `keywords`, `call_data`. JSON types are checked; unsupported keys and conflicting settings are `400`                                                                                                                                |
| `voice`, `language`, `task`, `max_duration`, `keywords`                             | Aliases for `settings.voice_id`, `.language`, `.prompt`, `.max_call_minutes`, `.keywords`. Duration is a whole number of minutes, 2 through 60, subject to the platform's stricter safety ceiling. With `mode` `prompt`, `task` is the whole conversation and is required. Otherwise the task supplements published rules. Keywords require a recognizer with per-call word-list support; otherwise `400` names `settings.keywords` |
| `mode`                                                                              | `agent` (default) or `prompt`. See Prompt mode below. `prompt_only` is not a field                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `block_interruptions`                                                               | Boolean: true blocks interruption, false allows it. Cannot be combined with interruption settings                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `background_track`                                                                  | Alias for `settings.background_noise`: `none`/`off`, `office`, `coffee_shop`, `restaurant`, `call_center`, `city_street`, `analog_phone`, `digital_phone`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `request_data`                                                                      | Alias for `settings.call_data`: a nonempty object of named text values. Never combine both spellings. Available throughout the call, separate from opening-template metadata                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

`call_data` is an object of up to 20 named text values for this conversation only. A key starts with a letter and contains only letters, digits and underscores, at most 40 characters; each value is at most 200 characters. The runtime binds these as call facts without changing the published agent. Do not send credentials in call data. The App's version picker lists the currently available published phone version and refuses an unavailable selection rather than silently replacing it. Scheduling in the App creates a deferred batch only when the scheduler is enabled; the public single-call API still places calls now.

Send only one spelling of an option, including across `settings` and top-level aliases. `voicemail` and `precall_dtmf_sequence` alias the existing voicemail and keypad settings. `webhook` selects a registered signed endpoint for this call; see webhooks.md. Any other option returns `400 validation_failed` naming its field, even when null or false. Recording overrides, transfers, per-call scheduling, retries, model selection and analysis overrides are refused until their runtime paths support them.

### Prompt mode

`mode: "prompt"` places one call from a prompt instead of the agent's conversation. `agent_id` is still required. It is the line the call goes out on (number, consent, do-not-contact, calling hours, caps and billing), not the conversation. A prompt is required: `task` or `settings.prompt`. `first_sentence` (alias of `message`) is the opening line after the automated-call disclosure. `voice` and `language` set the voice and language for this call. Omit `agent_version`, `production` and `environment`; sending any of them is `400`. `prompt_only` is not a field. Sending it is `400` and skips no check.

```http
POST /v1/calls
Idempotency-Key: friday-3pm-ada
{"agent_id": "northwind-barbers", "mode": "prompt", "phone_number": "+141****0123",
 "task": "Confirm Friday at 3pm. Ask whether that time still suits.",
 "first_sentence": "Hello, this is a quick call about Friday.",
 "voice": "voice_example", "language": "en",
 "consent_basis": "This person asked Northwind Barbers to call them about Friday."}
```

The same checks as an agent call still apply, and `mode` does not turn any of them off: the consent sentence, the idempotency key, calling hours, the do-not-contact list, outbound caps, an owned caller id, workspace screening, and billing. A missing prompt places nothing. The answer is `201` with `mode: "prompt"` and no `agent_version_id`. The line's instructions, tools, connections and knowledge are not used.

### Corrected transcripts

`POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/corrected-transcript` (`calls:write` and `calls:read`, owner role) imports corrected turns for a completed phone call: `source` (`human_review` or `recording_analysis`) and 1 to 5000 `segments`, each with ordered `start` and `end` seconds, a numeric `speaker`, a `speaker_label` (`caller`, `assistant` or `unknown`), `text` and a 0 to 1 `confidence`. `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}/corrected-transcript` (`calls:read`) reads it back. Every import reads as `provenance: owner_import`, `verified: false` and `confidence_kind: importer_reported`: `source` is what the importer said, and Sempera does not verify it or re-transcribe the call. The original transcript is unchanged, and the correction shares its retention and deletion. No correction yet is `409 correction_unavailable`; a deleted or expired transcript is `410`. A call recorded under Exclude from history, a call on an agent this key cannot see and a call that does not exist all answer the same `404`. Each import is audited with ids and counts, never the words.
## Active call controls

These routes require `calls:write`, the owner supervision permission and a
workspace-bound credential. An optional `agent_id` narrows the credential's
agent scope; it cannot widen it. Every request requires a nonempty `reason`
of at most 200 characters, recorded by the existing supervision audit trail.

- `POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/stop` ends one active phone call by its Sempera id.
- `POST /v1/calls/active/transfer` takes `call_id`, `to` (E.164) and `reason`.
  It uses the existing phone transfer path and preserves launch restrictions.
- `POST /v1/calls/active/stop` ends a snapshot of active phone calls within
  the authorized scope. Browser sessions and calls arriving afterward are
  not affected. The response has `data` (one outcome per call), `total` and
  `stopped`. Failures are reported individually, not hidden by aggregate success.
  A legacy room without a public call id can still be stopped in bulk; its
  result has `id: null` rather than exposing an internal room identifier.

One-call controls return `404` for missing, ended or out-of-scope calls.
An unreadable live roster returns `503`, not an empty success. A transport
failure can leave the outcome unknown: check active calls before retrying.
The console's Live now section offers owner-confirmed bulk stop for the
current agent, alongside its existing single-call stop and transfer controls.

## Questions about a finished call

`POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/analyze` takes `{"questions": ["What did the caller request?"]}`.
It requires `calls:read`, evaluation permission and a workspace-bound credential.
An optional `agent_id` query parameter narrows lookup. Each request reserves
one conversation-evaluation credit unit through the existing credit ledger.

Send 1 to 10 nonempty questions, each at most 500 characters. The call must
have a finished phone transcript. Missing or deleted transcripts are refused.
Transcripts over 60,000 characters are refused, never silently truncated.
Public outbound ids resolve to the call service's finished record of the call when that record
contains the public dispatch correlation; a dispatch checkpoint alone is not
a finished transcript.

The response includes `id`, `agent_id`, `object: call_analysis` and `answers`.
Each answer has `question`, `answer`, `evidence` and `status`. An answered
question must include a verbatim transcript quote. Missing information returns
`answer: null`, empty evidence and `status: unknown`. An unavailable evaluator
or invalid evidence returns a service error, never an invented answer.
Answers are returned without creating a new stored analysis record. The
conversation drawer offers the same questions form to members with evaluation
permission and explains the credit use before submission.


## Translate a finished call

`POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/translate` takes `{"target": "es"}`, a supported
language code. It requires `calls:read`, evaluation permission and a
workspace-bound credential. The optional `agent_id` query parameter narrows
the call lookup. The call must have a finished phone transcript. Each request
reserves one conversation-evaluation credit unit through the existing ledger.

The response includes `id`, `agent_id`, `object: call_translation`, `target`
and `lines`. Each line has `turn`, `side` (`caller` or `say`), the original
`text` and its `translation`. Every spoken line comes back in order, or the
request fails: a missing or empty translated line is a service error, never a
partial result. Results are returned without being stored. The conversation
drawer offers the same Translate action.


## Call batches

`POST /v2/batches/create` requires `calls:write`, owner outbound permission and
`Idempotency-Key`. Send `global` with the call's agent, production/version,
consent basis and supported call options, and `call_objects` containing
`phone_number`, optional `metadata` template context, `timezone` and
`precall_dtmf_sequence`. Alternatively supply `csv`, using the existing
recipient CSV columns. Invalid rows reject the request rather than disappearing.
Unknown per-recipient options are refused. Optional top-level fields are
`description`, `concurrency`, `max_attempts`, `retry_after_s`, `start_at`,
and `status_webhook` (an enabled signed endpoint registered in the workspace).

Creation persists and starts the batch, then advances one due pass through
the existing consent, do-not-contact, quota and call-cap gates. Future windows
and retries remain queued. The response includes the scheduler's actual state:
automatic continuation requires the existing deployment switch
`SEMPERA_OUTBOUND_SCHEDULER=1`; no API changes that switch or raises caps.
`POST /v2/batches/{batch_id}/run`, with an idempotency key, also advances due
recipients using that same checkpointed path.

`GET /v2/batches/list`, `GET /v2/batches/{batch_id}` and
`GET /v2/batches/{batch_id}/logs` return real persisted records and attempts.
Lists and logs support `take` and `skip`; logs also accept `direction=asc|desc`.
`POST /v2/batches/{batch_id}/stop` stops future recipients and retries, not
an already connected call. Repeating stop is safe. Every endpoint subscribed
to `batch.updated` receives signed events with `batch_id`, `state` and
`summary` after passes and lifecycle changes. A `status_webhook` must name an
endpoint subscribed to `batch.updated` (otherwise `400`), and receives each
event once. A failed notification never turns a placed batch into an error.
All resources are workspace and agent scoped.

The workspace Outbound list offers recorded attempts and owner-only Start,
Resume, Pause and Stop actions using the same guarded lifecycle as the agent's
Outbound page. Each action asks for confirmation; Stop requires a reason.
Starting or resuming makes the batch eligible for the scheduler, not proof
that a recipient was contacted. The list's `single_call` flag identifies
one-call checkpoints, which do not offer batch lifecycle actions. Attempts
show status and time without recipient numbers or provider messages.

The answer is `201` with a `call` object: `id` (`call-...`), `agent_id`, `channel` (`phone`), the dispatcher's real `status` (`answered` on connection), `direction` (`outbound`), `caller` and `to`, `agent_version_id`, `agent_version_number`, `batch_id`, `attempt` and `settings`. The request is checkpointed as a one-call batch before dialing. `GET /v1/calls/{id}` reads that dispatch record in the same workspace; this checkpoint is not a completed-call transcript or duration. Internal provider correlation ids never appear in the creation response. Before dialing, the number is checked against the workspace's do-not-contact list and outbound limits, and nobody is called when either stops it:

- A number on the do-not-contact list is refused with `501 capability_unavailable`, `reason` `do_not_contact` in the error and a message that says the number is on the list. The one-call batch is still recorded, with that person marked as blocked, and the refusal is audited.
- A reached limit answers `429 rate_limited` with `retry_after_s` in the error, and a limit that cannot be read answers `503 service_unavailable`. Nothing is recorded but the audit row (app-features.md).

The same request and key replay the successful response for 24 hours; a changed request is `409 idempotency_key_reused`. Concurrent requests and uncertain dispatches are `409 request_in_progress`. A timeout or process loss after dispatch begins does not release the reservation or reclaim it after two minutes. Reconcile the saved outbound attempt before making a new intent; do not use a new key to blindly retry an uncertain call.

## Phone numbers

`GET /v1/phone-numbers?agent_id=...` lists the numbers bound to an agent, with the carrier readback that proves where the number really points. `POST /v1/phone-numbers` with `{"agent_id", "number"}` binds a number to an agent (owner role, `phone_numbers:write`). Binding is what makes a real call storable at all: an unbound number's calls are never stored.

A developer does not need to know which telephony or voice platform Sempera runs to bind a number. Those are internal and may change.

### Shared caller numbers

A number can keep answering for agent A while other agents in the same workspace
use it as their outbound caller ID. This is API only; there is no console setting yet.
`shared_outbound` defaults to `false` and is returned on each number in
`GET /v1/phone-numbers?agent_id=...`.

To turn sharing on, send the existing bind route a number already held by the
named agent. This changes only the flag, without rebinding, reactivating or
changing the inbound route:

```http
POST /v1/phone-numbers
Idempotency-Key: share-northwind-line
{"agent_id": "northwind-barbers", "number": "+14165550101", "shared_outbound": true}
```

Use `false` to turn sharing off. The value must be a JSON boolean. This needs
`phone_numbers:write` and the same owner telephony permission as binding.
An unknown, released, other-agent or other-workspace number returns `404`.
Omitting the flag keeps the existing bind behavior. A request with the flag
cannot buy, attach, move or activate a number.

Any agent in that workspace may then name the answering, unreleased number in
`from` on `POST /v1/calls`, or in `global.from` on `POST /v2/batches/create`.
An unshared number still belongs only to its bound agent for outbound use.
The calling agent's workspace is derived from its stored binding, never from
request fields. Another workspace's number is never an allowed choice.

When `from` is omitted, the agent's own first answering number takes precedence.
With no own answering number, exactly one eligible shared number is selected.
Several shared choices return `400 validation_failed` on `from`, listing only
the choices in that workspace so the caller can name one. With no owned or shared
number, the existing gateway default behavior is unchanged. Dialing pools keep
their existing selection and number rules; this flag does not widen them.
A queued call's fixed caller ID is checked again before dispatch, so turning off
sharing or releasing a line removes that permission for future dispatches too.

Outbound caller ID is the only effect. People calling back still reach the one
agent the number is bound to. Sharing gives no access to that agent's transcripts,
recordings, SMS or configuration. Pending, released or orphaned numbers cannot
be shared caller IDs. Rebinding within the workspace keeps the flag on the same
number, but the line must be answering again before another agent can use it.
Deletion or a move to another workspace cannot leave the old workspace using it.

Buying, porting, inbound binding, SIP, consent, recording, calling hours,
do-not-contact screening, prices and billing are unchanged.


---

# API chat
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/api-chat.md

API chat sends a text message to an agent's published configuration. It is authenticated server-to-server access, not a public widget. It uses the existing typed runtime and its workspace privacy, model admission and daily message caps. Integration tools retain preview policy; enabling the channel is not approval for live integration writes.

Channel setup contacts no provider. Missing storage fails closed with `503 service_unavailable`.

## Channel configuration

GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/channels/api-chat requires agents:read and a workspace-bound credential able to read the agent.

PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id}/channels/api-chat requires agents:write and the owner role. Send exactly {"enabled":true} or {"enabled":false}. The response is read back from the same workspace's durable channel row. Writes are audited. A session write also requires the usual CSRF proof.

## Messages

POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/chat requires sessions:write and the operator or owner role. The channel must be enabled. Send {"message":"Hello"}. The message limit is 4,000 characters. Optional session_id continues the returned opaque chat handle. The workspace, agent and credential must all match the opening request. A wrong or expired handle returns 404, a simultaneous turn returns 409, and capacity or daily-message limits return 429. Disabled channels return 403 before inference. Provider or published-configuration unavailability is reported, never replaced with a simulated answer.

A successful response includes id, object (chat), agent_id, channel (api_chat), reply, ended, tool_policy (preview), expires_in_seconds and note. Responses are no-store. Conversation evidence remains in the existing typed conversation store, with its preview classification intact. API chat does not relabel these records as live phone calls.

In Conversations, these records carry the API chat channel and their last recorded activity time. Ordinary typed previews remain Web chat. The session read returns channel `api_chat` for API chat records (sessions-and-calls.md).

Sessions expire after 30 minutes idle. At most 20 are held per workspace and 200 per process, including openings in flight. A server restart ends open handles. Continue with the same credential; do not share a handle between users. API keys belong on your server and must never be embedded in browser JavaScript. No additional public ingress or provider activation is introduced.


---

# Text messages
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/sms.md

Outbound calls and text messaging are not enabled for the initial business release. A documented operation is not proof that a feature is enabled for every workspace.

A text sent to a number bound to an agent is stored on a two-way thread and answered by the agent, and a workspace owner can take a thread over in the App. Texting is turned on per agent in the Sempera App, as part of its phone setup (Send text messages), and it starts off. That one setting decides which numbers `GET /v1/sms/numbers` lists, whether the agent answers a text, and whether it sends one during or after a call: a text that reaches any bound number is always stored on its thread, and with texting off the agent never answers it and never texts anyone (below). Public sends use this same SMS path and its limits.

Routes answer in the compatibility envelope `{"data": ..., "errors": null}`. Phone numbers in a thread are masked to their last four digits, exactly as the owner sees them; full numbers never leave the thread.

## Public sends and handoff

Every write below requires `calls:write`, owner outbound permission and an
`Idempotency-Key`. Reads require `calls:read`. All routes check workspace
and agent scope, including cached idempotent responses. A customer database
is required for writes and individual conversation reads.

- `POST /v1/sms/send`: `agent_id`, `agent_number`, `user_number`,
  `agent_message` and `consent_basis` are required. The sender must be the
  agent's existing enabled SMS sender. Unsupported fields get a field-named
  400, not a silently ignored setting. Optional `timezone` (default
  `America/Toronto`) and `window` (`HH:MM-HH:MM`, default `09:00-18:00`) are
  the recipient's sending hours, as for calls. Outside them nothing is stored
  or sent and the answer is 409 with `reason: outside_sending_hours`.
  Whatever the window, no text is sent between 9 PM and 8 AM in the
  recipient's local time (the zone of the number's area code, else the
  workspace's own time zone): the send answers `status: refused` with
  `error: quiet_hours`, and nothing reaches the carrier.
- `POST /v1/sms/batch`: `global` defaults and `messages`, a list of 1 to 100
  objects overriding those defaults. This is bounded synchronous processing,
  not an uploaded-file workflow. Every row is validated before sending; the
  result contains a stable `batch_id` and each message's actual outcome. Each
  row is held to its own `timezone` and `window`; a row outside its hours is
  refused and not sent.
- `GET /v1/sms/conversations/{conversation_id}` returns the real thread and
  messages. `GET /v1/sms/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages` supports `take` (1 to 500, default 100) and `skip` (0 to 100000, default 0).
- `GET /v1/sms/conversations/{conversation_id}/policy` returns `thread`,
  `state`, `consent` (`not_opted_out`, `opted_out`, or `unreadable`),
  `do_not_contact`, `can_send`, a refusal `reason`, `max_body_chars`, and
  `sending_hours` (the default recipient timezone and window, and
  `human_reply_exempt: true`). Not opted out is not proof of opt-in. The
  send still requires a consent basis and rechecks the current guards.
- `POST /v1/sms/conversations/{conversation_id}/opt-out` with an empty object
  records a recipient's opt-out request against this thread's sender and
  returns the same policy shape. It is owner-only, scoped, audited and
  idempotent. It sends no confirmation text and stays available when launch
  eligibility disables sends. There is no owner restore action: only an
  inbound START, UNSTOP or YES restores texting. Suppression covers all sending
  numbers in that workspace; other recipients and workspaces are unchanged.
- `POST /v1/sms/conversations/{conversation_id}/handoff`,
  `POST /v1/sms/conversations/{conversation_id}/resume` and
  `POST /v1/sms/conversations/{conversation_id}/end` use the existing
  human/AI/ended state transitions. An ended thread cannot send or resume.
- `POST /v1/sms/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages`: `message`, `consent_basis`, optional `sender`
  (`human`, the default, or `agent`). A human must take over first; an agent
  cannot send while a human holds the thread. An `agent` reply obeys the same
  optional `timezone` and `window` as a send, and outside them nothing is
  stored or sent (409, `reason: outside_sending_hours`). A `human` reply in a
  live thread is exempt, and those two fields do not apply to it.

Sends obey launch eligibility, texting enablement, sender ownership, limits,
write policy, do-not-contact and durable opt-outs. No public send, batch row
or conversation reply goes to a verified, unreleased line on Sempera in any
workspace (403), which prevents two agents from answering each other without end. An
agent also answers at most 20 texts automatically per thread in 24 hours;
past that, the thread is flagged for a person. A pending message is
persisted before entering the send path; its outcome is recorded afterwards.
An uncertain send retains its idempotency reservation without stale takeover.
`sent` is provider acceptance, not proof of final delivery. Fixture mode says
`simulated` and `sent: false`. A refused or withheld send is recorded honestly
instead of reported as delivered. No credentials, full numbers or provider
error bodies appear in the results or audit events. No migration is required.

The App's inbox and reply composer use these same public writes with browser
session CSRF proof and an idempotency key. A legacy `/api/sms-handoff` reply
against the customer database is refused, so it cannot bypass the consent
basis, do-not-contact and send-policy checks. Its read/state controls and the
offline fixture contract remain available. Successful sends clear a thread's
unanswered marker only when no newer inbound message arrived during the send;
failed or withheld sends do not dismiss attention.

## Opt-out and help keywords

An inbound message containing only STOP, STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END or
QUIT, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace, opts the sender out of texts
from the workspace. Sempera confirms once per inbound message:
`You're unsubscribed from <business> texts. Reply START to resubscribe.`
Every later agent, campaign, tool or manual send is blocked until the person
texts START, UNSTOP or YES. These restore texting and send a confirmation.
YES restores only a person who is opted out; from anyone else it is an
ordinary message for the agent.
Replayed inbound messages do not send another confirmation or undo a newer
consent decision. Punctuation and extra words are not stripped when matching.

HELP and INFO return the business name and contact email or phone configured
in Settings > Business, without changing consent. If no contact is configured,
the business's receiving number is used. These keyword responses do not depend
on whether an agent or a person holds the conversation. When the carrier
reports that it already handled a keyword, Sempera does not double-reply.

## Numbers

`GET /v1/sms/numbers` (`phone_numbers:read`) lists the numbers the agents this credential can read text from: numbers bound to an agent whose phone setup turns texting on, less any the carrier reports cannot send texts.

Each row is `{"phone_number", "agent_id", "sms_config", "conversation_count"}`. `phone_number` is the bound number in E.164, `conversation_count` counts this workspace's text threads on that number, and `sms_config` is always null: Sempera keeps no per-number texting settings. `channel` defaults to `sms`; any other channel lists nothing, because Sempera offers no other messaging channel.

## Threads

`GET /v1/sms/conversations` (`calls:read`) lists text threads on the agents this credential can read.

| Parameter  | Rule                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agent_id` | One agent (`agentId` is accepted too); omit for every agent in scope                                      |
| `page`     | From 1 to 100000 (default 1)                                                                              |
| `pageSize` | 1 to 100 (default 50); `page_size` is accepted too                                                        |
| `sortDir`  | `desc` (default) or `asc`. Threads are ordered by when each thread was created, not by its latest message |

The answer carries `pagination` beside `data`: `{"currentPage", "pageSize", "totalItems", "totalPages"}`. Each thread reads:

| Field                                              | Meaning                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`, `agent_id`                                   | The thread and the agent answering it                                                     |
| `user_number`, `agent_number`                      | The texter's and the agent's numbers, last four digits only                               |
| `handoff`                                          | `ai` (the agent is answering), `human` (a person took it over) or `ended`                 |
| `is_active`                                        | False once `handoff` is `ended`                                                           |
| `message_count`, `last_message`, `last_message_at` | The thread so far                                                                         |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`                         | When the thread began; and the time of its last message, or `created_at` when it has none |
| `effective_channel`                                | Always `sms`                                                                              |

`variables`, `current_node_id`, `curr_pathway_id`, `pathway_tags`, `summary`, `citation_variables` and `disposition_tag` are always null: Sempera does not keep them for a text thread.

An invalid `page`, `pageSize` or `sortDir` answers `400` with `{"data": null, "errors": [{"error": "bad_request", "message"}]}`. An agent the credential cannot read answers `404`. A missing credential or scope gets the standard error envelope (errors-and-limits.md).

### Delivery states

When Sempera's servers have `SEMPERA_SMS_STATUS_CALLBACK_URL` set (the carrier-facing `/api/telephony/sms-status` address with its telephony token), every text the agent sends asks the carrier to report delivery there. The conversation drawer then shows each outbound text as `accepted` (the carrier took it), `sent` (handed to the phone network), `delivered` (the handset got it) or `not_delivered`. States only move forward, and a callback is matched to a message only inside the workspace that owns the sending number. An `undelivered` or `failed` state marks the thread not answered with a fixed sentence, never the carrier's own error text. Without the setting, texts stay `accepted`.

## Texts an agent sends on a call

Two texts leave during or after a call, both from the agent's own bound number: the in-call text tool (Send a text message, among the agent's tools), which texts the caller a confirmation, an address or a link they asked for, and the Send SMS voicemail action, which texts the message when an answering machine picks up an outbound call. Both obey the same Send text messages setting as an answer to an inbound text. With texting off, or with no phone setup yet:

- **The in-call text is refused and nothing is sent.** The agent is told that texting is off, so it can offer the details on the call instead. This holds in Test and Try it live as well as on a phone call.
- **The voicemail text is not sent.** The call's record says the text was not sent because texting is off, where it records every other reason a voicemail text did not go (no number of the agent's own, a limit reached, sending not allowed on this server). The outbound batch then treats the call as a machine that got no message.

## Who answers a text

An inbound text on a thread the agent holds (`handoff` is `ai`), on an agent whose texting is on, is answered by the agent itself: the same published version, with its own tools, knowledge and model, that answers the typed Test and the website chat. There is no separate texting prompt or model. The carrier is acknowledged at once and the answer is produced afterwards.

- **One conversation per thread.** The first text opens a conversation on the version published at that moment, and every later text on the thread is answered by that same conversation, so a publish in the middle changes nothing for it. The conversation ends after 30 minutes without a text, when the agent ends it, or when the service restarts; the next text opens a new one on whatever is published then, and it does not repeat the opening line. A service holds at most 200 conversations at once, and the least recently texted one ends first.
- **Texting off means the agent does not answer.** With texting off in the agent's phone setup, or with no phone setup yet, an inbound text is stored and shown on its thread like any other, the agent is not asked, and nothing is sent; the thread is flagged as not answered, with that reason, until a person replies or the agent answers a later text. Turned on, texting applies from the next text; a text stored while it was off is never answered later.
- **A person owns a thread they took over.** While `handoff` is `human` or `ended` nothing is asked of the agent. If a person takes a thread over while the agent is composing an answer, that answer is withheld and never sent.
- **One text.** An answer is the agent's own words with whitespace collapsed, cut to 480 characters at the end of a sentence, or at a word with an ellipsis.
- **Tools are write-protected.** An answer's tool calls run under the same protection the typed Test uses, so they do not write to a real system.
- **When the agent cannot answer, nothing is sent.** That covers an agent whose texting is off, an agent with no published version, a model that does not respond or cannot be bound, a turn that fails, a text with no words, and a number whose workspace does not own the agent. The reason is recorded on the caller's text, in one set sentence per kind of failure and never an engine's or a carrier's own error text, and the thread is flagged as not answered in the App until a person replies. There is no canned fallback reply: a fixed sentence sent from the business's own number would read like the agent answering. The API shows the thread's `handoff`; the reasons and the flag are in the App.
- **A texter left waiting needs attention.** An answer the carrier did not deliver leaves the texter waiting too. Each texter left waiting is one urgent item on the agent's Needs attention list, with the reason, however many texts they send before someone answers, and it counts toward the owner's attention alert when that is turned on. Its link opens the thread.
- **The thread in the App.** Opening a text conversation shows every message on the thread, oldest first: who sent it (the texter, the agent, or a person on the team), when, an answer that was not delivered, and why a text was not answered.


---

# Personal phone plan
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/phone-plan.md

Sempera Phone gives one workspace one number that its AI assistants can use: Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Grok Bot and Muse. It is separate from business plans. It carries no business onboarding, no managed support and no entitlement on them. See the [pricing page](https://sempera.org/pricing) for pricing.

The API and the MCP tools can use a plan. They cannot buy one. Signup and checkout belong on the owner's Billing > Phone plan page. Cancel happens there too, or through `POST /v1/phone-plan/cancel` with the owner's own workspace key (an assistant's phone credential cannot cancel). While `published` is false in the plan's configuration, no checkout starts and the page offers none. Connecting an assistant does not activate a plan, assign a number or publish an agent.

## Your first call

These steps need an active plan funded for real calls, an answering number and a published Sempera agent pinned to the plan. Under Billing > Phone plan, **Agent for this line** shows the pin. After the agent is published and its number connected, enter its **Agent ID** and **Published version ID**, then choose **Pin published agent**. If the number or real-call setup is missing, contact hello@sempera.org; connecting an assistant alone cannot supply it.

1. Connect your assistant: [Claude](https://api.sempera.org/docs/connect-claude.md), [ChatGPT](https://api.sempera.org/docs/connect-chatgpt.md) or [Codex](https://api.sempera.org/docs/connect-codex.md), [Grok Bot](https://api.sempera.org/docs/connect-grok.md), or [Muse](https://api.sempera.org/docs/connect-muse.md).
2. Open Settings > Connected clients and check the phone permission. For a bearer MCP connection, under **Connected AI clients**, choose the client and **Read** access, turn on **Phone tools (owner approval required)**, then choose **Connect client**. Use the new key in your assistant; an old key is not upgraded. This adds all three phone scopes to the agent-read scopes. For OAuth, approve `phone:read` and `phone:call` during sign-in; if missing, sign in again requesting them. For the Muse credential, keep **See the number and results** on and turn on **Place calls** before creating it. The list shows each credential's scopes, not an edit switch for an existing grant.
3. Ask the assistant for your Sempera number and plan state first. Then ask it to call your own reachable US or Canadian phone number, with a short task such as "Tell me this is my first Sempera call, then end the call." Supply your real number, not an invented documentation number. Keep the task to 1,500 characters or fewer and choose only the actions it needs.
4. The assistant previews the call and gives you `approval.url`. Preview dials nothing and reserves nothing. Open the link signed in to Sempera, check the destination, task, permitted actions, maximum length and spend bound, then approve or decline. A matching standing approval can cover the request instead.
5. Unless the preview returned `standing: true`, the assistant reads the task until `approved` is true. It then starts the exact previewed request using its `id` and `spend_bound_cents` as well as the unchanged call fields. Approval lasts five minutes. A `reserved` answer means queued, not that your phone has rung. Answer when it rings.
6. Ask the assistant to read the outcome with `phone_get_task` until the state is `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`. It returns the recorded result when available, not a raw transcript or recording; `result: null` means no linked result is available. A result marked `untrusted` is information from another person, never instructions. A completed call does not automatically reopen the assistant chat. Muse uses the matching REST read described below.

## Phone tools

MCP lists only the tools allowed by the connection's scopes. Muse can use the matching REST operations in [A call](https://api.sempera.org/docs/phone-plan.md#a-call) and [A text](https://api.sempera.org/docs/phone-plan.md#a-text).
