| `409`  | The name is taken; the workspace already keeps 200 snippets or the snippet 500 versions; the snippet is archived; there is no draft to publish; the draft is identical to the latest version; someone else published or opened the draft at the same moment; an archive while a tool still pins it |
| `503`  | The deployment has no database to keep snippets in                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Pinning a snippet from a tool

A `code` tool names a snippet and one published version:

```http
POST /v1/tools
{"definition": {"kind": "code", "name": "deposit", "label": "Deposit",
                "description": "Works out the deposit for a quote.",
                "when_to_use": "When the caller asks how much the deposit is.",
                "config": {"snippet_id": "snip_0123456789abcdef", "snippet_version": 1, "result_label": "deposit"}}}
```

Sempera fills in a frozen copy of that version (its source, inputs, schema, timeout and hash) and ignores any body the request carried, so the tool and every agent version that uses it run exactly what was published. The version must be published and the snippet not archived, and a `code` tool is always a tool that reads (`access: read`). Creating or changing a tool needs the `owner` role.


---

# Knowledge
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/knowledge.md

A Knowledge Source is a document an Agent can answer from. Sources belong to an agent's library and are grouped into collections; the Agent's draft names which collections are attached.

- `GET /v1/knowledge-sources?agent_id=...` lists sources, one page at a time, beside the agent's `collections` (each with whether it is attached and how it stands against the last build) and `pdf_supported` (whether a PDF upload can be read on this deployment).
- `POST /v1/knowledge-sources?agent_id=...` uploads one document as `multipart/form-data` (`file`, optional `collection`). Plain text, Markdown, CSV, saved web pages, Word documents and PDF are accepted (a PDF is read only where `pdf_supported` is true); the file is read at once and the response (`201`) is the source exactly as a read of it answers. If reading the library back fails after the file is saved, the upload still answers `201`, from the saved record, with `collections` and `attached` `null`; a read of the source a moment later fills them.
- `GET /v1/knowledge-sources/{id}?agent_id=...` reads one source.
- `POST /v1/knowledge-sources/{id}/reparse?agent_id=...` reads the stored file again and answers the `processing` state that re-read left (`parsed`, or `failed` with the reason).
- `DELETE /v1/knowledge-sources/{id}?agent_id=...` removes it from the library; the versions already built with it keep naming it.

A source carries `id`, `name`, `content_type` (the media type of what Sempera read the file as, which can differ from what the uploader claimed), `size_bytes`, `processing` (`state` is `queued`, `parsed` or `failed`, with `error`), `collections` (the ids of this agent's collections that hold it), `attached` (whether one of those collections is attached in the agent's draft) and `added_at` (when the file now on record was uploaded; an in-place edit through `PATCH /v1/knowledge/{id}/content` moves it). An id this agent's library does not hold, another agent's included, is `404 not_found` on every route. A source already removed reads as `404`, but `DELETE` and reparse answer it `409 conflict` with the reason ("that document was already removed"), and a library that cannot be read answers `DELETE` and reparse `409 conflict` with the reason, never `404`.

Processing state is tracked apart from the Agent's configuration: uploading never changes what the Agent says until the collection is attached in the draft and a version is published.

## Collections and agent attachments

Collections belong to an agent's library inside the credential's workspace.
They cannot reference another agent's collection or private documents, even
when both agents are in the same workspace. These routes require a
workspace-bound credential and access to the named agent. Reads need
`knowledge:read`; every write needs `knowledge:write` and the owner
configure-integration capability. Runtime, CI and read-only keys cannot write.
Paused workspaces cannot use the write routes.

- `GET /v1/knowledge-collections?agent_id=...` lists collections, including
  archived ones, with the usual `limit` and `cursor` pagination.
- `POST /v1/knowledge-collections?agent_id=...` creates a collection (201).
  Send `name` (nonblank, at most 80 characters), optional `description`
  (at most 400 characters), and optional `document_ids` (up to 200 library
  document ids). Omit `document_ids` to start empty. A duplicate active name
  returns `409 conflict`.
- `POST /v1/knowledge-collections/{collection_id}/documents?agent_id=...`
  takes `document_ids`, a nonempty array of up to 200 library document ids.
  It adds them without replacing existing members; repeated ids do not create
  duplicate memberships. Upload new files through the source upload route
  above, then pass the returned `id` here. Alternatively, upload with the
  multipart `collection` field set to the created collection id.
- `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/knowledge/collections` returns the effective draft
  `collection_ids` and its `revision`, including saved attachments when the
  draft has no attachment edit.
- `PUT /v1/agents/{agent_id}/knowledge/collections/{collection_id}` attaches
  one collection without dropping the others.
- `DELETE /v1/agents/{agent_id}/knowledge/collections/{collection_id}` detaches
  one collection without removing its documents or deleting the collection.
  Both PUT and DELETE take a JSON body with `expect_revision` from the latest
  attachment read or write. Repeating an attach or detach with the current
  revision is safe. A stale revision returns `409 conflict` with
  `reason: stale_draft` and the current `revision`; reload before retrying.

Collection writes return `object: knowledge_collection`, `agent_id`, `id`,
`name`, `description`, `documents`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and `archived_at`.
Attachment reads and writes return `object: agent_knowledge_collections`,
`agent_id`, `collection_ids`, `revision` and
`applies_to: next_published_version`.
Malformed bodies return `400 validation_failed`. Missing or foreign document
and collection ids return `404 not_found`, without disclosing their owner.
Removed documents, archived collections and unreadable library indexes return
`409 conflict` on collection membership writes. Archived or missing collections
already attached can still be detached. Attachment validation retains the
agent's existing knowledge and price-policy checks.

For example, using a fictional agent and an already uploaded library document:

```sh
curl -X POST 'https://api.sempera.org/v1/knowledge-collections?agent_id=example-agent' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEMPERA_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Visitor information"}'

curl -X POST 'https://api.sempera.org/v1/knowledge-collections/col-0123456789ab/documents?agent_id=example-agent' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEMPERA_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"document_ids":["doc-0123456789ab"]}'

curl 'https://api.sempera.org/v1/agents/example-agent/knowledge/collections' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEMPERA_API_KEY"

curl -X PUT 'https://api.sempera.org/v1/agents/example-agent/knowledge/collections/col-0123456789ab' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEMPERA_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"expect_revision":"REVISION_FROM_READ"}'

curl -X DELETE 'https://api.sempera.org/v1/agents/example-agent/knowledge/collections/col-0123456789ab' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEMPERA_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"expect_revision":"REVISION_FROM_ATTACH"}'
```

Replace the illustrative collection and document ids with the ids returned by
creation and upload. The generated TypeScript SDK exposes
`createKnowledgeCollection`, `addKnowledgeCollectionDocuments`,
`getAgentKnowledgeCollections`, `attachAgentKnowledgeCollection` and
`detachAgentKnowledgeCollection`; the Python SDK uses their snake_case names.
Creating, filling, attaching or detaching a collection never publishes an
agent or changes an existing built version. Publish separately through the
existing review flow before callers use a changed attachment or reading.

## Source testing

`PATCH /v1/knowledge-sources/{id}?agent_id=...` updates a text source with
`content` and optional `expect_revision` from the source's `raw.revision`.
Stale revisions return `409 conflict` with `current_revision` and do not
overwrite the newer reading. Editable kinds are plain text, Markdown, CSV and
saved HTML, not Word or PDF. This uses library document ids,
not the workspace UUIDs returned by the source testing context.

`POST /v1/knowledge/crawl` takes `agent_id`, `url` and optional `collection` to
read one public HTTPS page (201). To refresh, send `agent_id` and `source_id`
instead (200). This is a bounded single-page read, not a recursive site crawler.
The existing private-address, redirect, size, timeout and quota checks apply.
Both operations require `knowledge:write` and the configure-integration role.
Neither attaches a source or publishes an agent.

`POST /v1/knowledge/chat` exposes the source-testing contract below to API
clients and the console composer. It returns cited retrieved passages, not a
generated conversational answer. Each request is independent; it has no hidden
conversation history. Model-generated knowledge chat remains outside this contract.

`GET /v1/knowledge/testing-context?agent_id=...` requires `knowledge:read` and the read role capability in the selected workspace. It lists only sources visible to this credential (`sources`: id, name, parse status and owning agent), plus the requested agent's actual pathway nodes (`nodes`: id, label, prompt) and any `node_note`. Nodes are agent configuration: a credential without `agents:read` gets an empty `nodes` list and a note saying why. A foreign agent is not found. Loading a node in the console copies its recorded prompt into the composer; it does not simulate node execution, infer unrecorded per-node source bindings, or change source selection.

`POST /v1/knowledge/test` takes `agent_id`, `question`, and optional `source_ids` (at most 50 canonical source UUIDs from the context response). It requires `knowledge:write`, because a published test adds to the ask log, plus the read role and the same workspace/agent isolation. The question must be nonblank and at most 500 characters. Omitting `source_ids` or setting it to `null` searches the built version; an explicit empty array searches nothing. An explicit selection searches those sources' latest parsed readings, without attaching or publishing them. Foreign or missing sources return 404, malformed ids or invalid questions return 400, and sources that cannot be read or are not ready return 409. Paused workspaces retain the context read but cannot run the POST, following the neighboring action guard and partner entitlement policy.

The result is a deterministic local retrieval diagnostic: question, verdict, reason, scored passages with source attribution, and `mode` (`published` or `selected_sources`). The `published` mode records an ask in the existing knowledge log; a `selected_sources` test records nothing, so it cannot close a caller's open question or change coverage. It is not a model-generated answer or a live call, contacts no provider, and leaves the agent's draft and published artifacts unchanged.

## Console source inventory and query filters

`GET /v1/knowledge/sources` and `/v1/knowledge/sources/picker` accept `agent_id` to narrow the credential's workspace-visible sources. Parsed source inventory rows normally return `COMPLETED`. `STALE` means the owning agent's latest build (its compiled artifact and the verified knowledge snapshot it names) binds an older reading of that document; like `in_version_by` below, this is the latest build on disk, not proof of what is live. An unbuilt or unattached source alone is not evidence of staleness. Failed and processing rows retain `FAILED` and `PROCESSING`. Each row also carries its configured attachment state: `used_by` (`{"agent_id", "shared", "collections": [{"id", "name"}]}` per in-scope agent whose attached collection holds any reading of the source), `agent_count`, `used_by_state` (`complete`, `partial` or `unknown`), `used_by_basis` (`configured`: draft attachment, not the published build), `used_by_incomplete` and `used_by_unreadable` (in-scope agents whose configuration could not be read). `agent_count` is a number only when `used_by_state` is `complete`; otherwise it is null and an empty `used_by` does not mean unattached. `used_by_incomplete` lists the reasons: `unreadable` (an agent's configuration, or the store, could not be read), `outside_scope` (the source's workspace has agents beyond this credential) and `workspace_unknown` (the source is shared but its workspace could not be looked up; no other agent's reference is counted). Beside it, each row reports what agents' LATEST BUILT versions carry: `in_version_by` (same shape as `used_by`, from each in-scope agent's compiled artifact and the knowledge snapshot it names), `in_version_state` (`complete`, `partial` or `unknown`), `in_version_basis` (`latest_build`), `in_version_incomplete` (`unverified_version`, `outside_scope`, `workspace_unknown`, or `unreadable` when unknown) and `in_version_unverified` (every in-scope agent whose artifact or snapshot could not be read or does not match, including former siblings whose share was revoked or who left the workspace, since their last build may still carry the source). Each `used_by` row also carries `in_current_version` (`true`/`false`, or `null` when that agent's build is unverified). `latest_build` is the newest compiled artifact on disk, not proof of what is live: a build may still be going live, and an experiment may serve another saved version. An agent with no build carries nothing; a configuration change reaches `in_version_by` only after the next build. `in_version_state` is `complete` only when no in-scope agent's build is unverified.

`GET /v1/knowledge/queries` supports `source_id`, case-insensitive question search `q`, `status` (`all`, `answered`, `question_answered`, `question_open`), inclusive ISO 8601 `start_date` and `end_date`, `agent_id`, `take` (1 to 100), and `cursor`. These filters apply before pagination. Each row includes workspace-visible canonical `source_ids`; legacy asks without document attribution do not match a source filter. Foreign or missing source filters return 404. A question resolved by a later answer keeps that status even when the answer is outside the requested date window. The console sends local calendar-day boundaries as UTC instants.

The console's Export CSV downloads the currently filtered source inventory, with quoted cells and spreadsheet-formula escaping. Add sources at workspace level chooses the agent that owns the library, then uses the same upload, collection, web-page and Drive workflows as the agent page. Drive authorization and web fetching still require their configured owner permissions and network access; the console never claims a connection or import succeeded without the actual outcome.

## Recorded question lifecycle

`GET /v1/knowledge/queries` includes `question_id`, `question_revision`,
`question_state`, `answer` and `answer_source_id`. Question identity is bound to
the workspace, agent and normalized question text. Owner annotations are separate
from the retrieval diagnostic's `status`; the original query history is retained.

Both mutation routes require `knowledge:write` and the configure-integration role
capability. Read-only CI keys and runtime keys cannot use them. Send the recorded
`agent_id`, `question` text and current integer `revision` (`question_revision`
from the query row, initially 0). A stale revision returns `409 conflict`; an
invented question or a question outside the credential's workspace is not found.

- `PATCH /v1/knowledge/questions/{question_id}` takes `action`: `link`, `dismiss`
  or `delete`. Linking also requires a `source_id` naming a ready source in the
  workspace and marks the question resolved. Dismiss and delete update only the
  annotation, not the query history or source library. The response includes
  `id`, `state`, the new `revision` and `note`.
- `PUT /v1/knowledge/questions/{question_id}/answer` also takes `answer`, a
  nonblank string of at most 20,000 characters. It ingests the answer as a text
  source through the ordinary quota and credit checks, then marks the question
  resolved. The response also includes the canonical `source_id`. A failed
  ingestion does not resolve the question; retrying the same content reuses its
  source rather than creating another one.

Neither route changes published knowledge. Attach the source's collection and
publish a version before callers can use the answer. Question changes require
the workspace database; an unavailable database is not a successful save.

## Retrieval settings

`GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/knowledge/retrieval-settings` needs `knowledge:read` and answers `{settings, revision, applies_to, note}`. `PUT /v1/agents/{agent_id}/knowledge/retrieval-settings` needs `knowledge:write` and the `owner` role. It takes `settings` and `expect_revision`, the draft revision you read. `settings` is `{boost_columns, exclude_fields}`: up to 50 boost columns with weights from 1 to 20, and up to 50 excluded fields, none of which may also be boosted. Field names are labels in the extracted rows (1 to 64 characters, starting with an ASCII letter, followed by letters, digits, spaces, underscores or hyphens). Names are normalized to lowercase with spaces, underscores and hyphens collapsed to underscores; normalized names must be unique. A stale draft is `409 conflict`.

Save stages the settings in the agent draft, and they apply from the next published version. Exclusions drop labelled fields only, not unlabelled prose, and never delete source data.

## Pronunciation dictionaries

Shared pronunciation dictionaries belong to the workspace, not to one agent. Every route needs a credential bound to the workspace and a grant that covers every agent in it. Reads need `knowledge:read`; writes need `knowledge:write`.

- `GET /v1/pronunciation-dictionaries` answers `{dictionaries}`, sorted by name. Each dictionary is `{id, name, entries, version, updated_at}`, where `entries` is a list of `{word, say}` pairs.
- `POST /v1/pronunciation-dictionaries` takes `{name, entries}` and creates version 1 (201). A name is 1 to 120 characters on one line; a dictionary holds up to 1,000 pairs, each half 1 to 500 characters.
- `GET /v1/pronunciation-dictionaries/{dictionary_id}` answers `{dictionary}`.
- `POST /v1/pronunciation-dictionaries/{dictionary_id}` takes `{name, entries, expected_version}` and saves the next version. Every save is a new published version; a stale `expected_version` is `409 conflict`.
- `POST /v1/pronunciation-dictionaries/{dictionary_id}/delete` takes `{expected_version}` and answers `{ok: true}`.

An agent can attach up to three dictionaries from its own workspace in `pronunciation_dictionaries`, an ordered list of ids in its draft. Publish freezes the latest saved version of each dictionary into the agent version. Later dictionaries override earlier ones, and the agent's own pronunciation pairs win last. Editing or deleting a dictionary does not change an already published agent version. Shared dictionaries apply to voice calls using the published version, not to draft preview. Without the dictionary tables, the library routes answer `503 service_unavailable`, and draft attachment or publish returns an unavailable reason without applying the change. Send an empty list to detach the dictionaries.


---

# Tests and evals
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/tests-and-evals.md

## Tests

Tests are deterministic, scripted scenarios run before deployment on Sempera's own battery (the same one the Sempera App's Test tab runs).

- `POST /v1/tests` with `{"agent_id": "...", "scenarios": ["..."]}` (scenarios optional) starts a background run and answers `202` with a `test_run`.
- `GET /v1/tests/{id}` reports status and, when finished, the per-scenario verdicts and the evidence they wrote.
- `GET /v1/tests?agent_id=...` lists runs.

A published version's verification gates are on the Agent (`gates`). Tests never weaken those gates; they are the same battery under a simpler surface.

## Testbed

The Testbed takes one turn of a stored conversation and replays it against the step's current instruction and, if you give one, a candidate instruction, so you can see how a prompt change would have answered real callers before you make it. It is operator work under the same gate as standards: `run_local_test` on top of `tests:read` or `tests:write`, reads included. Nothing in the Testbed edits the agent; a candidate is returned as a proposal to apply as a reviewed change.

- `GET /v1/testbed/situation?agent_id=...&conversation_id=...&turn=...` answers the `testbed_situation` at that turn: the step the conversation stood on, the step's current instruction, the original reply and whether the step has an instruction to edit. Add `step` to name the step yourself. A text-message thread has no steps and answers `400`.
- `POST /v1/testbed/runs` starts a background run and answers `202` with a `testbed_run`. Body: `agent_id`, `conversation_id`, `turn`, optional `step`, optional `candidate_prompt` (up to 8000 characters), optional `expectations` (the same shape as a standard's) and optional `across_recent` (`true` for 5 situations, or a number from 1 to 20) to replay other recent conversations that stood on the same step. At most 20 expectations across all situations. One run per agent at a time: a simulation set or test battery already running answers `409`. Accepts `Idempotency-Key`.
- `GET /v1/testbed/runs/{run_id}?agent_id=...` reports the run: its `state`, the version it ran on, each situation with the original reply beside the current and candidate results, a `summary` and, when a candidate was given, the `proposal`.
- `POST /v1/testbed/standards` saves the situation at a turn as a standard and answers `201`. Body: `agent_id`, `conversation_id`, `turn`, optional `step`, `expectations` (1 to 8, as for any standard) and optional `name`. The new standard gates promotion like any other. Accepts `Idempotency-Key`.

Another workspace's agent or run is refused as not found. The turn must be a nonnegative integer. Invalid situations or candidate instructions answer `validation_failed`; a conflicting simulation or test run answers `conflict`. Saved standards retain the promotion gates described below.

## Synthetic concurrent runs

A synthetic concurrent run walks the built agent's own conversation graph with scripted routing decisions, several sessions at once, to show how the graph behaves under load. No model, voice, tool, webhook or business system is reached (`provider_calls` is always `0`), so a receipt proves graph behavior, not voice quality or model capacity. Same gate as the Testbed: `run_local_test` on top of `tests:write` to start and `tests:read` to read.

- `POST /v1/agent-testing/tornado` runs one and answers `201` with the finished `run`. Body: `agent_id`, `synthetic` (must be `true`), optional `concurrency` (1 to 4, default 1), optional `repeats` (1 to 100, default 1) and `scenarios`, each a `name` and 1 to 20 `turns` of `next_node`, `expected_node`, `condition_met` and `caller_said`. At most 100 sessions in total.
- `GET /v1/agent-testing/tornado/{run_id}?agent_id=...` reads a receipt again: `total`, `passed`, `failed`, the `service_version` it ran on, the `agent_sha256` of the build it walked and each session's `trace`.

Runs spend credits like simulations: one simulation attempt per session is held before any session starts, the sessions that completed are charged (`credited_sessions`) and a run that fails or is cancelled gives the hold back. Too few credits answers `402 credits_exhausted` with nothing started. A script naming a step the build does not have answers `validation_failed`, a workspace already running one, or a service already running two for other workspaces, answers `validation_failed` too, and an unreadable service version answers `503 service_unavailable`.

## Standards

A standard is a saved regression test for ONE step of an agent's conversation. It pins that step to a fixed situation (the caller's lines, and optionally the caller's number) and says what the step must do. It belongs to the agent and is the same standard on every version, so a change that breaks the step turns it red.

Standards are operator work: every route below needs the `run_local_test` capability (operator or owner) on top of the `tests:read` or `tests:write` scope, reads included, because step names and per-attempt conversations are internals an owner surface never shows. A standard or a run in another workspace answers exactly like one that does not exist.

- `GET /v1/standards?agent_id=...` lists the agent's standards. Each carries its `revision` (a short hash of what it asserts) and `last_result`, its newest result on the agent's CURRENT version, with `current: false` when the standard was edited after that result. The list also carries `version_number`, `blocks_promotion` and, when it is true, `gate`: the sentence that says which standards are red, stale or not yet run.
- `POST /v1/standards` saves one and answers `201`. Body: `agent_id`, `name`, `step` (the step it is bound to), `situation` (`script`: 1 to 12 caller lines of up to 400 characters; optional `caller_phone`), `expectations` (1 to 8), optional `repeats` (1 to 5, default 1) and `enabled` (default true). An agent holds at most 50 standards. Accepts `Idempotency-Key`.
- `PATCH /v1/standards/{standard_id}` changes one. The body is the whole standard again, with `agent_id`.
- `DELETE /v1/standards/{standard_id}?agent_id=...` deletes one.
- `POST /v1/standards/run` with `{"agent_id": "..."}` runs every enabled standard against the agent's current version as one background job and answers `202` with a `standards_run`. Add `standard_ids` to run only those (an unknown id answers `404`), and `timeout_s` to bound the run. A `version` other than the current one answers `409`: standards run on the current version only. One run holds at most 20 standards and 20 expectations; a larger agent names which to run. Accepts `Idempotency-Key`.
- `GET /v1/standards/runs?agent_id=...` lists the stored runs, newest first (the 30 most recent are kept), each with the version it ran on, its `state`, the standards it was asked for and a result per standard.

An expectation has a `kind`:

| `kind`             | Needs                                             | Passes when                                        |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `judged` (default) | `intent`: the rule, in words                      | a wording judge decides the step followed the rule |
| `says`             | `pattern`: a regular expression, case-insensitive | what the agent said at the step matches            |
| `never_says`       | `pattern`                                         | what the agent said at the step does not match     |
| `routes_to`        | `target`: a step name                             | the conversation goes on to that step              |
| `captures`         | `target`: a variable name                         | the step captures that variable                    |

`threshold` (above 0, at most 1, default 1) is the share of attempts that must meet the expectation; an attempt nobody could decide never counts as met. A standard's verdict is `passed`, `failed`, `unknown` (a rule nobody could decide), `error` (the attempt itself broke) or `incomplete` (the run stopped early). Only `passed` is green.

**The gate.** An agent with enabled standards cannot be approved or promoted on a version where any of them has not been run and passed. A result counts only for the version it ran on and the revision it ran as: edit a standard, or publish a new version, and it must run again. An agent with no enabled standards is not affected.

## Test analytics

- `GET /v1/test-analytics?agent_id=...` reads the stored runs and answers, per step of the conversation, how many attempts reached it (`visits`), how many failed there (`failures`), the `rate`, and whether there were enough attempts to trust it (`sufficient`). `weakest` is the step with the highest failure rate among those with enough attempts and at least one failure, or `null`.
- `days` (1 to 365, default 30) sets the window and `min_samples` (1 to 1000, default 5) the attempts a step needs. A value outside the range answers `400`; it is never clamped.
- `sources` says which runs were counted and which are not (evaluation runs and whole-scenario battery runs do not score individual steps). Same capability and scope as the standards reads.

## Evals

Evals judge completed conversations against owner-defined criteria with a language model. They are analytics, never a release authority.

- `POST /v1/evals` with `{"definition": {"name", "description", "kind": "binary"|"numeric", "instructions", "applies_to"}}`
- `GET /v1/evals`, `GET /v1/evals/{id}`, `PATCH /v1/evals/{id}` (with `revision`), `DELETE /v1/evals/{id}` (archive)
- `POST /v1/evals` and `PATCH` also take optional `pass_when` and `fail_when` (up to 1000 characters each), which the judge reads beside the instructions. Every agent named in `applies_to` must be one the caller can reach.
- `POST /v1/evals/run` with `{"agent_id": "..."}` scores the agent's completed conversations that are not yet scored. Add `eval_id` to run one criterion of this workspace, and/or `call_ids` (1 to 200) to score only those calls. A run with `eval_id` answers `503` when no judging model is reachable, rather than storing `unknown` verdicts.
- `GET /v1/evals/results?agent_id=...` reads the verdicts.
- `GET /v1/evals/agents` lists this workspace's criteria as judges, each with its pass/fail/unknown counts and latest run.
- `GET /v1/evals/test-cases` (optional `agent_id`) lists every call a judge can score (preview, simulator and scripted calls) with the verdicts this workspace's criteria gave it.
- `GET /v1/evals/runs` lists the evaluation runs `POST /v1/evals/run` recorded for this workspace's agents, newest first: status (`completed`, or `partial` when a judge returned unknown), pass rate (unknown excluded), the judges and agent versions covered, who started it and how long it took. It takes `agent_id`, `status`, `since` and `until` (days, `2026-10-29`) and the standard `limit` and `cursor`. A run before this existed has no record and is not listed.
- `GET /v1/evals/runs/{run_id}` returns one run with a result per call and judge (verdict, the judge's reasoning, whether it was scored in this run or carried over from an earlier verdict), how each result differs from the previous run of the same suite (the same agent and judges), and the body to start it again with `POST /v1/evals/run`. A run of another workspace answers `404`.
- `GET /v1/evals/agent-templates` lists the judge templates Sempera ships (`sempera/judge-templates.json`).
- `POST /v1/evals/quick-run` with `{"agent_id", "template_id", "limit"}` (limit 1 to 20, default 5) scores one template against the agent's most recent calls and saves nothing; `503` when no judging model is reachable.
- `GET /v1/evals/user-templates` lists this workspace's saved suites; `POST /v1/evals/user-templates` with `{"name", "agent_id", "template_ids"}` saves one.

These runs read the call transcript. Audio judges score only production calls, below.

The console's Runs page offers Create run to owners and operators. Choose a
workspace judge, then an agent it covers and the recorded calls to score.
This uses `POST /v1/evals/run?workspace=<id>` with explicit `agent_id`,
`eval_id` and `call_ids`, then opens the returned `run_id`. It never places a
phone call. If judging, admission or permissions refuse the request, the
dialog retains the refusal and no successful result is invented.
Recorded versions lists the selected agent's saved versions. These are not
replays: each evaluation result retains the version of the call it scored.

### Production-call judging

A judge can also be checked against stored production calls without saving a second copy of any call:

- `GET /v1/evals/{eval_id}/production-calls?agent_id=...` (`evals:read` and `calls:read`) lists up to 200 recent completed calls of an agent the judge covers, with `truncated` when more exist.
- `POST /v1/evals/{eval_id}/production-run` (`evals:write`, operator or owner) with `{"call_ids": [...]}` (1 to 10 completed calls) returns a verdict, score, rationale and reason per call. Nothing is saved and the result never satisfies a release gate.
- `POST /v1/evals/{eval_id}/align` (`evals:write`, owner) with `{"revision", "corrections": [{"call_id", "verdict": "pass"|"fail", "explanation"}]}` proposes new wording (transcript judges) or a new threshold (audio judges) at the revision you read. Nothing is saved; apply a proposal with `PATCH /v1/evals/{id}`.

Transcript judges read an imported corrected transcript when one exists, otherwise the original, and answer `503` when no independent judge is reachable. Audio judges (`mode: audio`) measure signal levels from the stored recording (16-bit PCM WAV, at most 30 minutes and 32 MiB): duration, energy, low-energy frames and clipping. They never infer meaning, and an unreadable, deleted, expired or altered recording is `unknown` with a reason. Each recording read is audited with ids only. A call recorded under Exclude from history is `404` and is never listed.

Both runs and alignment spend Eval credits: one per selected call is held before any work, a run is charged only for calls that received a pass or fail verdict, and a failed alignment is refunded. Too few credits is `402 credits_exhausted` and nothing is scored.

## Experiments

Experiments compare the published version of one agent with another verified,
already-published version of that same agent. They use the existing conversation
router and count the records it writes, not simulated traffic or projected results.

Reads require `agents:read`. Creating, updating and stopping require `agents:write`
and the owner-only `manage_experiments` capability. Every route is workspace and
agent scoped; an unknown or out-of-scope agent or experiment returns `404`.

- `GET /v2/agents/{uuid}/experiments` returns `data.experiments`, newest first.
- `POST /v2/agents/{uuid}/experiments` starts an experiment and returns `201` with
  `data.experiment`. Send `variant_version_id` and `traffic_percentage` (an integer
  from 1 through 99). Optional `name` is 1 to 80 characters, defaulting to
  `API experiment`. `variant_percent` is an alias for `traffic_percentage`; do not
  send both. The current published version, a draft, another agent's version, or a
  version without its verified saved artifact is refused.
- `GET /v2/agents/{uuid}/experiments/{experiment_id}` returns `data.experiment`,
  including its status, version identities, share and lifecycle timestamps.
- `PATCH /v2/agents/{uuid}/experiments/{experiment_id}` changes `name` and/or
  `traffic_percentage` (or its alias). A changed share applies to new conversations.
  The compared versions cannot be changed. A stopped experiment is immutable.
- `POST /v2/agents/{uuid}/experiments/{experiment_id}/stop` accepts no options and
  returns the stopped experiment. Repeating it is safe. New conversations return
  to baseline; conversations already open keep the version they started with.
- `GET /v2/agents/{uuid}/experiments/{experiment_id}/results` returns `data` containing
  `experiment`, `arms`, `reading`, `measure`, `dispositions`, `served_on` and
  `not_served`. Each arm has conversation and outcome counts, `reached_result`,
  `result_rate` (percent), `average_turns` and `flagged`. Empty arms have null rates
  and averages, not made-up scores. `reading` explains the sample size and uncertainty;
  it does not pick a winner. Disposition scores are not counted.

Only one experiment can run per agent (`409` for a second). A workspace can retain
up to 100 experiments. Creation starts immediately. Scheduling (`run_hours`,
`starts_at`, `ends_at`) and variant call quotas are not supported; these options
and other unknown fields are rejected with `400`, never silently ignored. Without
the customer database the routes return `503`, not an empty successful list.

The `served_on` and `not_served` fields describe the server's current channel
configuration. By default only new typed conversations in the App's Try it live
participate. Phone routing participates only where Sempera's existing pinned-version
call service is explicitly enabled; creating an experiment does not enable it. Calls
on a hosted call service, SMS and website chat do not participate. The public agent preview
endpoint does not opt into experiment assignment.

Publishing a new baseline suspends assignment until the experiment is stopped.
Assignment failures fall back to the published version. Experiments do not place
calls, send messages, promote versions, change consent, or bypass safety checks,
call caps or pinned-engine limits. The variant pins its prompt, model and settings;
tools and knowledge remain current. Results remain readable after stopping and
continue to reflect conversations that were already open.

## Production guardrails

Guardrails compiled into a published version are read on the Agent detail (`guardrails` in the App; the same rules the compiler enforces). Continuous monitoring of live behaviour is the evals road, run on a schedule from your side.


---

# Dispositions
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/dispositions.md

A disposition is a set of values you want Sempera to produce from every finished phone call of an agent: "did the caller book", "which service", "the callback number". You define the values, price the definition, publish it, and test it against real calls on your own schedule. From then on every new completed phone call runs the published version, and the result arrives on the `call.outcomes` webhook event (webhooks.md).

## Conventions

These are `/v2` compatibility routes (api-overview.md) under `/v2/agents/{agent_id}/dispositions`, where `{agent_id}` is the Sempera agent id. An agent the credential cannot read answers `404` like one that never existed.

| Work                                                                    | Scope          | Role                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------- |
| Reading                                                                 | `agents:read`  | any                   |
| Creating and editing drafts, estimating, extractors, corrections, align | `agents:write` | `operator` or `owner` |
| Starting a test run                                                     | `agents:write` | `operator` or `owner` |
| Publishing, disabling, deleting; publishing an extractor                | `agents:write` | `owner`               |

Answers use the compatibility envelope `{"data": ..., "errors": null}`. A refusal these routes make is `{"data": null, "errors": [{"error", "message"}]}` with `error` one of `BAD_REQUEST` (400), `NOT_FOUND` (404), `CONFLICT` (409), `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` (429) or `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (503). A missing credential, scope or role gets the standard error envelope (errors-and-limits.md). Every body field is checked; an unknown field is refused. `GET /v1/dispositions/` is a placeholder that always answers `403`; use the per-agent routes.

## Routes

| Route                                             | Notes                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET .../dispositions`                            | `{"dispositions": [...]}`, the live ones, oldest first                                                                     |
| `POST .../dispositions`                           | `{"key", "definition"}`. Starts `disabled` with its draft at revision 1. `201`                                             |
| `GET .../dispositions/{id}`                       | One disposition (a deleted one still reads)                                                                                |
| `DELETE .../dispositions/{id}`                    | Retire it. Idempotent; reads still answer, writes do not                                                                   |
| `GET .../dispositions/{id}/draft`                 | `{"dispositionId", "revision", "baseVersionId", "definition"}`                                                             |
| `PATCH .../dispositions/{id}/draft`               | `{"expectedDraftRevision", "definition"}` replaces the draft whole. `409` when someone saved first                         |
| `POST .../dispositions/{id}/estimates`            | Price the current draft per call. Stores nothing                                                                           |
| `POST .../dispositions/{id}/publish`              | `{"expectedDraftRevision", "estimateId", "acknowledgeEstimate"}`. Freezes the draft into a numbered version and enables it |
| `POST .../dispositions/{id}/disable`              | Stop it. Draft, versions and runs stay. No body                                                                            |
| `GET .../dispositions/{id}/versions`              | `{"versions", "nextCursor"}`, newest first, 25 a page; pass `beforeVersion` to page back                                   |
| `GET .../dispositions/{id}/versions/{version_id}` | One published version                                                                                                      |
| `GET .../dispositions/variable-catalog`           | The agent's variables and published Outcomes fields a value may read                                                       |

A disposition reads `id`, `agentId`, `key`, `state` (`enabled` or `disabled`), `publishedVersionId`, `publishedVersionNumber`, `draftRevision`, `draftValueCount`, `hasUnpublishedChanges`, `name`, `description`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `deletedAt`. `key` is 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and unique among the agent's live dispositions.

## The definition

```json
{"name": "Appointment outcome", "description": "Did the caller book?", "timing": "immediate",
 "values": [{"id": "44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444", "key": "booked", "label": "Booked",
             "schema": {"kind": "boolean"},
             "source": {"kind": "judge", "judgeId": "<eval criterion id>"}}],
 "transformation": {"version": 1, "root": {"kind": "object", "fields": {
     "booked": {"kind": "value", "valueId": "44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444"}}}},
 "postCallWebhook": {"mode": "emit_followup"}}
```

| Field                 | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`, `description` | Up to 120 and 2000 characters                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `timing`              | `immediate` or `within_24h`                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `values`              | Up to 50. Each is `{"id", "key", "label", "schema", "source"}`: `id` is a UUID you choose and keep, `key` follows the disposition key rule and is unique in the definition, `label` is up to 120 characters                               |
| `transformation`      | `{"version": 1, "root": <node>}` assembles the delivered payload. A node is `{"kind": "value", "valueId"}`, `{"kind": "literal", "value"}`, `{"kind": "object", "fields": {...}}` or `{"kind": "array", "items": [...]}` (up to 50 items) |
| `postCallWebhook`     | `{"mode": "emit_followup"}`: the result is sent as a follow-up event. `hold` is refused; the call's own webhook is never held back                                                                                                        |

A value `schema` has a `kind`: `boolean`, `string` (optional `format: "date-time"`), `number`, `enum` (`options`: 1 to 24 of `{"key", "label"}`), `array` (`items`, optional `minItems` and `maxItems` up to 1000) or `object` (`properties`, up to 64, and `required`). Any schema may carry a `description`. At most 8 levels, 200 nodes and 64 KB.

A value `source` says how the value is produced:

| `kind`                  | Shape                                   | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `judge`                 | `{"judgeId"}`                           | An eval criterion of this workspace (`GET /v1/evals`) that applies to this agent. The value's schema is `boolean`, or an `enum` whose keys are exactly `pass` and `fail`                                                                                    |
| `variable_extraction`   | `{"variableKey"}`                       | One of the agent's call variables, or a published Outcomes field named `outcomes.<key>`, whose value on a live call is the call's own captured outcome. The schema must match what the variable holds; the variable catalog lists each one's `outputSchema` |
| `structured_extraction` | `{"extractorId", "extractorVersionId"}` | Reads through a versioned extractor (below). The schema must equal the pinned version's `outputSchema` exactly. A draft may leave the version out; a test run needs one; publishing needs a published one                                                   |
| `custom_code`           |                                         | Refused: customer code does not run here yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

A source may add `"execution": {"reasoningEffort": "auto", "inputSourceIds": ["transcript"]}`. Sempera reads the call transcript with one setting, so any other effort or input source is refused.

## Estimate and publish

`POST .../estimates` answers a quote: `id`, `draftRevision`, `perValue` (each value's `executionPath`, token volumes and `usdPerCall`), `totalUsdPerCall` (`min`, `expected`, `max`) and the `assumptions` behind it. The `id` is a digest of exactly what would run and how it is priced. Publish with that `id` and the draft revision you estimated; if anything changed since, publish answers `409` and you estimate again. `acknowledgeEstimate: true` is required when the expected cost per call is above zero. Publishing needs at least one value, freezes a copy of every pinned extractor version and judge wording into the version (a later edit never changes a published version), enables the disposition, and answers the version: `id`, `versionNumber`, `definition`, `publishedAt`.

## On live calls

Every enabled disposition with a published version runs on every new completed phone call of the agent, after the call's outcomes are captured. Previews, typed tests and simulations never run it, and a version published after a call ended never runs on that call. The `call.outcomes` event then carries `dispositions`: one entry per disposition with its `status`, `values` and the `payload` the transformation assembled. When no model is reachable a value is stored `not_evaluated` rather than guessed; Sempera reads it again when a model is back, within a day of the call, and sends the event again.

## Test runs and corrections

| Route                                                          | Notes                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `POST .../dispositions/{id}/runs`                              | Start a run in the background. `201`; poll the run                                                                                        |
| `GET .../dispositions/{id}/runs`                               | `{"runs"}`, newest first; `limit` 1 to 100 (default 25)                                                                                   |
| `GET .../dispositions/{id}/runs/{run_id}`                      | Status, sizes, summary counts and the frozen definition                                                                                   |
| `GET .../dispositions/{id}/runs/{run_id}/rows`                 | One row per call: `status`, `results`, the latest `annotations` and, when complete, `payload`. `limit` 1 to 250 (default 50) and `offset` |
| `GET .../dispositions/{id}/runs/{run_id}/export-csv`           | The whole run as CSV                                                                                                                      |
| `PUT .../runs/{run_id}/cases/{call_id}/annotations/{value_id}` | Correct one value on one call. `201`                                                                                                      |
| `GET .../runs/{run_id}/cases/{call_id}/annotations/{value_id}` | That value's corrections, newest first (up to 50, `truncated` says if there are more)                                                     |
| `POST .../dispositions/{id}/runs/{run_id}/align`               | Proposed rewrites of each corrected value's instructions. Writes nothing                                                                  |

A run body is `{"target": "draft" | "published", "population": {...}, "executionSla": "realtime" | "queued"}`; `executionSla` defaults to `realtime` for a disposition whose timing is `immediate` and `queued` for `within_24h`. `population` may carry `environment`, which can only be `production`, and is `{"mode": "recent", "requestedSize": 1 to 250}` (default 20 of the agent's most recent finished calls with a transcript) or `{"mode": "calls", "callIds": [...]}` (1 to 250 ids). `{"replayRunId"}` instead replays a finished run over the same frozen definition and calls. At most 3 runs of one agent may be queued or running (`429`). A run's `status` is `queued`, `running`, `complete`, `partial` or `failed`; with no model reachable it fails and says so. Paging numbers on runs and rows are pulled into range rather than refused.

A correction is `{"state": "produced", "value": ..., "explanation": "..."}` or `{"state": "no_value", "explanation": "..."}`. The explanation is 40 to 4000 characters, the value must fit the value's frozen schema, and the run must be finished (`409` otherwise). Corrections are append-only revisions; the engine's own result is never changed.

Align takes an optional `{"valueIds": [...], "instructions": "..."}` (1 to 50 ids, up to 2000 characters) and answers `proposals` (each value's `changes`: `field`, `before`, `after`, `rationale`), `skipped` with a reason, and `truncatedCorrections`. It needs a finished run with at least one correction (`409 DISPOSITION_ALIGN_NOT_READY`), a reachable model (`503`), and allows 30 requests per workspace per hour (`429`). You apply a proposal yourself, or not.

## Extractors

An extractor is a reusable, versioned reader a `structured_extraction` value pins: a task prompt, an optional system prompt, the output schema and how it is read. It belongs to the workspace and is either workspace-wide or scoped to one agent; its `key` is unique in the workspace.

| Route                                                                  | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET .../dispositions/extractors`                                      | Every extractor this agent can use, most recently updated first                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `POST .../dispositions/extractors`                                     | `{"key", "name", "promptMd", "outputSchema", "inferenceConfig"}`, optional `description`, `systemPromptMd` and `scopedToAgent`. `201` with `{"extractor", "currentVersion"}`                                                                                                                                        |
| `GET .../dispositions/extractors/{extractor_id}`                       | `{"extractor", "currentVersion", "activeVersion"}`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `GET .../dispositions/extractors/{extractor_id}/versions/{version_id}` | One version                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `PATCH .../dispositions/extractors/{extractor_id}/draft`               | `{"expectedVersionId", "expectedDraftRevision", ...}` with any of `name`, `description`, `systemPromptMd`, `promptMd`, `outputSchema` and `inferenceConfig`; the fields you leave out keep their values. `key` and `scopedToAgent` are set at create and refused here as unknown fields. `409` when the draft moved |
| `POST .../dispositions/extractors/{extractor_id}/publish`              | `{"expectedVersionId", "expectedDraftRevision"}`. Answers `publishedVersion` and a fresh editable `currentVersion`                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `GET .../dispositions/extractor-catalog`                               | Extractors with a published version, with the `extractorVersionId` a value pins                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `GET .../dispositions/model-profile-catalog`                           | The reader profiles: one, `balanced`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

`promptMd` is required and up to 8000 characters and 8000 UTF-8 bytes, so text with many multi-byte characters is refused sooner; `systemPromptMd` has the same cap, and the pair is at most 16000 bytes. `outputSchema` follows the value schema rules. `inferenceConfig` is `{"contextSources": ["transcript"], "modelProfileKey": "balanced", "temperature": 0 to 2, "maxOutputTokens": 1 to 64000}`; only `contextSources` is required, and any other source, profile or `thinking` setting is refused. An extractor always has one editable version; publishing freezes it as the active version (its `state` reads `archived`, meaning frozen) and opens the next number for editing. A disposition that pinned an earlier version keeps it.


---

# Citation schemas
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/citation-schemas.md

A citation schema is the set of values an agent was published to capture from each call, frozen with that published version, together with how well each value has been captured. The values are the agent's **outcomes**: named facts such as "booked an appointment" or "service asked about", which Sempera reads from the transcript after each call together with the sentence that supports them (the `call.outcomes` webhook event carries them, webhooks.md). Dispositions (dispositions.md) are the per-call contract built on top of outcomes. Outcomes are defined on the agent's draft (the `outcomes` field of `PATCH /v1/agents/{id}/draft`, agents.md) and published with it.

The routes only read what already exists: they define nothing and write nothing.

| Route                                | Scope          | Notes                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/citation_schemas`           | `agents:read`  | Schemas, newest published version first within each agent                         |
| `GET /v1/citation_schemas/list`      | `agents:read`  | The same list at a second path                                                    |
| `POST /v1/citation_schemas/backfill` | `agents:write` | `{"agent_id"}`. Answers one agent's schemas and quality scores in a single object |

The list takes `agent_id` (also `client`) to narrow it to one agent, `limit` (1 to 200, default 50) and `cursor`, and answers `{"object": "list", "data": [...], "has_more", "next_cursor"}`. Without `agent_id` it covers every active agent the credential can read. A version that defined no outcomes has no schema and is not listed. An agent the credential cannot read is `404 not_found`.

## A schema

```json
{"id": "cit_northwind-barbers_4", "object": "citation_schema", "agent_id": "northwind-barbers", "version": 4,
 "source": "settings",
 "fields": [{"name": "booked", "type": "boolean", "description": "Booked an appointment"}],
 "quality": [{"version_number": 4, "key": "booked", "name": "Booked an appointment",
              "captured": 40, "found": 36, "corrected": 2, "accuracy": 95, "filled": 90}],
 "filled": 90, "created_at": "2026-09-28T09:15:42.386027Z"}
```

`version` is the agent's published version number and `created_at` is when that version was created. `source` is always `settings`. Each field's `name` is the outcome's key (the name a webhook receiver reads), `type` is `boolean`, `choice`, `text` or `number`, and `description` holds the outcome's display name, not its longer description.

`quality` has one row per outcome captured under that version. `captured` counts the calls where the outcome could be read, `found` the ones where a value with supporting text was found, and `corrected` the ones the owner marked wrong in the App. `filled` is `found` as a whole percentage of `captured`. `accuracy` is the whole percentage of captured values not corrected, so a value nobody has corrected counts as right: read it beside `captured`, because 100 over two calls means two calls. The schema's own `filled` is the average of its rows' `filled` values, rounded, and `null` when nothing was captured under that version.

## Backfill

`POST /v1/citation_schemas/backfill` needs `agents:write` and the `operator` or `owner` role, and answers `{"object": "citation_schema_backfill", "agent_id", "schemas", "quality"}`: the number of that agent's schemas and every quality row of them. Despite the name it changes nothing: it reads no new calls, scores nothing again and returns the figures the list route shows. An `agent_id` that is missing, unknown or not readable is `404 not_found`.


---

# Triage issues
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/triage.md

An issue is one problem your team is tracking with an agent: "callers asking for a colour correction are told we are closed". It carries a title, a severity and a category, a status on a small board, the calls that show the problem, attached files, links to other issues and an activity log.

Every issue belongs to one workspace. An issue id of another workspace answers `404` exactly like one that never existed. Reads need `evals:read`. Writes need `evals:write` and the `operator` or `owner` role; marking an issue viewed needs `evals:write` only.

These routes answer in the compatibility envelope: `{"data": ..., "errors": null}` on success and `{"data": null, "errors": [{"error", "message"}]}` on a refusal the route itself makes (`bad_request` 400, `not_found` 404, `conflict` 409). A missing credential, scope or role, a body that cannot be read as a JSON object, and an `agent_id` the credential cannot read (on create, and as the issues list filter) are refused with the standard error envelope (errors-and-limits.md). Lists page with `limit` and an opaque `next_cursor`; pass it back as `cursor` unchanged. The list routes refuse a query parameter they do not take; `GET /v1/triage/categories`, `GET /v1/triage/issues/{id}` and `GET .../affected` read none and ignore any you send. An issues list's cursor belongs to the filters and sort it was made with: change one between pages and the cursor is refused as invalid.

## Issues

| Route                             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/triage/issues`           | `{"items", "next_cursor"}`. `limit` 1 to 100 (default 50); `sort` `last_activity_at` (default), `created_at`, `severity` or `status`; `order` `desc` (default) or `asc`; filters `search` (title and description), `status`, `severity`, `category` (each may repeat), `owner_id`, `assignee_id`, `agent_id`, and `date_range` (`24h`, `7d`, `30d`, `90d`) over `date_field` (`last_activity_at` or `created_at`) |
| `POST /v1/triage/issues`          | Create. `201`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `GET /v1/triage/issues/{id}`      | One issue                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `PATCH /v1/triage/issues/{id}`    | Change `title`, `description`, `status`, `severity`, `category`, `owner_id` or `assignee_id`. A status change is written to the activity log                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `PUT /v1/triage/issues/{id}/view` | Mark the issue viewed by this credential: `{"issue_id", "last_viewed_at"}`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `GET /v1/triage/categories`       | Every category this workspace's issues use, as `{"items", "next_cursor"}` (one unpaged list, `next_cursor` always null). An item is `id`, `name`, `org_id` and `created_at`, the date it was first used                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

```http
POST /v1/triage/issues
{"title": "Beard trim callers told we are closed", "severity": "high", "category": "booking", "agent_id": "northwind-barbers"}
```

| Field                     | Rule                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`                   | Required, up to 200 characters                                                             |
| `severity`                | Required: `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`                                            |
| `category`                | Required free text, up to 64 characters. There is no fixed list                            |
| `description`             | Up to 10000 characters                                                                     |
| `status`                  | `backlog`, `todo` (default), `in_progress`, `in_review`, `done` or `closed`                |
| `source`                  | Create only: `manual` (default), `automated` or `client`                                   |
| `agent_id`                | Create only: an agent the credential can read                                              |
| `owner_id`, `assignee_id` | An active member of the workspace, or null                                                 |
| `resource_links`          | Create only: files to attach, each `{"resource_type": "file", "resource_id": "<file id>"}` |

An issue reads `id`, `triage_id` (`T-1001`, numbered per workspace), `number`, `org_id`, the fields above except `resource_links` (which is never returned), `author_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `last_activity_at`, `resource_count`, `flag_count`, `relation_count` and `has_unread_activity` (true until this credential marks the issue viewed, and again after any later activity). `external_link` and `latest_agent_session` are always null and `is_processing` is always false. Creating an issue is also the `issue.created` event your automation triggers can listen for (`GET /v1/automation/events`).

## Evidence: calls

| Route                                        | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/triage/issues/{id}/flags`           | The calls flagged onto the issue, newest first. `limit` 1 to 100 (default 50) and `cursor`                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `POST /v1/triage/issues/{id}/flags`          | `{"call_id", "type", "note"}`; `type` is `call` (default), `quality`, `routing` or `other`; `note` up to 2000 characters. `201`, or `409` when the call is already flagged on this issue                                                                       |
| `PUT /v1/triage/issues/{id}/calls/{call_id}` | Link a call whether or not it is already linked (the idempotent form)                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `GET /v1/triage/issues/{id}/affected`        | What the issue touches: `issue_id`, its `calls` and the `personas` of every agent involved. `pathways` is always empty and `skill_context` names only the issue's `agent_id`, its other fields being null: Sempera has no pathways, skills or dispatch routing |
| `GET /v1/triage/flag-types`                  | The flag types this workspace has used, with `usage_count`, `last_used_at` and the latest non-empty note as `description`. `limit` 1 to 100 and `cursor`                                                                                                       |

`call_id` names a conversation of an agent the credential can read; one it cannot read, or that does not exist, answers `404`. A flag reads `issue_id`, `call_id`, `agent_id`, `type`, `note`, `attached_by_id`, `org_id` and `created_at`.

## Files, comments, activity and links

| Route                                                   | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/triage/issues/{id}/resources`                  | Attached files, newest first; `limit` 1 to 100. `status` is `unavailable` once the credential can no longer see the file. No `cursor` yet                                                                                                                                                   |
| `POST /v1/triage/issues/{id}/resources`                 | `{"resource_type": "file", "resource_id": "<file id>"}`. `201`, or `200` with the existing attachment; `404` for a file id that is not one the credential can see                                                                                                                           |
| `POST /v1/triage/issues/{id}/comments`                  | `{"detail": "..."}`, up to 10000 characters. `201` with the activity entry                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `GET /v1/triage/issues/{id}/activity`                   | Comments, status changes, attached calls and link changes, newest first. `limit` 1 to 100 (default 100) and `cursor`                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `GET /v1/triage/issues/{id}/relations`                  | Links to and from the issue. Each item names the other issue (`related_issue_id`, `related_triage_id`, `related_title`), the `relation_type` and `direction` (`outgoing` when this issue stored it). `limit` 1 to 100 and `cursor`                                                          |
| `POST /v1/triage/issues/{id}/relations`                 | `{"related_issue_id", "relation_type"}` with `related_to`, `blocks` or `duplicate_of`. `201`; `404` when the related issue does not exist or belongs to another workspace; `409` when the same link exists (the reverse of a `related_to` is the same link); an issue cannot link to itself |
| `DELETE /v1/triage/issues/{id}/relations/{relation_id}` | Remove a link from either side. `204`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

File ids are the `id` values `GET /v1/files/list` returns (`knowledge:read`), the knowledge documents of the agents the credential can read. Only files can be attached today.


---

# Metric alerts
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/alerts.md

A metric alert rule says "tell me when X% of calls ...": when a share of an agent's recent calls crosses a threshold, Sempera records a trigger and notifies the people and systems the rule names. Every metric is computed from records Sempera already keeps; a metric Sempera does not record (cost, sentiment, audio quality) is not offered.

## Routes

| Route                           | Scope          | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GET /v1/alerts`                | `agents:read`  | This workspace's rules. `limit` (1 to 200, default 50), `page` (default 1), `sort` (`name`, `status`, `last_saved`, `last_triggered`; default `last_saved`), `direction` (`asc`, `desc`; default `desc`), `agent_id` or `agentId` (rules that cover one agent, every-agent rules included). A `limit` or `page` out of range (`page` is at most 100000) is refused with `400 validation_failed`, not clamped |
| `GET /v1/alerts/metrics`        | `agents:read`  | What a rule may measure and where it may notify                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `POST /v1/alerts`               | `agents:write` | Create a rule. `201`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `GET /v1/alerts/{id}`           | `agents:read`  | One rule and its trigger log, newest first                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `PATCH /v1/alerts/{id}`         | `agents:write` | Change any field; the fields you leave out keep their values. Optional `expected_updated_at` makes the save conditional (see Editing together)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `DELETE /v1/alerts/{id}`        | `agents:write` | Delete a rule and clear any alert it raised                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `POST /v1/alerts/{id}/evaluate` | `agents:write` | Run one evaluation of this rule now, the same pass the scheduler runs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `POST /v1/alerts/preview`       | `agents:write` | Replay an unsaved rule, sent as the body of a create, against past calls. The query parameter `hours` is `24` (default) or `168`. Nothing is saved and nobody is notified                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Writes need the `owner` role. A rule may only name agents the credential can reach, and a rule that names an agent the credential cannot read is left out of its list.
