Responses use the compatibility envelope `{"data": ..., "errors": null}`; the list is `{"data": {"alerts": [...], "pagination": {"limit", "page", "total", "total_pages"}}}`. Refusals use the standard error envelope (errors-and-limits.md).

## Editing together

To avoid overwriting another owner's edit, send the rule's `updated_at` back unchanged as `expected_updated_at` (a time with a zone):

```http
PATCH /v1/alerts/{id}
{"name": "Too many hand-offs", "expected_updated_at": "2026-10-31T15:00:00+00:00"}
```

The rule is saved only if it still has that `updated_at`. The check and save are one step, so of two saves carrying the same value exactly one is applied. Enabling or disabling a rule (`enabled`) takes the same guard.

If another owner saved first, the answer is `409 conflict` with `reason: "stale_alert"` and `updated_at`, the value now on file. Nothing is written or audited, and no firing state is cleared. Show the owner what changed, then either discard the edit or explicitly retry with `expected_updated_at` set to that newer `updated_at`. A value that is not a time with a zone (including null) is `400 validation_failed` with `field: "expected_updated_at"`. A rule of another workspace, or one deleted meanwhile, is `404 not_found` and names no `updated_at`.

Without the field a save behaves as before: the last save wins.

## A rule

```http
POST /v1/alerts
{"name": "Too many hand-offs",
 "metric": "handoffs",
 "thresholds": [{"percentage": 20, "severity": "warning"}, {"percentage": 40, "severity": "critical"}],
 "min_call_volume": 10,
 "lookback_minutes": 60,
 "agent_ids": "all",
 "notifications": [{"channel": "email", "to": "owner@example.com"}]}
```

| Field              | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`             | Required, up to 200 characters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `metric`           | One of the keys `GET /v1/alerts/metrics` lists: `failed_calls`, `slow_replies`, `handoffs`, `unfinished_requests`, `judge_failures`, `long_calls`                                                                                                                                     |
| `cutoff`           | Seconds, only for `slow_replies` (0.5 to 30, default 2) and `long_calls` (30 to 7200, default 300)                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `thresholds`       | 1 to 3 of `{"percentage", "severity"}`. Percentage is more than 0 and at most 100; severity is `info`, `warning` or `critical`. No two share a percentage or a severity, and a higher percentage carries a higher severity                                                            |
| `min_call_volume`  | 1 to 100000. Below it nothing fires: one failure in one call is not a 100% failure rate                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `lookback_minutes` | `10`, `30`, `60`, `180` or `1440`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `agent_ids`        | `"all"` (default) or a non-empty list of agent ids                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `notifications`    | Up to 10 of `{"channel": "email", "to": "<address>"}` or `{"channel": "webhook", "to": "<webhook endpoint id>"}`. A webhook target is one of this workspace's own enabled endpoints (webhooks.md), never a bare URL                                                                   |
| `tools`            | At most one of `{"id", "input"}`: `id` is an `api_request` tool's `tool_id` as `GET /v1/tools` shows it; `input` is up to 20 named values, each up to 2000 characters, which may reference the alert's fields as `{{name}}` (`GET /v1/alerts/metrics` lists them as `tool_variables`) |
| `enabled`          | `true` (default) or `false`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

A rule read adds `id`, `object: "alert"`, `org_id`, `metric_label`, `category`, `severity` (the highest threshold's), `lookback_window` (the same number as `lookback_minutes`), `status` (`ok`, `triggered` or `disabled`), `firing_severity`, `last_saved` (also `updated_at`), `last_triggered`, `last_evaluated` and `created_at`. A detail read adds `triggers`, newest first and at most 100: each has `id`, `kind` (`fired`, `worsened` or `recovered`), `severity`, `value_pct`, `threshold_pct`, `call_volume`, `matched`, the window, `agent_ids`, `notified`, `notify_failed`, `notify_error` and `at`.

## How a rule fires

Every evaluation measures the metric over the lookback window for the agents in scope. When the call volume reaches the minimum and the share is at or above a threshold, the rule fires once, records a trigger, raises an alert in the Sempera App and notifies each target. It records a second trigger only when it worsens to a higher severity, and a recovery when an evaluation finds it clear; a recovery notifies the same targets with a "Cleared" message. Changing a rule's definition, or disabling it, clears its firing state.

Webhook targets receive the signed `metric_alert.triggered` event (webhooks.md); this event is delivered only to the endpoints a rule names, never by subscription. A rule's tool runs through the same road, test mode and write rules as a tool step inside a call. A trigger's `notified` counts the targets that accepted delivery. A firing is also the `alert.fired` event your automation triggers can listen for (`GET /v1/automation/events`).

The App's Add notification menu offers Email and Webhook from the channel
catalogue, plus the separate Tool slot. A webhook selects an existing enabled
workspace endpoint, never a new URL. Ten email/webhook destinations do not
consume the tool slot. Phone-call notifications are not available.

Fixture email records a local test message but does not count as delivery:
`notified` stays zero for that target, with `notify_failed: true` and
`notify_error: email_environment_fixture`. Provider acceptance counts as
delivery, not proof that a person read it. Tool fixtures likewise do not count
as delivery.

`POST /v1/alerts/{id}/evaluate` answers `{"evaluation", "alert", "triggers"}`. `evaluation.action` is `fired`, `worsened`, `recovered` or `none`, beside `value_pct`, `matched`, `call_volume`, `enough_volume`, `severity`, `threshold_pct`, `agent_ids` and the window. `DELETE` answers `{"id", "deleted": true}`.

`POST /v1/alerts/preview` takes the same body as `POST /v1/alerts`, checks it the same way, and replays it once a minute over the last `hours`. It saves no rule, records no trigger and sends nothing, so `notifications_sent` is always `0`. It reads only the agents both the rule and the credential can reach, and any other `hours` is `400 validation_failed`. It answers `{"hours", "from", "to", "triggered", "evaluations", "interval_minutes", "windows", "call_volume", "notifications_sent"}`: `triggered` counts each rise into a firing or higher severity, and `windows` holds the hourly measurements plus every change of severity.

The call metrics read preview and simulator conversation records, the same records Attention reads in the App; phone calls kept only as call-log rows are not counted. `judge_failures` counts the Fail verdicts of this workspace's own judges, and its volume is the number of verdicts in the window.

## Refusals

| Status                    | When                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400 validation_failed`   | A field breaks a rule above, including a webhook target or tool that is not this workspace's own                                                                                                   |
| `404 not_found`           | No such rule in this workspace, a rule naming an agent the credential cannot read, or a body naming an agent it cannot reach                                                                       |
| `409 conflict`            | Evaluating a disabled rule                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `409 conflict`            | A conditional edit is stale: `reason: stale_alert` and the current `updated_at`; nothing is saved                                                                                                  |
| `503 service_unavailable` | The deployment has no customer database to keep rules in. Only writes and `GET /v1/alerts/{id}` refuse this way: `GET /v1/alerts` answers an empty list and `GET /v1/alerts/metrics` still answers |


---

# Automations
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/automations.md

A trigger says "when this event happens, and these conditions hold, do one thing". It listens for one event Sempera emits, tests the event against zero or more conditions, and runs one action aimed at a destination the workspace has already approved. Every run is recorded, including the ones a condition skipped.

A trigger covers the whole workspace or the agents it names; an event about an agent it does not cover leaves no run. Every trigger belongs to one workspace. A trigger or run of another workspace answers `404` exactly like one that never existed, and a trigger that names an agent the credential cannot read is not listed to it.

Reads need `agents:read`. Writes need `agents:write` and the `owner` role, because a trigger sends the business's call data to another system. A dry run needs `agents:write` only. Success answers use the compatibility envelope `{"data": ..., "errors": null}`; refusals use the standard error envelope (errors-and-limits.md). Without a customer database, the two list routes answer empty lists, the events route still answers, and every other route answers `503 service_unavailable`.

## Routes

| Route                                         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GET /v1/automation/events`                   | The events, their fields and the operators each field type offers, the actions offered and the actions refused                                                                                                           |
| `GET /v1/automation/triggers`                 | `{"triggers", "total", "limit", "offset"}`. `limit` 1 to 200 (default 50), `offset` from 0, `sort` `recent` (default), `runs`, `active` or `name`, and the filters `agent_id` (triggers covering that agent) and `event` |
| `POST /v1/automation/triggers`                | Create. `201`. `POST /v1/automation/pipelines` creates the same record; call one of them, not both                                                                                                                       |
| `GET /v1/automation/triggers/{id}`            | One trigger                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `PATCH /v1/automation/triggers/{id}`          | A partial edit: fields you leave out keep their values. `status` (`active` or `paused`) or `enabled` pauses and resumes. Optional `expected_updated_at` makes the save conditional (see Editing together)                |
| `DELETE /v1/automation/triggers/{id}`         | `{"id", "deleted": true}`                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `POST /v1/automation/triggers/{id}/test`      | A dry run. Nothing is sent and nothing is recorded, and a paused trigger can be tested                                                                                                                                   |
| `GET /v1/automation/triggers/{id}/executions` | One trigger's runs, newest first. `limit`, `offset` and `status`                                                                                                                                                         |
| `GET /v1/automation/executions`               | Every run the credential may read, newest first. `limit`, `offset`, `status` and `trigger_id`                                                                                                                            |
| `GET /v1/automation/executions/{id}`          | One run                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `POST /v1/automation/executions/{id}/retry`   | Send a failed or stalled webhook or tool run again, once                                                                                                                                                                 |

A `limit`, `offset`, `sort`, `event` or `status` outside the values above is refused with `400 validation_failed`, not clamped.

## Editing together

Two owners can open the same trigger and both save. Without a guard the later save wins and the earlier one is lost without a word. To avoid that, send the `updated_at` you read back with the edit:

```http
PATCH /v1/automation/triggers/{id}
{"name": "Booked calls", "expected_updated_at": "2026-10-23T15:00:00+00:00"}
```

`expected_updated_at` is the trigger's `updated_at`, sent back unchanged (a time with a zone). The trigger is saved only if it still has that `updated_at`, and the check and the save are one step, so of two saves that carry the same value exactly one is applied. A pause or a resume (`enabled` or `status`) is an edit and takes the same field.

If another owner saved first, the answer is `409 conflict` with `reason: "stale_trigger"` and `updated_at`, the value now on file. Nothing is written and nothing is recorded in the audit log. Show the owner what changed, then either discard the edit or send it again with `expected_updated_at` set to that `updated_at` to save it over the newer version. A value that is not a time with a zone is `400 validation_failed` with `field: "expected_updated_at"`. A trigger of another workspace, or one deleted meanwhile, is `404 not_found` and names no `updated_at`.

Without the field a save behaves as it always did: the last save wins.

## A trigger

```http
POST /v1/automation/triggers
{"name": "Long calls to the ops channel",
 "event": "call.completed",
 "conditions": [{"field": "duration_s", "operator": "greater_than", "value": 600}],
 "action": {"kind": "webhook", "endpoint_id": "<a webhook endpoint id>"},
 "agent_ids": ["northwind-barbers"],
 "enabled": true}
```

| Field        | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | Required, up to 200 characters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `event`      | Required: one key of the table below                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `conditions` | Up to 20 of `{"field", "operator", "value"}`; every one must hold. `field` is one of the event's fields, `operator` one that field's type offers, and `value` matches the field's type (text up to 500 characters). `is_empty` and `is_not_empty` take no value |
| `action`     | Required, one of the actions below                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `agent_ids`  | `"all"` (default) or 1 to 50 agent ids                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `enabled`    | `true` or `false`. A trigger created without it starts paused                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

A trigger reads `id`, `object: "automation_trigger"`, `org_id`, `name`, `enabled`, `status`, `event`, `event_name`, `conditions`, `action`, `agent_ids`, `run_count`, `last_run_at`, `created_at` and `updated_at`.

| Type                         | Operators                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Text                         | `equals`, `not_equals`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `is_empty`, `is_not_empty`; text compares without regard to case |
| Number                       | `equals`, `not_equals`, `greater_than`, `less_than`, `is_empty`, `is_not_empty`                                      |
| Yes or no                    | `equals`, `not_equals`                                                                                               |
| List of text                 | `contains`, `not_contains`, `is_empty`, `is_not_empty`                                                               |
| Object, or a list of objects | `is_empty`, `is_not_empty`                                                                                           |

## Events

| Event                              | Fired when                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Fields                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `call.completed`                   | A phone call ended and its record was stored                                                                                                                                                                                             | `call_id`, `agent_id`, `direction`, `duration_s` (number), `outcome`, `summary`, `recording_stored` (yes or no), `turns` (number)                                        |
| `call.failed`                      | An outbound call was not placed. A number on the do-not-contact list is a deliberate skip, not a failure                                                                                                                                 | `agent_id`, `batch_id`, `batch_name`, `attempt` (number), `reason`, `will_retry` (yes or no), `number_last4`                                                             |
| `knowledge.gap_detected`           | The agent searched its knowledge and nothing answered the caller                                                                                                                                                                         | `agent_id`, `call_id`, `question`, `search_query`, `coverage` (number, 0 to 1), `documents` (list of text)                                                               |
| `alert.fired`                      | A metric alert rule fired or worsened (alerts.md)                                                                                                                                                                                        | `alert_id`, `alert_name`, `metric`, `severity`, `kind`, `value_pct`, `threshold_pct`, `call_volume`, `matched`, `lookback_minutes` (numbers), `agent_ids` (list of text) |
| `issue.created`                    | A triage issue was opened (triage.md)                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `issue_id`, `number` (number), `title`, `severity`, `category`, `status`, `source`, `agent_id`                                                                           |
| `agent.published`                  | A version of an agent was published                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `agent_id`, `version` (object)                                                                                                                                           |
| `call.outcomes`                    | Dispositions were read from a finished call (dispositions.md)                                                                                                                                                                            | `agent_id`, `call_id`, `version_number` (number), `outcomes` (list of objects)                                                                                           |
| `tool.success`, `tool.failure`     | An attached conversation tool finished or was refused on a live phone call. A Test panel run, a simulation, a typed preview and API chat never fire them. Fixture results carry `environment: FIXTURE`; they are not live system success | `agent_id`, `call_id`, `tool`, `status` (number or null), `environment`                                                                                                  |
| `call.post_webhook`                | A completed call was recorded and its post-call event is ready, not proof of webhook delivery                                                                                                                                            | `agent_id`, `call_id`, `direction`                                                                                                                                       |
| `call.started`                     | A phone runtime session reached its opening                                                                                                                                                                                              | `agent_id`, `call_id`, `direction`                                                                                                                                       |
| `eval.completed`                   | An existing evaluation run announced completion or failure                                                                                                                                                                               | `agent_id`, `test_id`, `status`, `outcome`                                                                                                                               |
| `sms.received`, `sms.post_webhook` | An authenticated, non-replayed inbound SMS webhook was stored                                                                                                                                                                            | `agent_id`, `thread_id`, `message_id`                                                                                                                                    |
| `call.voicemail`                   | The outbound runtime classified an answering machine                                                                                                                                                                                     | `agent_id`, `call_id`                                                                                                                                                    |
| `call.inbound_received`            | An authenticated inbound phone request passed admission                                                                                                                                                                                  | `agent_id`, `call_id`                                                                                                                                                    |
| `integration.webhook_received`     | An authenticated incoming integration delivery was stored for the first time                                                                                                                                                             | `agent_id`, `endpoint_id`, `event_id`, `event_type`, `record_type`, `record_id`                                                                                          |

`call.completed` never fires for a test, and on a call Sempera's own call service answered its `summary` is empty (webhooks.md). `agent.published` and `call.outcomes` are the webhook events of the same name, reduced to the fields listed here. Integration events contain identifiers, never arbitrary incoming payloads or secrets. There are no invented CRM subscriptions. Tool actions triggered by automations do not recursively emit conversation tool events.

### Integration and CRM changes

Choose Integration webhook received in the trigger builder. The contact and booking templates add an event-type condition; they do not subscribe to another system. Configure your sender to deliver a JSON object to the agent's existing incoming webhook using the Sempera signature and delivery-ID headers. For example:

```json
{"event_type":"crm.contact.updated","record_type":"contact","record_id":"contact-123"}
```

The three optional values must be identifiers of 1 to 200 ASCII characters, starting with a letter or digit and containing only letters, digits, underscores, periods, colons, slashes or hyphens. Missing or invalid values become empty strings, not coerced or truncated identifiers. All other payload fields are excluded from trigger data. Workspace and agent identity always come from the authenticated endpoint, never the submitted body. A duplicate or rejected delivery does not announce another event.

Use all-condition matching with `endpoint_id` and `event_type` to limit a trigger to one connection and one change. Tool inputs can reference `{{record_id}}` to look up or update the record through a workspace-approved API tool. Do not send credentials or whole customer records in these identifier fields. The existing incoming-event storage still retains the original accepted body under its existing retention policy.

An owner must configure the external sender or a signing adapter. Native provider webhook signatures and automatic CRM subscriptions are not implemented by this path. Receipt-to-trigger dispatch remains best effort, not a durable subscription queue: a process interruption after storage can leave an event unannounced, and redelivery is deduplicated. No live delivery proof is implied by a template or dry run.

## Actions

| `action.kind` | Fields                                                                            | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `webhook`     | `endpoint_id`                                                                     | POSTs the event to one of the workspace's own enabled webhook endpoints (webhooks.md), signed with that endpoint's secret                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `tool`        | `tool_id`, `input`                                                                | Calls one of the workspace's own API request tools once (tools-and-integrations.md). `input` is up to 20 named text values, each up to 2000 characters, which may use `{{field}}` for a field of the event                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `email`       | `to`                                                                              | Emails every owner of the workspace with a verified address. `to` is `workspace_owners`, the only value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `call`        | `request`                                                                         | A full `POST /v1/calls` request with an explicit agent, recipient, production/version pin and consent. Uses that route's runtime dispatch, calling windows, caps and do-not-contact checks                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `sms`         | `agent_id`, `user_number`, `agent_message`, `consent_basis`, `timezone`, `window` | Sends through the agent's existing SMS handler, with texting enablement, sender ownership, limits, write policy, opt-out and do-not-contact checks. `timezone` and `window` are the recipient's sending hours, checked when saved and again before the send. Outside them, or on a trigger saved without them, nothing is sent and the run fails with `outside_sending_hours` or `sms_hours_required` |
| `slack`       | `tool_id`, `input`                                                                | Uses a registered workspace HTTPS API request tool aimed at `hooks.slack.com` or `slack.com`. Credentials remain in the existing tool registry, not the trigger                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `custom_code` | `snippet_id`, `version`, `input`                                                  | Runs an active published workspace snippet in the existing bounded, no-network sandbox. Inputs may use the same event field substitutions as tool inputs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

A bare URL is not a destination: register the address as a webhook endpoint first. An `endpoint_id` or `tool_id` that is not this workspace's own, or a tool that is not an API request tool, is a `400`. Call and SMS actions additionally require `calls:write` and outbound permission when created or edited. Their target agent must also be in the credential's scope. Choosing a `custom_code` action additionally requires `tools:write` and snippet permission. A `call` action's `timezone`, `window` and `webhook` are checked when saved, by the rules `POST /v1/calls` uses. A call or SMS action on `call.failed` or `call.outcomes` is a `400`: only inbound call events may start contact, so it could never run.

The four specialized actions are stored under the durable `tool` business-action class, so existing publication crash, retention and owner-review protections still apply. Their public action preserves its specialized kind. No schema migration is needed. Each execution has a stable one-shot dispatch key, with stale reservation recovery disabled. These actions cannot be manually retried; inspect an uncertain result before authoring new work. Tests and dry runs never send. A fixture-mode SMS or Slack action records that nothing was delivered rather than reporting a real delivery. Custom code records execution status, not arbitrary code output, in the delivery log.

A webhook action posts this body with `X-Sempera-Signature`, `X-Sempera-Event-Id` (the body's `id`, the same on every attempt), `X-Sempera-Event` and, when the workspace has turned on JWT request signing, the signing header (secrets-and-signing.md):

```json
{"id": "evt_...", "object": "event", "type": "call.completed", "created_at": "2026-09-28T12:00:00+00:00",
 "workspace_id": "...", "trigger": {"id": "...", "name": "Long calls to the ops channel"}, "data": {"call_id": "...", "duration_s": 640, "...": "every field the event lists"}}
```

It makes up to three attempts (at once, 30 seconds later, then 5 minutes later) until the first `2xx`, and follows the delivery rules in webhooks.md. A tool is called once, because a tool that changes something is not safe to repeat unasked, through the same road and write rules as a tool step inside a call. Where the deployment answers tools from fixtures, the run ends `failed` with an error saying nothing was sent.

## Runs

A run reads `id`, `object: "automation_execution"`, `trigger_id`, `trigger_name`, `event`, `event_id`, `event_summary`, `event_data`, `agent_ids`, `status`, `matched`, `failed_condition`, `action_kind`, `action`, `stalled`, `retryable`, `review_required`, `review_etag`, `started_at`, `completed_at` and `duration_ms`.

`status` is `skipped` (a condition did not hold; `failed_condition` names the first, with the value it saw), `running`, `succeeded` or `failed`. A run can also read `unknown`, when Sempera could not confirm whether the action went out (`review_required` is then true), `unavailable` or `reviewed`. `action` is the result: for a webhook the endpoint and every attempt with its `response_code` or `error`, for a tool the tool and the outcome, for an email `recipients` and `sent`. A run still `running` well after its attempts could have finished reads `stalled: true`.

`POST .../retry` sends a failed or stalled webhook or tool run once more, now: the same event id and time, to the trigger's current destination, numbered after the attempts it already has. It answers the run. A skipped or succeeded run, an email run (its owners would get it twice), a run whose call content was deleted, a run still delivering, and a run whose trigger's action has changed since, are refused with `409 conflict` and a sentence saying why.

## Dry run

```http
POST /v1/automation/triggers/{id}/test
{"event": {"duration_s": 700}}
```

`event` sets some of the event's fields; the event's own sample fills the rest (and a trigger that names agents uses its first). It answers `object: "automation_test"`, `dry_run: true`, `delivered: false`, the resolved `event_data`, `in_scope`, each condition with the value it saw (`actual`) and whether it `passed`, `failed_condition`, `would_run` and, when it would run, the `action` that would go out with its destination. A field the event does not have, or one of the wrong type, is a `400`.

## Refusals

| Status                    | When                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400 validation_failed`   | A field breaks a rule above; `field` names it                                                                                                                          |
| `404 not_found`           | No such trigger or run in this workspace, or one naming an agent the credential cannot read                                                                            |
| `409 conflict`            | Retrying a run that cannot be sent again; or an edit whose `expected_updated_at` is no longer the trigger's (`reason: "stale_trigger"`, with the `updated_at` on file) |
| `503 service_unavailable` | The deployment has no customer database to keep triggers in                                                                                                            |


---

# Workspaces and organizations
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/workspaces.md

## Workspaces

A workspace is the boundary between one customer and another. Agents, tools, integrations, knowledge, calls, keys and webhooks belong to exactly one. `GET /v1/workspaces` lists the workspaces the credential can see (an API key sees exactly one). `GET /v1/workspaces/{id}` adds `your_role` and the agents in scope. `PATCH /v1/workspaces/{id}` renames (owner).

## Organizations

An organization is the membership and billing umbrella over workspaces. `GET /v1/organizations` lists the caller's workspace organizations. `GET /v1/organizations/{organization_id}` reads one (`organizations:read`); an id the credential cannot see answers `404 not_found`, the same as an id that never existed. Membership and invitations are managed in the Sempera App.

### Reseller-funded child organizations

`POST /v1/organizations` creates a child workspace under an existing reseller. It requires a signed-in reseller owner or admin, the session's CSRF token and an allowed Sempera App origin. Workspace API keys do not carry reseller authority and are refused, even with `organizations:write`.

The JSON body contains `parent_organization_id` (the reseller partner id), `name`, `owner_email`, `external_ref` and optional `support_responsibility` (`partner` or `sempera`, default `partner`). Other fields are refused. The customer's owner must already have an active Sempera account with a verified email and cannot be reseller staff. An established customer receives an ownership invitation through the existing invitation flow. The parent needs an approved entitlement and an available customer slot.

The child is always wholesale-funded: the reseller, not the child, is responsible for funding. Workspace creation and its parent link commit together. A new child returns 201. Reusing an `external_ref` under the same parent returns the existing child with 200, including when the parent's customer slots are now full. Keep the reference stable after a lost response; use a different reference for a different customer. The App generates a reference for retries within the open form when none is supplied.

The response's `id` is the partner customer id; `workspace_id` is the child's workspace id. Manage existing children in the signed-in partner console: list and read customers, suspend or resume service, and read attributed usage for a date range. Those session-authenticated management operations are not part of this canonical API's published route contract. Recorded amounts are not credit balances.

Each action checks the caller's current reseller role and the parent-child relationship. Creating a child gives reseller staff no membership in it and no access to its calls or recordings.

Credit purchases, credit transfers and reseller price configuration are not enabled by this endpoint. The published credit offers remain catalogue-only. A usage allowance is not a purchased balance, and credits are not converted into minutes or cash. Credit settlement, reservation/consumption, reversals and price-floor enforcement must be implemented before these operations can be offered.

## Doug text Assistant

These routes manage the workspace owner's text channel from their signed-in Sempera App session. API keys, including owner and CI keys, cannot use them. Every route needs the workspace owner's signed-in session; reads require `workspaces:read`, writes require `workspaces:write` and CSRF proof. New work requires an active workspace and Assistant entitlement. The channel is default off and is available only on a deployment configured to deliver messages; these routes do not activate a provider.

| Route                                  | Contract                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GET /v1/text-assistant/settings`      | Returns `name`, `available`, `enabled`, `linked`, masked `mobile` or null, and `pending`.                          |
| `PATCH /v1/text-assistant/settings`    | Takes a boolean `enabled` and returns the settings. Disabling remains available without entitlement.               |
| `POST /v1/text-assistant/link`         | Takes `mobile` in international E.164 format and sends a linking code. Returns `sent: true`, not a verified link.  |
| `POST /v1/text-assistant/link/confirm` | Takes the received `code` in the authenticated App session and returns settings after successful verification.     |
| `DELETE /v1/text-assistant/link`       | Removes the owner's link and its messages, then returns settings. Unlinking remains available without entitlement. |
| `GET /v1/text-assistant/thread`        | Returns only this owner's messages in the current workspace, never another owner's thread.                         |

The thread response contains `name`, `messages`, `has_more` and `next_before`. Each message contains `id`, `body`, nullable `answer`, `state` and timestamp `at`. A page contains up to 50 messages, oldest first within that page. Pass `before=<next_before>` to fetch the next older page. The cursor must be a canonical UUID in this owner's workspace thread; an unknown or foreign cursor returns no messages. An invalid cursor answers `400 validation_failed`.

Linking codes expire after ten minutes and allow at most five verification attempts. Requests are throttled, and an already linked number must be unlinked before changing it. Settings expose only the mobile number's last four digits. A disabled or unavailable channel does not imply a successful send.

## Service version

A workspace pins the Sempera runtime release its new sessions start on, independent of any agent's published version. Only releases installed on this deployment are listed; today that is one.

- `GET /v1/org/service-versions` (`workspaces:read`) answers `{"versions": [...]}`, each with `id`, `name` and `available`.
- `GET /v1/org/service-version` (`workspaces:read`) answers the pin: `{"version": "...", "applies_to": "new_sessions"}`. A pin that cannot be read answers `503 service_unavailable`.
- `PUT /v1/org/service-version` (`workspaces:write`, owner only) with `{"version": "...", "expected_version": "..."}` changes it. A stale `expected_version` or a release that is not installed answers `409 conflict`; a paused workspace answers `403 forbidden` on every route here.

Sessions already running keep the release they started on. A call, preview or test whose workspace pin cannot be read, or names a release that is not installed, is refused before it starts rather than run on another release.

## Platform

`GET /v1/platform` (scope `deploy:read`, the CI and certification credential) reports the deployment's build identity, its production posture and the current call-capacity snapshot. It never names a machine or a path.

## API keys

`GET /v1/api-keys`, `POST /v1/api-keys`, `GET /v1/api-keys/{id}`, `PATCH /v1/api-keys/{id}`, `DELETE /v1/api-keys/{id}`. See authentication.md for kinds, roles and scopes. Creating, renaming and revoking need the owner role and `api_keys:write`; from the App they also carry the session's CSRF token. `PATCH` takes `{"name": "..."}` (1 to 120 characters) and changes only the label: the secret, scopes and role stay. A revoked key and a connection key (named `mcp:`, `oauth:` or `rest:`) answer `409 conflict`, and a new name cannot start with one of those prefixes.

Expiry has its own routes, for the owner only. `GET /v1/api-key-settings` (`api_keys:read`) answers `enabled`, `expiry_edit_available` and `notice_delivery_available`; `PUT /v1/api-key-settings` (`api_keys:write`) takes `{"enabled": true}` or `false` to turn expiry notices on or off, and answers `503 service_unavailable` while this server cannot send them yet; `PATCH /v1/api-key-settings/{key_id}` (`api_keys:write`) changes a key's name, its `expires_at` date, or sets `expires_at` to `null` so the key never expires.


---

# Secrets and request signing
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/secrets-and-signing.md

Two owner settings keep credentials out of your tool definitions and let a receiver check where a request came from. **Secrets** are values you store once for the workspace, such as the token a tool sends to your own system; Sempera never returns a value. **Request signing** adds a short-lived signed token, verifiable with public keys, to the requests Sempera sends in your name.

Both are workspace settings. Writes need the `owner` role and the scope shown; a secret or key of another workspace answers `404` exactly like one that never existed. A write from the Sempera App also passes the CSRF check (errors-and-limits.md).

## Secrets

| Route                           | Scope         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/secrets`               | `tools:read`  | The workspace's secrets, unpaged, in the compatibility envelope `{"data": {...}, "errors": null}`: `secrets` beside `types`, `statuses`, `sorts`, `reference_formats` and `configured` |
| `POST /v1/secrets`              | `tools:write` | Add one. `201` with the secret                                                                                                                                                         |
| `PATCH /v1/secrets/{id}`        | `tools:write` | Rename it, replace a Static value, or pause and resume it                                                                                                                              |
| `POST /v1/secrets/{id}/refresh` | `tools:write` | Fetch a Refresh secret's value now                                                                                                                                                     |
| `DELETE /v1/secrets/{id}`       | `tools:write` | Delete it: the stored value goes with it. Answers the secret with `"deleted": true`                                                                                                    |

`GET /v1/secrets` takes `q` (a name search, up to 80 characters), `type` (`all`, `static`, `refresh`), `status` (`all`, `active`, `paused`) and `sort` (`created_desc` by default, `created_asc`, `updated_desc`, `updated_asc`); any other value is refused with `400 validation_failed`. Other routes answer the secret itself.

A secret has a name in `CAPITALS_WITH_UNDERSCORES`, 2 to 80 characters, starting with a letter, unique in the workspace. There are two types.

```http
POST /v1/secrets
{"name": "ORDERS_TOKEN", "value": "<the value>"}
```

```http
POST /v1/secrets
{"name": "ORDERS_ACCESS", "type": "refresh",
 "refresh": {"url": "https://orders.example.com/oauth/token", "method": "POST",
             "headers": {"X-Client": "sempera"}, "body": "{\"grant_type\": \"client_credentials\"}",
             "interval_minutes": 55, "json_path": "$.access_token"}}
```

| Field                      | Rule                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`                     | Required                                                                                                                                                |
| `type`                     | `static` (default) or `refresh`                                                                                                                         |
| `value`                    | Static only: up to 8192 characters, no line breaks or control characters. A Refresh secret takes none                                                   |
| `refresh.url`              | Refresh only, required: `https`, no username, password, fragment or template, and not a local or private address                                        |
| `refresh.method`           | `GET` (default) or `POST`                                                                                                                               |
| `refresh.headers`          | Up to 20, each value up to 2000 characters. Not `Host`, `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding` or `Connection`                                           |
| `refresh.body`             | POST only, up to 8192 characters                                                                                                                        |
| `refresh.interval_minutes` | Required, 1 to 1440                                                                                                                                     |
| `refresh.json_path`        | Required, up to 200 characters: `$.access_token`, `$.data.items[0].token` or `$['access-token']`. It must reach one text, number or true or false value |

A Refresh secret is fetched when you create it, on `.../refresh`, and again, when a tool is about to use it, if its last attempt is older than the interval. The request goes out with a 10 second timeout, and the answer must be a `2xx` JSON document. A failed fetch is recorded in `refresh.last_error` (a sentence that never contains the value or the answer) and keeps the last good value; creating a secret whose first fetch fails still succeeds, and the secret says why it has no value. A refresh needs the deployment's encryption key, like every stored secret; without it writes answer `503 owner_setup_required`.

A secret reads `id`, `object: "secret"`, `name`, `key`, `type` (`Static` or `Refresh`), `status` (`Active` or `Paused`), `reference` (`{{secret.NAME}}`), `id_reference` (`{{secret.id.<id>}}`), `has_value`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and `refresh`, null for a Static secret, otherwise `url` (without its query string), `method`, `header_names` (never the values), `interval_minutes`, `json_path`, `last_refreshed_at`, `last_attempt_at` and `last_error`.

`PATCH` takes `name`, `value` and `status` (`active` or `paused`), at least one. A value on a Refresh secret is refused, and a Refresh secret's settings cannot be edited, only its name and status. `.../refresh` on a Static secret is `400`, and on a paused one `409 conflict`.

### Using a secret in a tool

A tool names a secret by its name in `auth` (`{"type": "bearer_reference", "secret": "ORDERS_TOKEN"}`, or `api_key_reference` with a `header`), or by a template in its request URL path or query, a static header or a static body: `{{secret.ORDERS_TOKEN}}` or `{{secret.id.<id>}}` (never in the host). A tool your workspace owns resolves them from your workspace's secrets only. A reference to an unknown secret, a paused secret or one with no value refuses the call before anything is sent, and the value is masked wherever it would appear in a result, including an answer that echoes it (tools-and-integrations.md).

## Request signing

When signing is on, the requests Sempera sends to your systems in your workspace's name carry one more header holding a JWT: an owner-built tool call that reaches your system (a sandbox test or a live conversation), every outbound webhook delivery, every webhook action of an automation trigger (automations.md) and a widget's chat webhooks (widgets.md). It adds to `X-Sempera-Signature` (webhooks.md); it never replaces it.

| Route                                                     | Scope            | Notes                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /v1/signing`                                         | `webhooks:read`  | The settings, the keys and where to verify                                                      |
| `PATCH /v1/signing`                                       | `webhooks:write` | Change settings; fields you leave out keep their values                                         |
| `POST /v1/signing/keys`                                   | `webhooks:write` | Generate the first key, or rotate. `201`, with the settings view and the new key as `generated` |
| `POST /v1/signing/keys/revoke-previous`                   | `webhooks:write` | Withdraw every key but the active one, now                                                      |
| `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/.well-known/jwks.json` | none             | The published public keys                                                                       |

These answer plain objects, not the compatibility envelope. `GET /v1/signing` answers `object: "request_signing"`, `workspace_id`, `algorithm` (`RS256`), `settings`, `keys`, `issuer`, `jwks_url`, `jwks_path`, `key_storage_configured` and `signed_requests` (`["tool_calls", "webhooks"]`). A key reads `id`, `object: "signing_key"`, `kid`, `algorithm`, `status` (`active`, `previous` or `revoked`), `public_key_pem`, `created_at`, `retired_at`, `revoked_at` and, in the list, `published`. A private key is never returned.

| Setting            | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`          | `false` until you turn it on, which needs an active key: without one, `409 conflict`                                                                                                          |
| `header_name`      | Default `X-Sempera-JWT`. Letters, digits and hyphens, up to 64 characters; not `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Host`, `Cookie` or a header Sempera itself sets for events |
| `header_prefix`    | Default `Bearer `. Up to 32 printable characters                                                                                                                                              |
| `audience`         | Blank by default, which means the target's origin. Up to 300 characters                                                                                                                       |
| `include_protocol` | `true` by default. When `false` and no `audience` is set, the audience is the host alone                                                                                                      |
| `ttl_seconds`      | Token lifetime, 60 to 3600 (default 300)                                                                                                                                                      |
| `custom_claims`    | Up to 20 string values (names up to 64 characters, values up to 500) added to every token. `iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `iat`, `nbf`, `exp`, `jti` and `body_sha256` are Sempera's own and refused    |

The header value is the prefix followed by an RS256 token. Its header carries `kid`; its claims are `iss` (`https://api.sempera.org/v1/workspaces/<workspace_id>`), `sub` (the workspace), `aud`, `iat`, `nbf`, `exp`, a fresh `jti`, `body_sha256` (the hex SHA-256 of the exact body bytes sent, of the empty string for no body) and your custom claims.

To verify, read `kid` from the token, take that key from the JWKS, check the RS256 signature, `iss`, `aud` and `exp`, and compare `body_sha256` with the SHA-256 of the raw body you received. A request without the header should fail that check: if the key cannot be read when a request is sent, the request goes out without the header rather than not at all.

Rotating makes the new key the one that signs and keeps the previous key in the JWKS for 24 hours, so tokens already in flight still verify; at most three keys are published, and older ones are revoked. Revoking previous keys removes every earlier key from the JWKS at once, for a suspected compromise, and answers the settings view with `revoked`, the number withdrawn. A key is 2048-bit RSA and its private half is stored encrypted under the deployment's key; without that key no signing key can be made. The JWKS needs no credential, answers `{"keys": []}` for a workspace without keys (or one that does not exist) and may be cached for 5 minutes.

## Refusals

| Status                     | When                                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400 validation_failed`    | A field breaks a rule above                                                                        |
| `403 forbidden`            | The credential's role is not `owner`; `403 csrf_failed` for an App-session write without its proof |
| `404 not_found`            | No such secret in this workspace                                                                   |
| `409 conflict`             | A name is taken, a paused secret is refreshed, or signing is turned on without a key               |
| `503 owner_setup_required` | The deployment has no encryption key for stored credentials                                        |
| `503 service_unavailable`  | The deployment has no customer database                                                            |


---

# Owner features in the App
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/app-features.md

Some of what a workspace owner does in the Sempera App has no route in this API. The routes behind these features are the App's own (`app.sempera.org/api/*`): they take a signed-in session, and a Sempera API key is honoured only on `/v1` (authentication.md, api-overview.md). They are described here so an integration knows what the App does around the API, what the customer sees, and which `/v1` reads cover the same ground. Nothing on this page is a route you can call with a key.

## Exporting call data

Where: Conversations (Export) and Settings, Data and privacy. Who: workspace owners only.

An owner exports one agent's phone calls, narrowed by the same filters the Conversations list has, as JSON or CSV.

| Filter      | Rule                                                                                                                        |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Date window | An absolute start and end; either may be left open. A call with no start time is never left out by the window               |
| Length      | `any`, under 1 minute, 1 to 5, 5 to 15, or over 15 minutes. A call with no measured length is in none of the length buckets |
| Search      | Up to 200 characters, matched the way the list matches it (the caller as shown, the call id and the outcome's own sentence) |

The file is built in the background, so a large export never holds a request open:

- One export at a time per agent; asking for a second while one is being built is refused with the export already underway named.
- At most 10,000 calls and 64 MiB. Past either, the export fails with a sentence that says to narrow the date range.
- When it is ready, the workspace's verified owners get an email with a link to Data and privacy in the App. The link opens a page; it is never a link to the file and carries no token, so a forwarded email opens nothing without an owner's own session.
- The file leaves only through an owner-gated download in the App, with the same owner, agent-scope and workspace checks as the export itself. It is never a public URL, and it is served `no-store`.
- A file can be downloaded for seven days, then it expires and is removed.

Deleted content is never exported. A transcript that was deleted, or is past its retention window and waiting for the next sweep, is listed with its state and no words. If a transcript is deleted after the file was built, the file is withdrawn and removed, and its download answers that the file is gone.

A JSON export is one document: a header naming what the export covers, then `calls`. A CSV export has one row per call, with the columns `id`, `started_at`, `duration_s`, `caller`, `outcome`, `summary`, `recording`, `transcript`, `turns`, `qc_status`, `qc_tags`, `deleted_at`, `delete_reason` and `conversation`, a byte order mark and CRLF line ends so a spreadsheet opens it as UTF-8. A cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets an apostrophe in front, so a spreadsheet shows it and never runs it.

Requests, builds and downloads are recorded in the workspace's audit log as `call.export_requested`, `call.exported` and `call.export_downloaded`, with counts and filters and never a number, a search string or a word of a transcript.

Reading calls from code is `GET /v1/calls` and `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}` (sessions-and-calls.md).

## Outbound batches: start time, CSV recipients, scheduler

Where: an agent's Outbound page. A batch is a list of people the business has permission to reach. It carries a name, a consent basis in words (at least 12 characters, kept on the record), a calling window read in each person's own time zone (default 09:00 to 18:00), and its limits: at most 500 recipients, 1 to 20 at once (default 3), 1 to 5 attempts (default 3), a wait of a minute to a week before a retry (default an hour). A call batch also needs an owner's approval before it can start. Before anyone is reached the workspace's do-not-contact list is checked, and a number on it is recorded as blocked and never called.

**Start time.** A new batch takes an optional "Start sending at", a date and time read in the batch's time zone (or carrying its own offset). It may be at most five minutes in the past and at most a year ahead. Nothing is due before it, and after it each person is still reached only inside their own window. The batch says when it sends.

**CSV recipients.** People can be added from a CSV file as well as typed. The file is at most 256 KiB, and it is only read: checking a file stores nothing and contacts nobody.

- With a header row, the number column is the one named `number`, `phone`, `phone_number`, `phone number`, `mobile`, `cell` or `to`; a `timezone`, `time zone`, `time_zone` or `tz` column sets each person's zone; on a call batch a `precall_dtmf` or `keys` column sets the keys pressed when the call connects; every other named column becomes a `{field}` the message can use. Without a header, the columns are number, name and note.
- Every row goes through the same check a typed person does. A row that fails, or that has a cell starting the way a spreadsheet formula does (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return; a phone-shaped number is not one), is left out and reported with its row number and the reason, never the cell. A number listed twice is contacted once. Rows past the 500th are left out with a note.

**Scheduler.** Whether a started batch sends on its own is a setting of the deployment. When it is on, a pass runs once a minute and advances every running batch whose start time has come and that has someone due. When it is off, a batch moves only when the owner presses "Send the next few now". The scheduler has no way of dialling of its own: it runs the same pass the button runs, with the same do-not-contact check, the same outbound call limits, the same per-person window and the same audit record (which notes whether the button or the scheduler ran the pass). It never touches a draft, and skips a paused or stopped batch. A pause or stop pressed while a pass is placing calls takes effect before the next person.

A restart never dials anyone twice. A person marked as being dialled when a pass was interrupted is recorded as failed, with a note that the call may already have rung, and is not called again.

The Outbound page shows whether started batches send on their own here and how often, why a running batch is waiting (an outbound call limit, or the workspace's limit on calls at once), and what the last pass sent and who ran it.

**Outbound call limits.** An owner can cap the calls the workspace places per UTC hour and per UTC day (Settings, Usage and balance). No cap is set by default. The platform may set a ceiling for every workspace, and the stricter of the two applies. Every road that places a call spends one call from the cap after the do-not-contact check and before the dial: a batch pass, a single call from the Outbound page, and `POST /v1/calls`. When a cap is reached nobody is called and the answer says which limit and when it lifts: a batch pass leaves the rest pending, a single call is refused with `409`, and `POST /v1/calls` answers `429 rate_limited` with `retry_after_s` in the error. A cap that cannot be read stops calling: a batch pauses, a single call is refused, and `POST /v1/calls` answers `503 service_unavailable`. A call turned back before it was dialled gives its slot back. Texts are not calls and are not counted.

**Calls at once.** A workspace's own limit on calls at once and on minutes a day, the one checked when a preview call starts, also applies to every call the Outbound page dials, a batch pass or a single call. It is the limit of the workspace the agent belongs to, whoever pressed the button. It is checked just before the dial, and each outbound call counts against it while it lasts, and in Calls started today on Settings, Usage and balance (below). At the limit nobody is called: a batch pass leaves the rest pending and the page says why the batch waits, and a single call is refused with `409` and the reason. The refusal is audited with the reason (a batch pass in its own pass record), and so is a single call refused because it is outside the person's calling hours.

From the API: `POST /v1/calls` places one outbound call (sessions-and-calls.md). The compatibility read `GET /v2/batches/list` lists an agent's batches with their recipients and progress; it does not carry the start time.

## Usage this billing period

Where: Settings, Usage and balance (This billing period). Who: any member of the workspace.

The card sets the workspace's inbound calls and minutes beside its outbound calls and minutes for the current billing period: the subscription's own current period when there is one, otherwise the UTC calendar month, and it says which.

- **Inbound** counts every phone call the workspace's agents answered in the period, once each: the calls the carrier reported and the calls answered on Sempera's own voice service. A call seen both ways is counted once, by the same rule that sends one `call.completed` (webhooks.md). A call answered on Sempera's own voice service is counted once it is announced, usually within a minute or two of ending; one not announced within a day of ending is not counted. Test, Try it live and simulator sessions are never counted.
- **Outbound** counts the calls the workspace placed, how many were answered, and the minutes from answer to hang-up.
- A call with no measured length is counted as a call and named, never as zero minutes.
- Every figure is an estimate of use, not an invoice. The plan's published figures are shown beside them as published; no overage charge is worked out, and inbound and outbound minutes are not combined against the plan's included minutes.

There is no `/v1` read for these figures.

**Today's use**, on the same page, shows **Calls started today** (the UTC day): each call the workspace's limit on calls at once let through, whether a session started from the App or `POST /v1/sessions`, or an outbound call the Outbound page dials (a batch pass or a single call). An outbound call counts once it passes that check, even when the line then turns out busy or nobody answers, and each retry counts again; a call refused at the limit does not count. Calls answered on the workspace's phone numbers are not in this count.

## Buying a phone number

Where: Channels, Phone numbers, Buy number. Workspace owners only. Opening the dialog buys nothing. It shows Country and verifies whether a payment method is saved for this workspace. A failed verification says the status is unknown, never that no method exists. Add payment method opens the existing hosted billing settings with a return link; returning to the App refreshes the status. If billing is not configured, the App reports that refusal instead of displaying a card form.

Buying still requires an active paid plan, a verified saved payment method, the workspace's own agent, the carrier purchase gate, explicit cost confirmation and CSRF protection. Neither a saved method nor a paid plan alone authorizes a purchase. No card details or processor customer identifiers are returned to the dialog. These are session-only App controls, not developer-key API endpoints.

## Tool analytics

Where: an agent's Tools page. For each tool the agent called, over the last 7, 30 or 90 days (default 30):

| Figure                            | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Calls, succeeded, failed, refused | What happened to each call of the tool. A refusal is a call the tool's rules stopped before it ran                                                                                                  |
| Success share                     | Succeeded calls over all calls, in percent                                                                                                                                                          |
| Time taken                        | The median and the 95th percentile, counting only calls that actually went out; a refusal, or a preview answer that nothing sent, is left out. The card says how many calls the two figures rest on |
| Why the rest did not succeed      | Each reason with its count, from one fixed vocabulary of plain sentences; an unknown cause reads as "something else went wrong" and is never echoed                                                 |
| Last problem                      | The most recent reason, with when                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Trend                             | One bucket per day on the business's own calendar (its time zone, or UTC when none is set): calls and how many did not succeed                                                                      |

The page also totals every tool. Tools letting callers down come first, then the busiest. The figures are counted from the tool calls recorded in the agent's conversations (previews, simulations and phone calls): request and response bodies never reach the rollup, and a call with no time at all cannot be placed in a window, so it is left out and counted.

Other pages: a tool's own test lives on its Test call tab, and the tool form can read a pasted `curl` command into its fields. The command is only read, never run: files, certificates, substitutions and pipes are refused, every credential in it becomes a named secret reference and its value is dropped, and nothing is saved until the owner reviews and saves. `GET /v1/tools` lists the tools (tools-and-integrations.md); there is no API read for these analytics.

## Code snippets in the App

The Tools page covers the whole owner road for the snippets `snippets.md` describes, on the same records: write a snippet in one editor (name, description, code, inputs, result shape, timeout) that says which draft a save writes and that published versions stay as published; test the draft or any version on sample input shaped from its inputs; publish behind a dialog that says the number is frozen; discard a draft; read the version history, newest first, with each version's code and hash, and which tools pin it.

In the tool builder, a Code snippet tool has a pin picker: a snippet and one of its published versions, and a preview of what the model fills in. An existing tool shows what it runs today. Its version changes only after "Move the pin" and an explicit confirmation, and Save stays closed until then. Writing a snippet needs the operator role or above; pinning it in a tool needs the owner role, as `POST /v1/tools` does.

## Staging and analytics: App routes, not `/v1`

Two App features are served by the App's own routes and have no public `/v1` counterpart yet. They take the signed-in owner's session, not an API key, carry no stability promise and are not in `openapi.json`. Build nothing against them; if you need the data over the API, say so at [hello@sempera.org](mailto:hello@sempera.org).

- **Staging.** An agent's Environments page keeps one staged snapshot of the draft between development and production. Owners publish the draft (or an earlier version) to staging, try it live against it, restage an earlier snapshot, discard it, promote it, or roll production back. Promotion is the ordinary publish from the staged snapshot, and a snapshot is pinned to the production version it was staged over: once production moves it is stale and cannot be promoted. By default staging never reaches a caller: a phone number set to staging answers with production. Only when Sempera's call service has its pinned-version switches on (`SEMPERA_PINNED_VERSIONS` and the agent's own serve-staging-numbers setting) does such a number answer with the staged snapshot, once Sempera's servers have compiled and sealed it, and any problem falls back to production; the environments view's `numbers_note` says which applies. The routes live under `/api/agent/environments`. Read-only listings of what each environment holds are on `/v2/agents/{uuid}/environments` (mcp.md).
- **Analytics.** The workspace and agent Insights pages (Traffic, saved Reports with CSV download, and Boards of report tiles) read the App's routes under `/api/analytics` and `/api/insights`. An old `/analytics` address on an agent opens Insights.


---

# Webhooks
URL: https://api.sempera.org/docs/webhooks.md

Two directions live under `/v1/webhooks`.

- **Outbound events** are what Sempera sends to an HTTPS endpoint you register: signed JSON about calls, agents, test runs and alerts. This page is their contract: the events, the shape of each, how to verify a delivery, and what is and is not guaranteed.
- **Provider ingress** is where the telephony carrier and the payment provider deliver to Sempera, each under its own proof. You never call these (see the end of this page).

## Outbound events

### The events

| Category | Event                    | Sent when                                                                                                                                                             | Reaches                               |
